observed_output.review_content: I would not consider buying an i-phone simply because my friend owns two of them – or blindly go for a new Android model suggested by my son or nephew (both of whom are more tech savvy than me) because their recommendations are obviously based on their own needs and expectations, which may differ from mine. I am an old-fashioned mechanical engineer with a basic understanding of parameters like millimetres, megapixels and megabytes – but I think of a cellphone as a utility item, not a status symbol. Applying a technocratic approach, I would not choose a costlier option unless I get additional features which suit my requirements.My foremost requirement – which is entirely non-negotiable – is that my handset must have provision for two SIM cards, since I do not want to carry two separate handsets for my CUG and personal numbers. My other requirements are not difficult to fulfil: a phonebook with at least 2000 contacts, basic net connectivity, a basic camera for photos and videos and scope for downloading a few apps such as the ubiquitous WhatsApp and my favourite word games (which do not need much memory or processing capacity). I would certainly appreciate practical features like high reliability, software and security updates and high battery capacity (sufficient for 24 hours or preferably 48 hours at my normal level of usage). Besides, I would like to use a new handset for at least two years.Apart from exigencies, I do not intend to use my cellphone for surfing the Internet, videoconferencing or sending e-mails as I prefer using a desktop or laptop for such activities.I am equally clear about what I do not need. I do not intend to use my cellphone for watching movies, reading books, listening to music or creating fancy social media posts. Nor do I want a device for taking high resolution photos during a vacation as I would prefer to use a camera. At the risk of sounding flippant, I would say that I do not want a device to unlock my car or count the strokes in a game of golf – primarily because I do not own a car and I do not play golf!Having used smartphones of Samsung and Motorola makes over the past few years, I vastly prefer the former. My last phone, which gave me over 30 months of good service, was a Samsung M30. Since that model is obsolete now, I focused on its upgraded cousins: M32, M33 and M52. The last was immediately ruled out as it does not support two SIM cards along with an SD card. After studying the relative specifications of M32 and M33, I concluded that the latter offers better value for money. Generally, it is worth going for the higher memory and higher RAM versions as these parameters affect the performance and the difference in cost is relatively small. I also watched some Youtube videos about these handsets for a better appreciation of their competing features. It is a few millimetres longer and a few grams heavier than my old phone, but these differences are acceptable to me. inputs.product_name: Wireless Ergonomic Mouse, 6-Button, Adjustable DPI, Silent Clicks (Model B09TWH8YHM)
inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I recently bought the wireless ergonomic mouse (model B09TWH8YHM). Overall it feels comfortable, but I’m facing a few issues. Sometimes the cursor movement is jittery, and the side buttons don’t always register clicks.

Support (Sanjay Kulkarni, emp_0819): Thank you for reaching out and for sharing your experience, Priya. Since you mention jittery cursor movement, could you confirm whether you’re using the mouse on a glossy or reflective surface and whether the receiver is plugged directly into your laptop/PC or through a hub?

Customer: I’m using it on a glass-topped desk, and the receiver is plugged into a USB hub.

Support: That helps clarify things. Optical sensors can struggle on glass surfaces, and USB hubs sometimes introduce latency or instability. As a first step, I recommend trying the mouse on a non‑reflective mouse pad or matte surface, and plugging the receiver directly into a USB port on your device. This usually stabilizes cursor movement.

Customer: Okay, I can try that. What about the side buttons not responding all the time?

Support: For the side buttons, please check whether the bundled configuration software is installed, and ensure the buttons are mapped to the expected actions (e.g., Back/Forward in the browser). Also, confirm that no third‑party macro utility is overriding button behavior. If issues persist after these checks, we can explore a firmware reset or replacement option.

Customer: Understood. I’ll test with a mouse pad and direct USB connection, and I’ll reinstall the configuration software.

Support: Great. Please use the mouse for a day after applying these changes and note whether jitter or missed clicks still occur. If the problem continues, reply to this chat or our follow‑up email, and we’ll initiate a warranty evaluation for a possible replacement. Thank you for choosing our product, and we’re committed to ensuring you have a smooth experience.

inputs.Issue:
Hello IT Team,

This is Priya Desai from the Customer Support department (emp_0152). Over the past two days, several of my outbound support emails related to customer authentication and policy clarification have intermittently failed to send or have been significantly delayed. In particular, replies tied to support threads initiated on March 15–16 seem to get stuck with a "pending" status in our mail client, and customers report not receiving updates.

This is impacting my ability to follow up on escalated tickets and maintain proper documentation of communications. Could you please investigate whether there is an issue with SMTP routing, spam filter configuration, or any limits applied to the `@inazuma.com` domain for support staff?

Thank you,
Priya
inputs.Resolution:
Hi Priya,

This is Rajat Anand from the IT department (emp_0996). Thanks for the detailed report; it helped narrow down the cause quickly.

We checked the mail gateway logs and identified that several of your outbound messages were being throttled due to an overly aggressive rate-limit rule that was recently applied to the Customer Support segment. In addition, a misconfigured spam filter rule was flagging some templated responses as potential bulk mail.

Actions taken:
1. Relaxed the rate-limit threshold for `@inazuma.com` support accounts while keeping security controls intact.
2. Updated the spam filter rules to whitelist your CS08 support templates and the primary support domains used in your communications.
3. Flushed the queue of delayed messages and confirmed successful delivery for the affected customers.

Please monitor your next few outbound emails and let us know if you notice any further delays or failures. If issues persist, share a couple of example message IDs so we can run a deeper trace.

Regards,
Rajat
Junior IT Associate, IN09
Information Technology, Inazuma.co

input_bindings.product_name: High-speed HDMI Extender Cable for Streaming Devices (Fire Stick Compatible)
input_bindings.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased an HDMI extender cable for my Fire Stick (product ID B08PFSZ7FH). It works fine most of the time, but occasionally the video signal drops for a few seconds and then comes back. Is this normal, or could it be a defect?

SUPPORT REP (Mithilesh Patel): Thanks for reaching out, Sven. Intermittent signal drops are not expected behavior, so let's run a few quick checks. First, please confirm that the extender is firmly connected on both ends (to the Fire Stick and to the TV) and that there is no visible damage to the cable.

CUSTOMER: I’ve checked both ends—they seem secure and the cable looks fine. The issue happens mostly when I adjust the TV angle or touch the cable.

SUPPORT REP: That suggests a possible loose contact or strain on the HDMI port. I recommend securing the cable so it doesn’t move when you adjust the TV, and trying another HDMI port if available. Also, ensure your Fire Stick power adapter is the original one, as low power can sometimes cause brief dropouts.

CUSTOMER: I switched to another HDMI port and used the original power adapter. The drops are less frequent but still happen occasionally.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, we may be looking at a borderline hardware issue with this specific extender. As a next step, I can arrange a replacement unit under warranty so you can test if the behavior persists. If the replacement works fine, we’ll treat the original as a defective piece and close the case.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. Please go ahead with the replacement.

SUPPORT REP: I’ve initiated the replacement request and you should receive a confirmation email shortly. If the new cable also shows similar issues, please contact us with the new order details and we’ll investigate further, including compatibility with your TV model.

[Chat Session Closed]

inputs.product_name: High-speed HDMI Extender Cable for Streaming Devices (Fire Stick Compatible)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased an HDMI extender cable for my Fire Stick (product ID B08PFSZ7FH). It works fine most of the time, but occasionally the video signal drops for a few seconds and then comes back. Is this normal, or could it be a defect?

SUPPORT REP (Mithilesh Patel): Thanks for reaching out, Sven. Intermittent signal drops are not expected behavior, so let's run a few quick checks. First, please confirm that the extender is firmly connected on both ends (to the Fire Stick and to the TV) and that there is no visible damage to the cable.

CUSTOMER: I’ve checked both ends—they seem secure and the cable looks fine. The issue happens mostly when I adjust the TV angle or touch the cable.

SUPPORT REP: That suggests a possible loose contact or strain on the HDMI port. I recommend securing the cable so it doesn’t move when you adjust the TV, and trying another HDMI port if available. Also, ensure your Fire Stick power adapter is the original one, as low power can sometimes cause brief dropouts.

CUSTOMER: I switched to another HDMI port and used the original power adapter. The drops are less frequent but still happen occasionally.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, we may be looking at a borderline hardware issue with this specific extender. As a next step, I can arrange a replacement unit under warranty so you can test if the behavior persists. If the replacement works fine, we’ll treat the original as a defective piece and close the case.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. Please go ahead with the replacement.

SUPPORT REP: I’ve initiated the replacement request and you should receive a confirmation email shortly. If the new cable also shows similar issues, please contact us with the new order details and we’ll investigate further, including compatibility with your TV model.

[Chat Session Closed]

inputs.product_name: Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+UF+Taste Adjuster(MTDS) with Active Copper & Zinc 7L water purifier
inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I recently purchased the Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+UF+Taste Adjuster water purifier. The unit works well overall, but I’m confused about the taste adjuster settings and I’m not sure if the Active Copper feature is enabled correctly.

Support Rep (Bhupinder Kapoor - emp_0944): Thank you for reaching out, Jaime. I’m glad to hear the purifier is working well. I can help clarify both the taste adjuster and Active Copper features. First, could you confirm whether you’ve set the source water type (borewell, tanker, or municipal) on the MTDS controller?

Customer: I haven’t changed any setting yet; we primarily use municipal water. I also noticed that sometimes the taste varies slightly from day to day.

Support Rep: Understood. For municipal water, we recommend starting with the default MTDS setting and then slowly increasing it one step at a time until you reach a taste you prefer. Small day‑to‑day variations can occur based on the input water quality. Regarding Active Copper, when the purifier is powered on and dispensing, copper ions are automatically infused, so there’s no separate switch to toggle. If you ever feel the taste is too strong or too mild, you can fine‑tune using the MTDS controller.

Customer: That helps. Is there anything I should watch for in terms of maintenance that might affect taste or copper levels?

Support Rep: Yes. Please ensure cartridges are replaced as per the service alerts, and periodically check the pre‑filter for clogging. If you notice a sudden change in taste or flow rate, it’s often a sign that filters need servicing. You’ll also see LED indications when service is due. If the issue persists after adjusting MTDS and basic cleaning, we can arrange a technician visit.

Customer: Great, I’ll follow these steps. Could you email me a short guide on recommended settings for municipal water?

Support Rep: Absolutely. I’ll send you a quick reference guide with recommended MTDS ranges and maintenance tips for municipal water. If you have any further questions, feel free to contact us again.

Customer: Thanks for the detailed explanation and support.

Support Rep: You’re welcome, Jaime. Enjoy your purified water, and have a great day.

inputs.product_name: Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+UF+Taste Adjuster(MTDS) with Active Copper & Zinc 7L water purifier
inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I recently purchased the Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+UF+Taste Adjuster water purifier. The unit works well overall, but I’m confused about the taste adjuster settings and I’m not sure if the Active Copper feature is enabled correctly.

Support Rep (Bhupinder Kapoor - emp_0944): Thank you for reaching out, Jaime. I’m glad to hear the purifier is working well. I can help clarify both the taste adjuster and Active Copper features. First, could you confirm whether you’ve set the source water type (borewell, tanker, or municipal) on the MTDS controller?

Customer: I haven’t changed any setting yet; we primarily use municipal water. I also noticed that sometimes the taste varies slightly from day to day.

Support Rep: Understood. For municipal water, we recommend starting with the default MTDS setting and then slowly increasing it one step at a time until you reach a taste you prefer. Small day‑to‑day variations can occur based on the input water quality. Regarding Active Copper, when the purifier is powered on and dispensing, copper ions are automatically infused, so there’s no separate switch to toggle. If you ever feel the taste is too strong or too mild, you can fine‑tune using the MTDS controller.

Customer: That helps. Is there anything I should watch for in terms of maintenance that might affect taste or copper levels?

Support Rep: Yes. Please ensure cartridges are replaced as per the service alerts, and periodically check the pre‑filter for clogging. If you notice a sudden change in taste or flow rate, it’s often a sign that filters need servicing. You’ll also see LED indications when service is due. If the issue persists after adjusting MTDS and basic cleaning, we can arrange a technician visit.

Customer: Great, I’ll follow these steps. Could you email me a short guide on recommended settings for municipal water?

Support Rep: Absolutely. I’ll send you a quick reference guide with recommended MTDS ranges and maintenance tips for municipal water. If you have any further questions, feel free to contact us again.

Customer: Thanks for the detailed explanation and support.

Support Rep: You’re welcome, Jaime. Enjoy your purified water, and have a great day.

Customer: Hi, I recently purchased the Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+UF+Taste Adjuster water purifier. The unit works well overall, but I’m confused about the taste adjuster settings and I’m not sure if the Active Copper feature is enabled correctly.

Support Rep (Bhupinder Kapoor - emp_0944): Thank you for reaching out, Jaime. I’m glad to hear the purifier is working well. I can help clarify both the taste adjuster and Active Copper features. First, could you confirm whether you’ve set the source water type (borewell, tanker, or municipal) on the MTDS controller?

Customer: I haven’t changed any setting yet; we primarily use municipal water. I also noticed that sometimes the taste varies slightly from day to day.

Support Rep: Understood. For municipal water, we recommend starting with the default MTDS setting and then slowly increasing it one step at a time until you reach a taste you prefer. Small day‑to‑day variations can occur based on the input water quality. Regarding Active Copper, when the purifier is powered on and dispensing, copper ions are automatically infused, so there’s no separate switch to toggle. If you ever feel the taste is too strong or too mild, you can fine‑tune using the MTDS controller.

Customer: That helps. Is there anything I should watch for in terms of maintenance that might affect taste or copper levels?

Support Rep: Yes. Please ensure cartridges are replaced as per the service alerts, and periodically check the pre‑filter for clogging. If you notice a sudden change in taste or flow rate, it’s often a sign that filters need servicing. You’ll also see LED indications when service is due. If the issue persists after adjusting MTDS and basic cleaning, we can arrange a technician visit.

Support Rep: Absolutely. I’ll send you a quick reference guide with recommended MTDS ranges and maintenance tips for municipal water. If you have any further questions, feel free to contact us again.

Customer: Thanks for the detailed explanation and support.

Support Rep: You’re welcome, Jaime. Enjoy your purified water, and have a great day.

inputs.title: Clarify State Handling for GTM Datacenter Tests (present/enabled/disabled)
inputs.description:
Aarav Mittal (emp_0121, Junior Software Engineer, EN09) has reviewed the updated GTM datacenter test suite and would like more explicit documentation around how different `state` values (`present`, `enabled`, `disabled`) are expected to influence the `enabled` and `disabled` flags in both `ModuleParameters` and `ModuleManager`.

From the current tests in `test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py`, the behavior appears to be:
- `state='present'` -> resource exists, `enabled` not explicitly asserted, but `state` remains `present`.
- `state='enabled'` -> `ModuleParameters.enabled` and `results['enabled']` should be `True`, `disabled` should be `False`.
- `state='disabled'` -> `enabled` should be `False`, `disabled` should be `True`.

The earlier closed issue fixed incorrect assertions for the `enabled` state, but the relationship between `state` and the `enabled`/`disabled` booleans is still derived implicitly from tests and code. Aarav suggests adding comments or a short design note near the `ModuleParameters` and `ModuleManager` implementations, and possibly a brief docstring in the test class, to make this contract clearer for future contributors.

Role/Category: Engineering - Junior Software Engineer (EN09)
Experience: Foundational experience in software development, coding, and debugging; strong analytical thinking and problem-solving; eager to contribute to innovative projects.
Skills: Software Development, Coding, Debugging, Analytical Thinking, Problem Solving, Team Collaboration, Technical Skills.
Description: A promising Junior Software Engineer at the EN09 level, embarking on his career in software engineering with a strong willingness to learn and collaborate on high-quality software solutions.
inputs.patch:
--- a/test/units/modules/network/f5/test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py
+++ b/test/units/modules/network/f5/test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py
@@ -90,6 +90,26 @@ class TestParameters(unittest.TestCase):
 
     def test_module_parameters_state_enabled(self):
         args = dict(
             state='enabled'
         )
         p = ModuleParameters(params=args)
         assert p.state == 'enabled'
         assert p.enabled is True
         assert p.disabled is None
+
+    def test_state_flag_contract_documentation(self):
+        """Document the expected relationship between state, enabled and disabled.
+
+        This test acts as living documentation for contributors:
+        - state='present': resource exists; enabled/disabled reflect current device config.
+        - state='enabled': resource must exist and be explicitly enabled
+          (enabled=True, disabled=False).
+        - state='disabled': resource must exist and be explicitly disabled
+          (enabled=False, disabled=True).
+
+        The assertions are intentionally redundant to clarify the contract
+        and prevent regressions similar to the previously reported issue
+        where enabled-state assertions were incorrectly set to False.
+        """
+        enabled_params = ModuleParameters(params=dict(state='enabled'))
+        assert enabled_params.enabled is True
+        assert enabled_params.disabled is None
+
+        disabled_params = ModuleParameters(params=dict(state='disabled'))
+        assert disabled_params.enabled is None
+        assert disabled_params.disabled is True
@@ -150,6 +170,18 @@ class TestManager(unittest.TestCase):
         results = mm.exec_module()
         assert results['changed'] is True
         assert results['enabled'] is True
         assert results['disabled'] is False
+
+    def test_state_enabled_contract_in_manager_results(self, *args):
+        """Ensure manager result flags follow the documented state contract.
+
+        This test reinforces that an enabled datacenter yields
+        results['enabled'] == True and results['disabled'] == False,
+        preventing future regressions where these flags might be inverted
+        or left inconsistent with ModuleParameters."""
+        set_module_args(dict(state='enabled', password='admin', server='localhost', user='admin', name='foo'))
+        module = AnsibleModule(argument_spec=self.spec.argument_spec, supports_check_mode=self.spec.supports_check_mode)
+        mm = ModuleManager(module=module)
+        mm.exists = Mock(side_effect=[False, True])
+        mm.create_on_device = Mock(return_value=True)
+        results = mm.exec_module()
+        assert results['enabled'] is True
+        assert results['disabled'] is False

input_bindings.title: Clarify State Handling for GTM Datacenter Tests (present/enabled/disabled)
input_bindings.description:
Aarav Mittal (emp_0121, Junior Software Engineer, EN09) has reviewed the updated GTM datacenter test suite and would like more explicit documentation around how different `state` values (`present`, `enabled`, `disabled`) are expected to influence the `enabled` and `disabled` flags in both `ModuleParameters` and `ModuleManager`.

From the current tests in `test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py`, the behavior appears to be:
- `state='present'` -> resource exists, `enabled` not explicitly asserted, but `state` remains `present`.
- `state='enabled'` -> `ModuleParameters.enabled` and `results['enabled']` should be `True`, `disabled` should be `False`.
- `state='disabled'` -> `enabled` should be `False`, `disabled` should be `True`.

The earlier closed issue fixed incorrect assertions for the `enabled` state, but the relationship between `state` and the `enabled`/`disabled` booleans is still derived implicitly from tests and code. Aarav suggests adding comments or a short design note near the `ModuleParameters` and `ModuleManager` implementations, and possibly a brief docstring in the test class, to make this contract clearer for future contributors.

Role/Category: Engineering - Junior Software Engineer (EN09)
Experience: Foundational experience in software development, coding, and debugging; strong analytical thinking and problem-solving; eager to contribute to innovative projects.
Skills: Software Development, Coding, Debugging, Analytical Thinking, Problem Solving, Team Collaboration, Technical Skills.

input_bindings.patch:
--- a/test/units/modules/network/f5/test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py
+++ b/test/units/modules/network/f5/test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py
@@ -90,6 +90,26 @@ class TestParameters(unittest.TestCase):
 
     def test_module_parameters_state_enabled(self):
         args = dict(
             state='enabled'
         )
         p = ModuleParameters(params=args)
         assert p.state == 'enabled'
         assert p.enabled is True
         assert p.disabled is None
+
+    def test_state_flag_contract_documentation(self):
+        """Document the expected relationship between state, enabled and disabled.
+
+        This test acts as living documentation for contributors:
+        - state='present': resource exists; enabled/disabled reflect current device config.
+        - state='enabled': resource must exist and be explicitly enabled
+          (enabled=True, disabled=False).
+        - state='disabled': resource must exist and be explicitly disabled
+          (enabled=False, disabled=True).
+
+        The assertions are intentionally redundant to clarify the contract
+        and prevent regressions similar to the previously reported issue
+        where enabled-state assertions were incorrectly set to False.
+        """
+        enabled_params = ModuleParameters(params=dict(state='enabled'))
+        assert enabled_params.enabled is True
+        assert enabled_params.disabled is None
+
+        disabled_params = ModuleParameters(params=dict(state='disabled'))
+        assert disabled_params.enabled is None
+        assert disabled_params.disabled is True
@@ -150,6 +170,18 @@ class TestManager(unittest.TestCase):
         results = mm.exec_module()
         assert results['changed'] is True
         assert results['enabled'] is True
         assert results['disabled'] is False
+
+    def test_state_enabled_contract_in_manager_results(self, *args):
+        """Ensure manager result flags follow the documented state contract.
+
+        This test reinforces that an enabled datacenter yields
+        results['enabled'] == True and results['disabled'] == False,
+        preventing future regressions where these flags might be inverted
+        or left inconsistent with ModuleParameters."""
+        set_module_args(dict(state='enabled', password='admin', server='localhost', user='admin', name='foo'))
+        module = AnsibleModule(argument_spec=self.spec.argument_spec, supports_check_mode=self.spec.supports_check_mode)
+        mm = ModuleManager(module=module)
+        mm.exists = Mock(side_effect=[False, True])
+        mm.create_on_device = Mock(return_value=True)
+        results = mm.exec_module()
+        assert results['enabled'] is True
+        assert results['disabled'] is False

input_bindings.title: Clarify State Handling for GTM Datacenter Tests (present/enabled/disabled)
input_bindings.description:
Aarav Mittal (emp_0121, Junior Software Engineer, EN09) has reviewed the updated GTM datacenter test suite and would like more explicit documentation around how different `state` values (`present`, `enabled`, `disabled`) are expected to influence the `enabled` and `disabled` flags in both `ModuleParameters` and `ModuleManager`.

From the current tests in `test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py`, the behavior appears to be:
- `state='present'` -> resource exists, `enabled` not explicitly asserted, but `state` remains `present`.
- `state='enabled'` -> `ModuleParameters.enabled` and `results['enabled']` should be `True`, `disabled` should be `False`.
- `state='disabled'` -> `enabled` should be `False`, `disabled` should be `True`.

The earlier closed issue fixed incorrect assertions for the `enabled` state, but the relationship between `state` and the `enabled`/`disabled` booleans is still derived implicitly from tests and code. Aarav suggests adding comments or a short design note near the `ModuleParameters` and `ModuleManager` implementations, and possibly a brief docstring in the test class, to make this contract clearer for future contributors.

Employee context from the employees table:
Name: Aarav Mittal
Role/Category: Engineering - Junior Software Engineer (EN09)
Experience: Foundational experience in software development, coding, and debugging; strong analytical thinking and problem-solving; eager to contribute to innovative projects.
Skills: Software Development, Coding, Debugging, Analytical Thinking, Problem Solving, Team Collaboration, Technical Skills.
Description: A promising Junior Software Engineer at the EN09 level, embarking on his career in software engineering with a strong willingness to learn and collaborate on high-quality software solutions.
input_bindings.patch:
--- a/test/units/modules/network/f5/test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py
+++ b/test/units/modules/network/f5/test_bigip_gtm_datacenter.py
@@ -90,6 +90,26 @@ class TestParameters(unittest.TestCase):
 
     def test_module_parameters_state_enabled(self):
         args = dict(
             state='enabled'
         )
         p = ModuleParameters(params=args)
         assert p.state == 'enabled'
         assert p.enabled is True
         assert p.disabled is None
+
+    def test_state_flag_contract_documentation(self):
+        """Document the expected relationship between state, enabled and disabled.
+
+        This test acts as living documentation for contributors:
+        - state='present': resource exists; enabled/disabled reflect current device config.
+        - state='enabled': resource must exist and be explicitly enabled
+          (enabled=True, disabled=False).
+        - state='disabled': resource must exist and be explicitly disabled
+          (enabled=False, disabled=True).
+
+        The assertions are intentionally redundant to clarify the contract
+        and prevent regressions similar to the previously reported issue
+        where enabled-state assertions were incorrectly set to False.
+        """
+        enabled_params = ModuleParameters(params=dict(state='enabled'))
+        assert enabled_params.enabled is True
+        assert enabled_params.disabled is None
+
+        disabled_params = ModuleParameters(params=dict(state='disabled'))
+        assert disabled_params.enabled is None
+        assert disabled_params.disabled is True
@@ -150,6 +170,18 @@ class TestManager(unittest.TestCase):
         results = mm.exec_module()
         assert results['changed'] is True
         assert results['enabled'] is True
         assert results['disabled'] is False
+
+    def test_state_enabled_contract_in_manager_results(self, *args):
+        """Ensure manager result flags follow the documented state contract.
+
+        This test reinforces that an enabled datacenter yields
+        results['enabled'] == True and results['disabled'] == False,
+        preventing future regressions where these flags might be inverted
+        or left inconsistent with ModuleParameters."""
+        set_module_args(dict(state='enabled', password='admin', server='localhost', user='admin', name='foo'))
+        module = AnsibleModule(argument_spec=self.spec.argument_spec, supports_check_mode=self.spec.supports_check_mode)
+        mm = ModuleManager(module=module)
+        mm.exists = Mock(side_effect=[False, True])
+        mm.create_on_device = Mock(return_value=True)
+        results = mm.exec_module()
+        assert results['enabled'] is True
+        assert results['disabled'] is False

Please remove the sales record with ID 13476 from the sales history. In addition, register a new customer support interaction with chat ID 90615 for customer merep (customer name: jean fresnière) regarding the product boAt Type C A750 Stress Resistant, Tangle-free, Sturdy Flat Cable with 6.5A Fast Charging (product ID B09RWZRCP1). Associate the interaction with employee emp_0143 and store the following conversation text exactly as the chat content:

"Customer: Hello, I recently purchased the boAt Type C A750 cable. While the charging speed is great, I'm a bit confused about whether it's safe to use with my older power bank and laptop USB ports.

Support (emp_0143 – Finance Manager assisting with policy clarification): Thank you for reaching out and for choosing the boAt Type C A750 cable. I can help clarify usage guidelines and warranty implications. Could you share the output rating (voltage and amperage) listed on your power bank and laptop USB ports?

Customer: The power bank says 5V/2A, and my laptop USB ports are standard USB 3.0.

Support: Great, thanks for the details. The A750 cable supports up to 6.5A fast charging, but it will only draw as much current as your device and charger safely support. Using it with a 5V/2A power bank and USB 3.0 laptop ports is safe; you just won’t get the maximum 6.5A fast-charging performance—charging will occur at your charger’s supported rate.

Customer: That makes sense. Is there anything I should avoid to prevent damage?

Support: To keep everything safe and within warranty, we recommend: (1) Using BIS-certified or manufacturer-recommended chargers; (2) Avoiding visibly damaged adapters or ports; (3) Not sharply bending or pinching the flat cable near the connectors despite its stress-resistant design; and (4) Ensuring the cable is kept away from moisture and high heat sources. The product is designed for 10000+ bends, but careful use will extend its life further.

Customer: Understood. What’s the warranty coverage if something goes wrong?

Support: The boAt Type C A750 cable typically comes with a 2-year warranty from the date of purchase, covering manufacturing defects like connector failure, internal breakage not caused by misuse, or issues with data transfer under normal usage. Physical damage due to cuts, burns, or improper handling is usually not covered. Please retain your invoice, as it will be required for any claim.

Customer: Thanks, that clears things up. I’ll keep the invoice and follow these guidelines.

Support: You’re welcome. If you notice any intermittent charging, data sync issues, or visible wear, please contact us with your purchase details and we’ll guide you through the replacement or claim process. Have a great day and enjoy the hassle-free charging experience with your A750 cable." Record the interaction date as 2018-09-15.

input_bindings.product_name: boAt Type C A750 Stress Resistant, Tangle-free, Sturdy Flat Cable with 6.5A Fast Charging
input_bindings.text:
Customer: Hello, I recently purchased the boAt Type C A750 cable. While the charging speed is great, I'm a bit confused about whether it's safe to use with my older power bank and laptop USB ports.

Support (emp_0143 – Finance Manager assisting with policy clarification): Thank you for reaching out and for choosing the boAt Type C A750 cable. I can help clarify usage guidelines and warranty implications. Could you share the output rating (voltage and amperage) listed on your power bank and laptop USB ports?

Customer: The power bank says 5V/2A, and my laptop USB ports are standard USB 3.0.

Support: Great, thanks for the details. The A750 cable supports up to 6.5A fast charging, but it will only draw as much current as your device and charger safely support. Using it with a 5V/2A power bank and USB 3.0 laptop ports is safe; you just won’t get the maximum 6.5A fast-charging performance—charging will occur at your charger’s supported rate.

Customer: That makes sense. Is there anything I should avoid to prevent damage?

Support: To keep everything safe and within warranty, we recommend: (1) Using BIS-certified or manufacturer-recommended chargers; (2) Avoiding visibly damaged adapters or ports; (3) Not sharply bending or pinching the flat cable near the connectors despite its stress-resistant design; and (4) Ensuring the cable is kept away from moisture and high heat sources. The product is designed for 10000+ bends, but careful use will extend its life further.

Customer: Understood. What’s the warranty coverage if something goes wrong?

Support: The boAt Type C A750 cable typically comes with a 2-year warranty from the date of purchase, covering manufacturing defects like connector failure, internal breakage not caused by misuse, or issues with data transfer under normal usage. Physical damage due to cuts, burns, or improper handling is usually not covered. Please retain your invoice, as it will be required for any claim.

Customer: Thanks, that clears things up. I’ll keep the invoice and follow these guidelines.

Support: You’re welcome. If you notice any intermittent charging, data sync issues, or visible wear, please contact us with your purchase details and we’ll guide you through the replacement or claim process. Have a great day and enjoy the hassle-free charging experience with your A750 cable.

This is Ravi Deshmukh from Customer Support, writing to follow up on the email access difficulties you reported earlier today via IT ticket 32616. I understand that getting stuck in a credential verification loop can be disruptive, especially given the HR team’s need for continuous communication.

Thank you for your patience while we work to restore normal access.

Best regards,

Ravi

+++ 3rdParty/V8/V8-5.0.71.39/tools/swarming_client/tests/lru_test.py
@@ -1,31 +1,228 @@
-def test_basic_dict_funcs(self):

-
-  # Replace value.

-

-  self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')

-  # Removed 'with self.assertRaises(KeyError):'

-
-  # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
-  lru_dict.touch(1)
-  self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)

-  # Touch fails on missing key.
-  with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
-    lru_dict.touch(22)+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# Copyright 2013 The Swarming Authors. All rights reserved.
+# Use of this source code is governed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 that
+# can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+sys.path.insert(0, ROOT_DIR)
+
+from utils import lru
+
+
+class LRUDictTest(unittest.TestCase):
+  @staticmethod
+  def prepare_lru_dict(keys):
+    """Returns new LRUDict with given |keys| added one by one."""
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    for key in keys:
+      lru_dict.add(key, None)
+    return lru_dict
+
+  def assert_order(self, lru_dict, expected_keys):
+    """Asserts order of keys in |lru_dict| is |expected_keys|.
+
+    expected_keys[0] is supposedly oldest key, expected_keys[-1] is newest.
+
+    Destroys |lru_dict| state in the process.
+    """
+    # Check keys iteration works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(expected_keys))
+
+    # Check pop_oldest returns keys in expected order.
+    actual_keys = []
+    while lru_dict:
+      oldest_key, _ = lru_dict.pop_oldest()
+      actual_keys.append(oldest_key)
+    self.assertEqual(actual_keys, expected_keys)
+
+  def assert_same_data(self, lru_dict, regular_dict):
+    """Asserts that given |lru_dict| contains same data as |regular_dict|."""
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(regular_dict.keys()))
+    self.assertEqual(set(lru_dict.itervalues()), set(regular_dict.values()))
+
+    for k, v in regular_dict.items():
+      self.assertEqual(lru_dict.get(k), v)
+
+  def test_basic_dict_funcs(self):
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+
+    # Add a bunch.
+    data = {1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three'}
+    for k, v in data.items():
+      lru_dict.add(k, v)
+    # Check its there.
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Replace value.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one!!!')
+    data[1] = 'one!!!'
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Check pop works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')
+    data.pop(2)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Pop missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.pop(2)
+
+    # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
+    lru_dict.touch(1)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch fails on missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.touch(22)
+
+  def test_magic_methods(self):
+    # Check __nonzero__, __len__ and __contains__ for empty dict.
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    self.assertFalse(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 0)
+    self.assertFalse(1 in lru_dict)
+
+    # Dict with one item.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one')
+    self.assertTrue(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 1)
+    self.assertTrue(1 in lru_dict)
+    self.assertFalse(2 in lru_dict)
+
+  def test_order(self):
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge cases.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([]), [])
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([1]), [1])
+
+    # No touches.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict(data), data)
+
+    # Touching newest item is noop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch to move to newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # Pop newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(1)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [2, 3])
+
+    # Pop in the middle.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # Pop oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 2])
+
+    # Add oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(4, 4), (5, 5)])
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [4, 5] + data)
+
+    # Add newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data + [4])
+
+  def test_load_save(self):
+    def save_and_load(lru_dict):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        lru_dict.save(tmp_name)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        try:
+          os.unlink(tmp_name)
+        except OSError:
+          pass
+
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge case.
+    empty = save_and_load(lru.LRUDict())
+    self.assertFalse(empty)
+
+    # Normal flow.
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(self.prepare_lru_dict(data))
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # After touches.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # After pop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # After add.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(5, 5), (6, 6)])
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [5, 6] + data + [4])
+
+  def test_corrupted_state_file(self):
+    def load_from_state(state_text):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        with open(tmp_name, 'w') as f:
+          f.write(state_text)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        os.unlink(tmp_name)
+
+    # Loads correct state just fine.
+    self.assertIsNotNone(load_from_state(json.dumps([
+        ['key1', 'value1'],
+        ['key2', 'value2'],
+    ])))
+
+    # Not a json.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('garbage, not a state')
+
+    # Not a list.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('{}')
+
+    # Not a list of pairs.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value', 'and whats this?'],
+      ]))
+
+    # Duplicate keys.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value'],
+          ['key', 'another_value'],
+      ]))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+  VERBOSE = '-v' in sys.argv
+  logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if VERBOSE else logging.ERROR)
+  unittest.main()

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hello, I recently purchased the Prestige PKGSS 1.7L 1500W Electric Kettle (Stainless Steel). It generally works well, but I’ve noticed that when I boil a full 1.7L, the outer body feels quite hot to the touch and there’s a bit of condensation around the lid area. Is this normal, and is there anything I should do to use it more safely?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1112 - Rohit Agarwal): Hi Anabela, thank you for contacting us and for choosing the Prestige electric kettle. Some warmth on the stainless-steel exterior is expected with high‑wattage kettles, especially when heating to boiling, but it should not be so hot that it is unsafe to touch briefly.

To help you better, could you please confirm:
1) Whether you always fill it to the MAX line or sometimes slightly above it.
2) If the lid is firmly locked when you start boiling.
3) Whether you notice any water droplets escaping from the spout or lid during operation.

Based on your answers, we can check if this is within normal operating behavior or if the unit might have a sealing/steam‑vent issue.

CUSTOMER: I usually fill it right up to the MAX mark, sometimes just a little over when I’m making tea for more people. The lid is pressed down but I do see a bit of steam escaping near the lid and some droplets around the handle after boiling.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for the details, Anabela. Slight steam release is normal, but regularly filling above the MAX level can increase internal pressure and cause more steam and condensation around the lid area, which also makes the outer surface feel hotter.

Here are a few recommendations:
1) Always keep the water level at or below the MAX line.
2) Ensure the lid clicks fully into place before turning the kettle on.
3) After boiling, let the kettle rest on the base for 30–60 seconds before lifting, so the steam settles a bit.
4) Wipe away any condensation around the lid and handle after use to keep the surface dry and safe.

If, after following these steps, the exterior still becomes extremely hot or you see water leaking from the lid joint, please let us know—we can arrange an inspection or discuss a replacement under warranty.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll make sure not to overfill it and to let it rest a bit before lifting. Thanks for the clear explanation and safety tips.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome, Anabela. I’ve documented your feedback about the lid condensation and heat so our product team can review the design for future improvements. If you notice any unusual smells, sparks, or if the automatic cut‑off fails at any point, stop using the kettle immediately and contact us again so we can help further.

It generally works well, but I’ve noticed that when I boil a full 1.7L, the outer body feels quite hot to the touch and there’s a bit of condensation around the lid area. Is this normal, and is there anything I should do to use it more safely?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1112 - Rohit Agarwal): Hi Anabela, thank you for contacting us and for choosing the Prestige electric kettle. Some warmth on the stainless-steel exterior is expected with high‑wattage kettles, especially when heating to boiling, but it should not be so hot that it is unsafe to touch briefly.

To help you better, could you please confirm:
1) Whether you always fill it to the MAX line or sometimes slightly above it.
2) If the lid is firmly locked when you start boiling.
3) Whether you notice any water droplets escaping from the spout or lid during operation.

Based on your answers, we can check if this is within normal operating behavior or if the unit might have a sealing/steam‑vent issue.

CUSTOMER: I usually fill it right up to the MAX mark, sometimes just a little over when I’m making tea for more people. The lid is pressed down but I do see a bit of steam escaping near the lid and some droplets around the handle after boiling.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for the details, Anabela. Slight steam release is normal, but regularly filling above the MAX level can increase internal pressure and cause more steam and condensation around the lid area, which also makes the outer surface feel hotter.

Here are a few recommendations:
1) Always keep the water level at or below the MAX line.
2) Ensure the lid clicks fully into place before turning the kettle on.
3) After boiling, let the kettle rest on the base for 30–60 seconds before lifting, so the steam settles a bit.
4) Wipe away any condensation around the lid and handle after use to keep the surface dry and safe.

If, after following these steps, the exterior still becomes extremely hot or you see water leaking from the lid joint, please let us know—we can arrange an inspection or discuss a replacement under warranty.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll make sure not to overfill it and to let it rest a bit before lifting. Thanks for the clear explanation and safety tips.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome, Anabela. I’ve documented your feedback about the lid condensation and heat so our product team can review the design for future improvements. If you notice any unusual smells, sparks, or if the automatic cut‑off fails at any point, stop using the kettle immediately and contact us again so we can help further.

-    lru_dict.touch(22)+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# Copyright 2013 The Swarming Authors. All rights reserved.
+# Use of this source code is governed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 that
+# can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+sys.path.insert(0, ROOT_DIR)
+
+from utils import lru
+
+
+class LRUDictTest(unittest.TestCase):
+  @staticmethod
+  def prepare_lru_dict(keys):
+    """Returns new LRUDict with given |keys| added one by one."""
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    for key in keys:
+      lru_dict.add(key, None)
+    return lru_dict
+
+  def assert_order(self, lru_dict, expected_keys):
+    """Asserts order of keys in |lru_dict| is |expected_keys|.
+
+    expected_keys[0] is supposedly oldest key, expected_keys[-1] is newest.
+
+    Destroys |lru_dict| state in the process.
+    """
+    # Check keys iteration works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(expected_keys))
+
+    # Check pop_oldest returns keys in expected order.
+    actual_keys = []
+    while lru_dict:
+      oldest_key, _ = lru_dict.pop_oldest()
+      actual_keys.append(oldest_key)
+    self.assertEqual(actual_keys, expected_keys)
+
+  def assert_same_data(self, lru_dict, regular_dict):
+    """Asserts that given |lru_dict| contains same data as |regular_dict|."""
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(regular_dict.keys()))
+    self.assertEqual(set(lru_dict.itervalues()), set(regular_dict.values()))
+
+    for k, v in regular_dict.items():
+      self.assertEqual(lru_dict.get(k), v)
+
+  def test_basic_dict_funcs(self):
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+
+    # Add a bunch.
+    data = {1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three'}
+    for k, v in data.items():
+      lru_dict.add(k, v)
+    # Check its there.
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Replace value.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one!!!')
+    data[1] = 'one!!!'
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Check pop works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')
+    data.pop(2)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Pop missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.pop(2)
+
+    # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
+    lru_dict.touch(1)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch fails on missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.touch(22)
+
+  def test_magic_methods(self):
+    # Check __nonzero__, __len__ and __contains__ for empty dict.
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    self.assertFalse(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 0)
+    self.assertFalse(1 in lru_dict)
+
+    # Dict with one item.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one')
+    self.assertTrue(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 1)
+    self.assertTrue(1 in lru_dict)
+    self.assertFalse(2 in lru_dict)
+
+  def test_order(self):
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge cases.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([]), [])
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([1]), [1])
+
+    # No touches.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict(data), data)
+
+    # Touching newest item is noop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch to move to newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # Pop newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(1)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [2, 3])
+
+    # Pop in the middle.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # Pop oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 2])
+
+    # Add oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(4, 4), (5, 5)])
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [4, 5] + data)
+
+    # Add newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data + [4])
+
+  def test_load_save(self):
+    def save_and_load(lru_dict):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        lru_dict.save(tmp_name)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        try:
+          os.unlink(tmp_name)
+        except OSError:
+          pass
+
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge case.
+    empty = save_and_load(lru.LRUDict())
+    self.assertFalse(empty)
+
+    # Normal flow.
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(self.prepare_lru_dict(data))
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # After touches.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # After pop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # After add.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(5, 5), (6, 6)])
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [5, 6] + data + [4])
+
+  def test_corrupted_state_file(self):
+    def load_from_state(state_text):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        with open(tmp_name, 'w') as f:
+          f.write(state_text)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        os.unlink(tmp_name)
+
+    # Loads correct state just fine.
+    self.assertIsNotNone(load_from_state(json.dumps([
+        ['key1', 'value1'],
+        ['key2', 'value2'],
+    ])))
+
+    # Not a json.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('garbage, not a state')
+
+    # Not a list.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('{}')
+
+    # Not a list of pairs.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value', 'and whats this?'],
+      ]))
+
+    # Duplicate keys.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value'],
+          ['key', 'another_value'],
+      ]))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+  VERBOSE = '-v' in sys.argv
+  logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if VERBOSE else logging.ERROR)
+  unittest.main()

CUSTOMER: Hello, I recently purchased the Prestige PKGSS 1.7L 1500W Electric Kettle (Stainless Steel). It generally works well, but I’ve noticed that when I boil a full 1.7L, the outer body feels quite hot to the touch and there’s a bit of condensation around the lid area. Is this normal, and is there anything I should do to use it more safely?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1112 - Rohit Agarwal): Hi Anabela, thank you for contacting us and for choosing the Prestige electric kettle. Some warmth on the stainless-steel exterior is expected with high‑wattage kettles, especially when heating to boiling, but it should not be so hot that it is unsafe to touch briefly.

To help you better, could you please confirm:
1) Whether you always fill it to the MAX line or sometimes slightly above it.
2) If the lid is firmly locked when you start boiling.
3) Whether you notice any water droplets escaping from the spout or lid during operation.

Based on your answers, we can check if this is within normal operating behavior or if the unit might have a sealing/steam‑vent issue.

CUSTOMER: I usually fill it right up to the MAX mark, sometimes just a little over when I’m making tea for more people. The lid is pressed down but I do see a bit of steam escaping near the lid and some droplets around the handle after boiling.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for the details, Anabela. Slight steam release is normal, but regularly filling above the MAX level can increase internal pressure and cause more steam and condensation around the lid area, which also makes the outer surface feel hotter.

Here are a few recommendations:
1) Always keep the water level at or below the MAX line.
2) Ensure the lid clicks fully into place before turning the kettle on.
3) After boiling, let the kettle rest on the base for 30–60 seconds before lifting, so the steam settles a bit.
4) Wipe away any condensation around the lid and handle after use to keep the surface dry and safe.

If, after following these steps, the exterior still becomes extremely hot or you see water leaking from the lid joint, please let us know—we can arrange an inspection or discuss a replacement under warranty.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll make sure not to overfill it and to let it rest a bit before lifting. Thanks for the clear explanation and safety tips.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome, Anabela. I’ve documented your feedback about the lid condensation and heat so our product team can review the design for future improvements. If you notice any unusual smells, sparks, or if the automatic cut‑off fails at any point, stop using the kettle immediately and contact us again so we can help further.

--- 3rdParty/V8/V8-5.0.71.39/tools/swarming_client/tests/lru_test.py
+++ 3rdParty/V8/V8-5.0.71.39/tools/swarming_client/tests/lru_test.py
@@ -1,31 +1,228 @@

-  self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')

-  self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
-

-  # Removed 'with self.assertRaises(KeyError):'

-

-  lru_dict.touch(1)

-
-  # Touch fails on missing key.
-  with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
-    lru_dict.touch(22)+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# Copyright 2013 The Swarming Authors. All rights reserved.
+# Use of this source code is governed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 that
+# can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+sys.path.insert(0, ROOT_DIR)
+
+from utils import lru
+
+
+class LRUDictTest(unittest.TestCase):
+  @staticmethod
+  def prepare_lru_dict(keys):
+    """Returns new LRUDict with given |keys| added one by one."""
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    for key in keys:
+      lru_dict.add(key, None)
+    return lru_dict
+
+  def assert_order(self, lru_dict, expected_keys):
+    """Asserts order of keys in |lru_dict| is |expected_keys|.
+
+    expected_keys[0] is supposedly oldest key, expected_keys[-1] is newest.
+
+    Destroys |lru_dict| state in the process.
+    """
+    # Check keys iteration works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(expected_keys))
+
+    # Check pop_oldest returns keys in expected order.
+    actual_keys = []
+    while lru_dict:
+      oldest_key, _ = lru_dict.pop_oldest()
+      actual_keys.append(oldest_key)
+    self.assertEqual(actual_keys, expected_keys)
+
+  def assert_same_data(self, lru_dict, regular_dict):
+    """Asserts that given |lru_dict| contains same data as |regular_dict|."""
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(regular_dict.keys()))
+    self.assertEqual(set(lru_dict.itervalues()), set(regular_dict.values()))
+
+    for k, v in regular_dict.items():
+      self.assertEqual(lru_dict.get(k), v)
+
+  def test_basic_dict_funcs(self):
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+
+    # Add a bunch.
+    data = {1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three'}
+    for k, v in data.items():
+      lru_dict.add(k, v)
+    # Check its there.
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Replace value.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one!!!')
+    data[1] = 'one!!!'
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Check pop works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')
+    data.pop(2)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Pop missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.pop(2)
+
+    # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
+    lru_dict.touch(1)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch fails on missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.touch(22)
+
+  def test_magic_methods(self):
+    # Check __nonzero__, __len__ and __contains__ for empty dict.
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    self.assertFalse(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 0)
+    self.assertFalse(1 in lru_dict)
+
+    # Dict with one item.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one')
+    self.assertTrue(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 1)
+    self.assertTrue(1 in lru_dict)
+    self.assertFalse(2 in lru_dict)
+
+  def test_order(self):
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge cases.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([]), [])
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([1]), [1])
+
+    # No touches.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict(data), data)
+
+    # Touching newest item is noop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch to move to newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # Pop newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(1)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [2, 3])
+
+    # Pop in the middle.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # Pop oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 2])
+
+    # Add oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(4, 4), (5, 5)])
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [4, 5] + data)
+
+    # Add newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data + [4])
+
+  def test_load_save(self):
+    def save_and_load(lru_dict):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        lru_dict.save(tmp_name)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        try:
+          os.unlink(tmp_name)
+        except OSError:
+          pass
+
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge case.
+    empty = save_and_load(lru.LRUDict())
+    self.assertFalse(empty)
+
+    # Normal flow.
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(self.prepare_lru_dict(data))
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # After touches.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # After pop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # After add.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(5, 5), (6, 6)])
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [5, 6] + data + [4])
+
+  def test_corrupted_state_file(self):
+    def load_from_state(state_text):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        with open(tmp_name, 'w') as f:
+          f.write(state_text)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        os.unlink(tmp_name)
+
+    # Loads correct state just fine.
+    self.assertIsNotNone(load_from_state(json.dumps([
+        ['key1', 'value1'],
+        ['key2', 'value2'],
+    ])))
+
+    # Not a json.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('garbage, not a state')
+
+    # Not a list.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('{}')
+
+    # Not a list of pairs.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value', 'and whats this?'],
+      ]))
+
+    # Duplicate keys.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value'],
+          ['key', 'another_value'],
+      ]))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+  VERBOSE = '-v' in sys.argv
+  logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if VERBOSE else logging.ERROR)
+  unittest.main()

input_bindings.product_name: Prestige PKGSS 1.7L 1500W Electric Kettle (Stainless Steel)
input_bindings.text:
CUSTOMER: Hello, I recently purchased the Prestige PKGSS 1.7L 1500W Electric Kettle (Stainless Steel). It generally works well, but I’ve noticed that when I boil a full 1.7L, the outer body feels quite hot to the touch and there’s a bit of condensation around the lid area. Is this normal, and is there anything I should do to use it more safely?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1112 - Rohit Agarwal): Hi Anabela, thank you for contacting us and for choosing the Prestige electric kettle. Some warmth on the stainless-steel exterior is expected with high‑wattage kettles, especially when heating to boiling, but it should not be so hot that it is unsafe to touch briefly.

To help you better, could you please confirm:
1) Whether you always fill it to the MAX line or sometimes slightly above it.
2) If the lid is firmly locked when you start boiling.
3) Whether you notice any water droplets escaping from the spout or lid during operation.

Based on your answers, we can check if this is within normal operating behavior or if the unit might have a sealing/steam‑vent issue.

CUSTOMER: I usually fill it right up to the MAX mark, sometimes just a little over when I’m making tea for more people. The lid is pressed down but I do see a bit of steam escaping near the lid and some droplets around the handle after boiling.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for the details, Anabela. Slight steam release is normal, but regularly filling above the MAX level can increase internal pressure and cause more steam and condensation around the lid area, which also makes the outer surface feel hotter.

Here are a few recommendations:
1) Always keep the water level at or below the MAX line.
2) Ensure the lid clicks fully into place before turning the kettle on.
3) After boiling, let the kettle rest on the base for 30–60 seconds before lifting, so the steam settles a bit.
4) Wipe away any condensation around the lid and handle after use to keep the surface dry and safe.

If, after following these steps, the exterior still becomes extremely hot or you see water leaking from the lid joint, please let us know—we can arrange an inspection or discuss a replacement under warranty.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll make sure not to overfill it and to let it rest a bit before lifting. Thanks for the clear explanation and safety tips.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome, Anabela. I’ve documented your feedback about the lid condensation and heat so our product team can review the design for future improvements. If you notice any unusual smells, sparks, or if the automatic cut‑off fails at any point, stop using the kettle immediately and contact us again so we can help further.

-

-  lru_dict.touch(1)

-
-  # Touch fails on missing key.

-    lru_dict.touch(22)+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# Copyright 2013 The Swarming Authors. All rights reserved.
+# Use of this source code is governed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 that
+# can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+sys.path.insert(0, ROOT_DIR)
+
+from utils import lru
+
+
+class LRUDictTest(unittest.TestCase):
+  @staticmethod
+  def prepare_lru_dict(keys):
+    """Returns new LRUDict with given |keys| added one by one."""
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    for key in keys:
+      lru_dict.add(key, None)
+    return lru_dict
+
+  def assert_order(self, lru_dict, expected_keys):
+    """Asserts order of keys in |lru_dict| is |expected_keys|.
+
+    expected_keys[0] is supposedly oldest key, expected_keys[-1] is newest.
+
+    Destroys |lru_dict| state in the process.
+    """
+    # Check keys iteration works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(expected_keys))
+
+    # Check pop_oldest returns keys in expected order.
+    actual_keys = []
+    while lru_dict:
+      oldest_key, _ = lru_dict.pop_oldest()
+      actual_keys.append(oldest_key)
+    self.assertEqual(actual_keys, expected_keys)
+
+  def assert_same_data(self, lru_dict, regular_dict):
+    """Asserts that given |lru_dict| contains same data as |regular_dict|."""
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(regular_dict.keys()))
+    self.assertEqual(set(lru_dict.itervalues()), set(regular_dict.values()))
+
+    for k, v in regular_dict.items():
+      self.assertEqual(lru_dict.get(k), v)
+
+  def test_basic_dict_funcs(self):
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+
+    # Add a bunch.
+    data = {1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three'}
+    for k, v in data.items():
+      lru_dict.add(k, v)
+    # Check its there.
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Replace value.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one!!!')
+    data[1] = 'one!!!'
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Check pop works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')
+    data.pop(2)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Pop missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.pop(2)
+
+    # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
+    lru_dict.touch(1)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch fails on missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.touch(22)
+
+  def test_magic_methods(self):
+    # Check __nonzero__, __len__ and __contains__ for empty dict.
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    self.assertFalse(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 0)
+    self.assertFalse(1 in lru_dict)
+
+    # Dict with one item.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one')
+    self.assertTrue(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 1)
+    self.assertTrue(1 in lru_dict)
+    self.assertFalse(2 in lru_dict)
+
+  def test_order(self):
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge cases.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([]), [])
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([1]), [1])
+
+    # No touches.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict(data), data)
+
+    # Touching newest item is noop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch to move to newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # Pop newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(1)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [2, 3])
+
+    # Pop in the middle.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # Pop oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 2])
+
+    # Add oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(4, 4), (5, 5)])
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [4, 5] + data)
+
+    # Add newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data + [4])
+
+  def test_load_save(self):
+    def save_and_load(lru_dict):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        lru_dict.save(tmp_name)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        try:
+          os.unlink(tmp_name)
+        except OSError:
+          pass
+
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge case.
+    empty = save_and_load(lru.LRUDict())
+    self.assertFalse(empty)
+
+    # Normal flow.
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(self.prepare_lru_dict(data))
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # After touches.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # After pop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # After add.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(5, 5), (6, 6)])
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [5, 6] + data + [4])
+
+  def test_corrupted_state_file(self):
+    def load_from_state(state_text):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        with open(tmp_name, 'w') as f:
+          f.write(state_text)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        os.unlink(tmp_name)
+
+    # Loads correct state just fine.
+    self.assertIsNotNone(load_from_state(json.dumps([
+        ['key1', 'value1'],
+        ['key2', 'value2'],
+    ])))
+
+    # Not a json.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('garbage, not a state')
+
+    # Not a list.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('{}')
+
+    # Not a list of pairs.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value', 'and whats this?'],
+      ]))
+
+    # Duplicate keys.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value'],
+          ['key', 'another_value'],
+      ]))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+  VERBOSE = '-v' in sys.argv
+  logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if VERBOSE else logging.ERROR)
+  unittest.main()

input_bindings.product_name: Prestige PKGSS 1.7L 1500W Electric Kettle (Stainless Steel)
input_bindings.text:
CUSTOMER: Hello, I recently purchased the Prestige PKGSS 1.7L 1500W Electric Kettle (Stainless Steel). It generally works well, but I’ve noticed that when I boil a full 1.7L, the outer body feels quite hot to the touch and there’s a bit of condensation around the lid area. Is this normal, and is there anything I should do to use it more safely?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1112 - Rohit Agarwal): Hi Anabela, thank you for contacting us and for choosing the Prestige electric kettle. Some warmth on the stainless-steel exterior is expected with high‑wattage kettles, especially when heating to boiling, but it should not be so hot that it is unsafe to touch briefly.

To help you better, could you please confirm:
1) Whether you always fill it to the MAX line or sometimes slightly above it.
2) If the lid is firmly locked when you start boiling.
3) Whether you notice any water droplets escaping from the spout or lid during operation.

Based on your answers, we can check if this is within normal operating behavior or if the unit might have a sealing/steam‑vent issue.

CUSTOMER: I usually fill it right up to the MAX mark, sometimes just a little over when I’m making tea for more people. The lid is pressed down but I do see a bit of steam escaping near the lid and some droplets around the handle after boiling.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for the details, Anabela. Slight steam release is normal, but regularly filling above the MAX level can increase internal pressure and cause more steam and condensation around the lid area, which also makes the outer surface feel hotter.

Here are a few recommendations:
1) Always keep the water level at or below the MAX line.
2) Ensure the lid clicks fully into place before turning the kettle on.
3) After boiling, let the kettle rest on the base for 30–60 seconds before lifting, so the steam settles a bit.
4) Wipe away any condensation around the lid and handle after use to keep the surface dry and safe.

If, after following these steps, the exterior still becomes extremely hot or you see water leaking from the lid joint, please let us know—we can arrange an inspection or discuss a replacement under warranty.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll make sure not to overfill it and to let it rest a bit before lifting. Thanks for the clear explanation and safety tips.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome, Anabela. I’ve documented your feedback about the lid condensation and heat so our product team can review the design for future improvements. If you notice any unusual smells, sparks, or if the automatic cut‑off fails at any point, stop using the kettle immediately and contact us again so we can help further.

inputs.Issue: Hi IT Support, this is Neha Verma (emp_1352) from the Engineering team.
