Employee_id: emp_1231
For customer Yang Wang (customer ID chops), locate their existing account details, including any linked invoices, purchase orders, and shipping documents. Using that same customer record, create and save a new customer support chat entry with chat ID 74845 for product B08D6RCM3Q, the PrettyKrafts Folding Laundry Basket with Lid, Mushroom Print, 75L. The interaction should be recorded under employee Tarun Varma (employee ID emp_1231), dated April 2, 2019, and include the following full transcript as the chat content:

"CUSTOMER SUPPORT CHAT TRANSCRIPT

CUSTOMER (yang wang / ID: chops): Hi, I recently bought the PrettyKrafts folding laundry basket with the mushroom print. The description mentioned a 75 litre capacity and a removable lid, but my basket seems smaller than expected and the lid doesn’t sit properly.

SUPPORT REP (Tarun Varma, emp_1231): Hello Yang, thanks for reaching out. I’m sorry to hear about the issue with your laundry basket. I can help you with this. Could you confirm if the product ID on your invoice matches B08D6RCM3Q and whether the product arrived with any visible damage?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the invoice says B08D6RCM3Q and there was no visible damage to the packaging. It’s just that the basket feels more cramped than described and the lid tilts to one side.

SUPPORT REP: Understood, thank you for confirming. The advertised dimensions are approximately Length 15 inch x Width 14 inch x Height 21.5 inch, with a nominal volume of 75 litres. Sometimes minor manufacturing tolerance can cause a small variation, but it shouldn’t affect lid alignment. Let’s try a quick check:
1) Please ensure the base is fully opened and the sides are pushed out evenly.
2) Check if any of the stitching around the upper rim is loose or uneven.

If the lid still does not sit flat after this, we can proceed with either a replacement or a refund.

CUSTOMER: I’ve tried that. The sides are fully opened and the stitching looks fine, but the lid still doesn’t align properly.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for trying, Yang. Since the troubleshooting did not resolve the issue, I’ll initiate a quality-issue case for product B08D6RCM3Q and arrange a free replacement for you. You will receive an email shortly with a pickup label for the current basket and tracking details for the new one. If you’d prefer a refund instead of replacement, you can reply to that email and our team will adjust the request.

CUSTOMER: A replacement works for me. Please go ahead with that.

SUPPORT REP: Great, I’ve submitted the replacement request and linked it to your customer ID (chops) and the original order. You should receive an update within 24–48 hours. If you notice any other issues or if the replacement also feels off, please contact us again and we’ll review alternative options.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Yang. We appreciate your patience and feedback — it helps us improve our product quality. Have a good day!"

input_bindings.text:
CUSTOMER SUPPORT CHAT TRANSCRIPT

CUSTOMER (yang wang / ID: chops): Hi, I recently bought the PrettyKrafts folding laundry basket with the mushroom print. The description mentioned a 75 litre capacity and a removable lid, but my basket seems smaller than expected and the lid doesn’t sit properly.

SUPPORT REP (Tarun Varma, emp_1231): Hello Yang, thanks for reaching out. I’m sorry to hear about the issue with your laundry basket. I can help you with this. Could you confirm if the product ID on your invoice matches B08D6RCM3Q and whether the product arrived with any visible damage?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the invoice says B08D6RCM3Q and there was no visible damage to the packaging. It’s just that the basket feels more cramped than described and the lid tilts to one side.

SUPPORT REP: Understood, thank you for confirming. The advertised dimensions are approximately Length 15 inch x Width 14 inch x Height 21.5 inch, with a nominal volume of 75 litres. Sometimes minor manufacturing tolerance can cause a small variation, but it shouldn’t affect lid alignment. Let’s try a quick check:
1) Please ensure the base is fully opened and the sides are pushed out evenly.
2) Check if any of the stitching around the upper rim is loose or uneven.

If the lid still does not sit flat after this, we can proceed with either a replacement or a refund.

CUSTOMER: I’ve tried that. The sides are fully opened and the stitching looks fine, but the lid still doesn’t align properly.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for trying, Yang. Since the troubleshooting did not resolve the issue, I’ll initiate a quality-issue case for product B08D6RCM3Q and arrange a free replacement for you. You will receive an email shortly with a pickup label for the current basket and tracking details for the new one. If you’d prefer a refund instead of replacement, you can reply to that email and our team will adjust the request.

CUSTOMER: A replacement works for me. Please go ahead with that.

SUPPORT REP: Great, I’ve submitted the replacement request and linked it to your customer ID (chops) and the original order. You should receive an update within 24–48 hours. If you notice any other issues or if the replacement also feels off, please contact us again and we’ll review alternative options.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Yang. We appreciate your patience and feedback — it helps us improve our product quality. Have a good day!

instruction:
Employee ID: emp_0812
Please register a new customer support interaction under chat reference 861 for customer Christina Berglund (customer ID bergs) regarding her Redmi 10A (Slate Grey, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, product ID B09XB7SRQ5). Record the following conversation text in full as the interaction content and associate it with employee ID emp_0812, dated 2018-11-12:

"CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Redmi 10A and I’m facing frequent app freezes and occasional reboots, especially when using the camera and switching between apps quickly. Can you help?

SUPPORT REP (Jonathan Sinclair, Business Development): Thanks for reaching out, Christina. I’m sorry to hear about the issues you’re experiencing with your Redmi 10A. To assist you better, could you confirm whether all system and app updates have been installed, and whether you’ve recently added any new apps just before the freezes began?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the phone says it’s up to date. I did install a couple of games last week, but the freezing happens even when I’m just using the camera or WhatsApp.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Let’s try a couple of troubleshooting steps. First, please clear the cache for the camera and messaging apps from Settings > Apps. Next, try restarting the device in safe mode to see if the issue persists without third‑party apps running. If the phone is still freezing in safe mode, it may indicate a deeper system or hardware issue.

CUSTOMER: I tried safe mode and it still froze once when I opened the camera.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking that. Since the problem persists in safe mode, I’d like to register this as a service case and arrange a diagnostic at our authorized service center. The technicians can run hardware checks on the memory and storage and, if needed, re‑flash the software. If a defect is confirmed, you’ll be eligible for a repair or replacement as per warranty terms.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Please proceed.

SUPPORT REP: I’ve created a service request tied to your customer profile and purchase record. You’ll receive an email shortly with the case number, service center details near your location, and instructions on backing up your data before handing over the device. If you notice any new symptoms or error messages, please include them when you visit the center so we have a complete picture.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the clear explanation and next steps.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Christina. We appreciate your patience and will do our best to resolve this quickly. If you have any questions or need to reschedule your appointment, feel free to reply to the email or contact our support line."

inputs.body:
Hi Nicole,

I’m reaching out from the engineering team regarding your earlier issue with the locked email account (IT Ticket 30590). Beyond the immediate fix that Nishant implemented, we’re working on improving how IT tickets, email threads, and customer-support chats connect behind the scenes.

Specifically, I’m proposing a small pilot where your future email access incidents are automatically associated with a unified thread ID, so that:
- IT can see related email messages directly within the ticket view,
- Customer-support representatives can reference the same thread when assisting your clients,
- We can better audit and prevent repeat lockout patterns.

This email has been attached to Ticket 30590 as a starting point for that unified thread. If you’re comfortable participating, I’d appreciate any feedback on what kind of status updates or alerts you’d like to receive when access issues occur (e.g., automatic notifications, escalation rules, or integration with your sales dashboards).

Thanks for your time, and for helping us make our internal tooling more reliable for the Sales team.

Best regards,
Rahul

CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Redmi 10A and I’m facing frequent app freezes and occasional reboots, especially when using the camera and switching between apps quickly. Can you help?

To assist you better, could you confirm whether all system and app updates have been installed, and whether you’ve recently added any new apps just before the freezes began?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the phone says it’s up to date. I did install a couple of games last week, but the freezing happens even when I’m just using the camera or WhatsApp.

Next, try restarting the device in safe mode to see if the issue persists without third‑party apps running. If the phone is still freezing in safe mode, it may indicate a deeper system or hardware issue.

If a defect is confirmed, you’ll be eligible for a repair or replacement as per warranty terms.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Please proceed.

SUPPORT REP: I’ve created a service request tied to your customer profile and purchase record. You’ll receive an email shortly with the case number, service center details near your location, and instructions on backing up your data before handing over the device. If you notice any new symptoms or error messages, please include them when you visit the center so we have a complete picture.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the clear explanation and next steps.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Christina. We appreciate your patience and will do our best to resolve this quickly. If you have any questions or need to reschedule your appointment, feel free to reply to the email or contact our support line.

inputs.body:
Hi Nicole,

I’m reaching out from the engineering team regarding your earlier issue with the locked email account (IT Ticket 30590). Beyond the immediate fix that Nishant implemented, we’re working on improving how IT tickets, email threads, and customer-support chats connect behind the scenes.

Specifically, I’m proposing a small pilot where your future email access incidents are automatically associated with a unified thread ID, so that:
- IT can see related email messages directly within the ticket view,
- Customer-support representatives can reference the same thread when assisting your clients,
- We can better audit and prevent repeat lockout patterns.

Thanks for your time, and for helping us make our internal tooling more reliable for the Sales team.

Best regards,
Rahul

inputs.product_name: iQOO Z6 Lite 5G by vivo (Stellar Green, 6GB RAM, 128GB Storage)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I bought the iQOO Z6 Lite 5G recently and I’m unsure about the best way to optimize battery life while using 5G and high refresh rate.

SUPPORT REP (Riya Sharma - emp_1379): Hello matti, thanks for reaching out. Since you’re using 5G and a 120Hz refresh rate, both can impact battery life. I’d recommend enabling the phone’s adaptive refresh rate so it only uses 120Hz when needed, and turning off 5G when you’re on Wi‑Fi or don’t need high-speed data.

SUPPORT REP: You can also lower screen brightness, disable background app refresh for non-essential apps, and use the built-in battery optimization mode. These steps together usually provide a noticeable improvement.

CUSTOMER: That sounds helpful. Is there any risk in frequently switching between 5G and 4G?

SUPPORT REP: No functional risk to the device; it’s designed to handle that seamlessly. The main trade-off is convenience vs. battery usage. If you prioritize battery life, keeping 5G off when not needed is a good practice.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll follow these steps. Thank you for the clear explanation.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, matti. If you experience any unusual battery drain even after these changes, feel free to contact us again and we can walk through more advanced diagnostics.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll follow these steps. Thank you for the clear explanation.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, matti. If you experience any unusual battery drain even after these changes, feel free to contact us again and we can walk through more advanced diagnostics.

The login succeeds occasionally but often times out or returns an authorization error, which is slowing down my ability to monitor deployments and debug production issues. Could you please investigate whether there are any directory, SSO, or network configuration problems affecting my account or machine and help restore stable access?
inputs.Resolution: Hi Riya, thanks for reporting the intermittent authentication issues with the microservices dashboard and CI/CD pipeline. We have reviewed your account in the directory service, verified your SSO configuration, and checked for any network-level throttling or firewall rules affecting your workstation. Your group memberships and permissions are correct, but we identified transient network packet loss from your floor segment. As an immediate fix, we have updated the routing configuration for your subnet and restarted the local authentication proxy. Please sign out of all enterprise apps, clear your SSO session, and reboot your workstation before trying again. If you still encounter timeouts or authorization errors after these steps, reply to this ticket with exact timestamps and URLs so we can capture additional logs and perform deeper analysis.

CUSTOMER: Hi, I bought the iQOO Z6 Lite 5G recently and I’m unsure about the best way to optimize battery life while using 5G and high refresh rate.

SUPPORT REP (Riya Sharma - emp_1379): Hello matti, thanks for reaching out. Since you’re using 5G and a 120Hz refresh rate, both can impact battery life. I’d recommend enabling the phone’s adaptive refresh rate so it only uses 120Hz when needed, and turning off 5G when you’re on Wi‑Fi or don’t need high-speed data.

SUPPORT REP: You can also lower screen brightness, disable background app refresh for non-essential apps, and use the built-in battery optimization mode. These steps together usually provide a noticeable improvement.

CUSTOMER: That sounds helpful. Is there any risk in frequently switching between 5G and 4G?

SUPPORT REP: No functional risk to the device; it’s designed to handle that seamlessly. The main trade-off is convenience vs. battery usage. If you prioritize battery life, keeping 5G off when not needed is a good practice.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll follow these steps. Thank you for the clear explanation.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, matti. If you experience any unusual battery drain even after these changes, feel free to contact us again and we can walk through more advanced diagnostics.

inputs.product_name: RC PRINT GI 790 Ink Refill for Canon G-series PIXMA Printers
inputs.text:
Customer Support Chat Transcript

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm having trouble with the RC PRINT GI 790 ink refill I bought for my Canon PIXMA G2010. After refilling, the prints are coming out streaky and some colors seem faded. I followed the basic instructions, but I'm not sure if I missed a step.

SUPPORT REP (Allen Thompson, Engineering): Thanks for reaching out, Paolo. I understand how frustrating print quality issues can be, especially when you're relying on accurate colors. Let me walk you through a quick diagnostic and a few steps that usually resolve these problems.

First, please confirm:
1) Which exact printer model are you using (e.g., G2010, G3010, etc.)?
2) Whether you fully cleaned the ink tank and print head before using the RC PRINT GI 790 ink, as mixing old pigment ink with new dye ink can cause streaks.

In the meantime, here are some steps you can try:
- Run the printer's built-in nozzle check and head cleaning routine from the maintenance menu.
- Make sure the ink tanks are not overfilled and that the vent caps are properly open.
- Print a test page using the printer's highest quality setting to see if the issue persists.

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Canon PIXMA G2012. I did a quick clean of the tank, but I don't think I fully flushed the old ink out. I haven't run the nozzle check yet.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. Since G2012 is fully compatible with RC PRINT GI 790, the issue is likely due to residual pigment ink mixing with the new dye-based ink.

Here is what I recommend:
1) Perform a deep cleaning cycle from the printer maintenance settings (not just a standard cleaning).
2) If possible, flush the print head with compatible cleaning solution recommended for Canon G-series before refilling again.
3) After cleaning, refill with fresh RC PRINT GI 790 ink, ensuring each color tank is filled only to the indicated line.
4) Run a nozzle check and align the print head.

If, after these steps, streaks remain, please send us a scanned sample of the print. We can analyze the pattern and confirm if the print head has a hardware issue or if further software-level calibration is needed.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. I'll perform the deep cleaning and refill properly following your steps. If it still looks off, I'll send a sample.

SUPPORT REP: Great. Once you've tried these steps, reply to this chat or email us the scanned print at support@inazuma-print.com with the subject line "RC PRINT GI 790 – Quality Check for Paolo (frans)". We'll monitor your case and, if needed, arrange a replacement ink batch or additional guidance.

Thank you for your patience and for choosing RC PRINT GI 790. We're here to help you get clear, vibrant prints again.

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm having trouble with the RC PRINT GI 790 ink refill I bought for my Canon PIXMA G2010. After refilling, the prints are coming out streaky and some colors seem faded. I followed the basic instructions, but I'm not sure if I missed a step.

SUPPORT REP (Allen Thompson, Engineering): Thanks for reaching out, Paolo. I understand how frustrating print quality issues can be, especially when you're relying on accurate colors. Let me walk you through a quick diagnostic and a few steps that usually resolve these problems.

First, please confirm:
1) Which exact printer model are you using (e.g., G2010, G3010, etc.)?
2) Whether you fully cleaned the ink tank and print head before using the RC PRINT GI 790 ink, as mixing old pigment ink with new dye ink can cause streaks.

In the meantime, here are some steps you can try:
- Run the printer's built-in nozzle check and head cleaning routine from the maintenance menu.
- Make sure the ink tanks are not overfilled and that the vent caps are properly open.
- Print a test page using the printer's highest quality setting to see if the issue persists.

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Canon PIXMA G2012. I did a quick clean of the tank, but I don't think I fully flushed the old ink out. I haven't run the nozzle check yet.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. Since G2012 is fully compatible with RC PRINT GI 790, the issue is likely due to residual pigment ink mixing with the new dye-based ink.

Here is what I recommend:
1) Perform a deep cleaning cycle from the printer maintenance settings (not just a standard cleaning).
2) If possible, flush the print head with compatible cleaning solution recommended for Canon G-series before refilling again.
3) After cleaning, refill with fresh RC PRINT GI 790 ink, ensuring each color tank is filled only to the indicated line.
4) Run a nozzle check and align the print head.

If, after these steps, streaks remain, please send us a scanned sample of the print. We can analyze the pattern and confirm if the print head has a hardware issue or if further software-level calibration is needed.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. I'll perform the deep cleaning and refill properly following your steps. If it still looks off, I'll send a sample.

SUPPORT REP: Great. Once you've tried these steps, reply to this chat or email us the scanned print at support@inazuma-print.com with the subject line "RC PRINT GI 790 – Quality Check for Paolo (frans)". We'll monitor your case and, if needed, arrange a replacement ink batch or additional guidance.

Thank you for your patience and for choosing RC PRINT GI 790. We're here to help you get clear, vibrant prints again.

inputs.product_name: RC PRINT GI 790 Ink Refill for Canon G-series PIXMA Printers
inputs.text:
Customer Support Chat Transcript

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm having trouble with the RC PRINT GI 790 ink refill I bought for my Canon PIXMA G2010. After refilling, the prints are coming out streaky and some colors seem faded. I followed the basic instructions, but I'm not sure if I missed a step.

SUPPORT REP (Allen Thompson, Engineering): Thanks for reaching out, Paolo. I understand how frustrating print quality issues can be, especially when you're relying on accurate colors. Let me walk you through a quick diagnostic and a few steps that usually resolve these problems.

First, please confirm:
1) Which exact printer model are you using (e.g., G2010, G3010, etc.)?
2) Whether you fully cleaned the ink tank and print head before using the RC PRINT GI 790 ink, as mixing old pigment ink with new dye ink can cause streaks.

In the meantime, here are some steps you can try:
- Run the printer's built-in nozzle check and head cleaning routine from the maintenance menu.
- Make sure the ink tanks are not overfilled and that the vent caps are properly open.
- Print a test page using the printer's highest quality setting to see if the issue persists.

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Canon PIXMA G2012. I did a quick clean of the tank, but I don't think I fully flushed the old ink out. I haven't run the nozzle check yet.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. Since G2012 is fully compatible with RC PRINT GI 790, the issue is likely due to residual pigment ink mixing with the new dye-based ink.

Here is what I recommend:
1) Perform a deep cleaning cycle from the printer maintenance settings (not just a standard cleaning).
2) If possible, flush the print head with compatible cleaning solution recommended for Canon G-series before refilling again.
3) After cleaning, refill with fresh RC PRINT GI 790 ink, ensuring each color tank is filled only to the indicated line.
4) Run a nozzle check and align the print head.

If, after these steps, streaks remain, please send us a scanned sample of the print. We can analyze the pattern and confirm if the print head has a hardware issue or if further software-level calibration is needed.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. I'll perform the deep cleaning and refill properly following your steps. If it still looks off, I'll send a sample.

SUPPORT REP: Great. Once you've tried these steps, reply to this chat or email us the scanned print at support@inazuma-print.com with the subject line "RC PRINT GI 790 – Quality Check for Paolo (frans)". We'll monitor your case and, if needed, arrange a replacement ink batch or additional guidance.

Thank you for your patience and for choosing RC PRINT GI 790. We're here to help you get clear, vibrant prints again.

observed_output.text:
---

**Customer Support Chat Transcript**

**CUSTOMER**: Hi, I purchased the Amazon Basics Wireless Mouse, but I'm experiencing an issue with the OTG adapter. It's not working. Also, I'm a bit concerned about the mouse's battery life, as I've only had it for 2 months and the battery level is already quite low.

**SUPPORT REP**: Hello! Thank you for reaching out to us about the issues with your Amazon Basics Wireless Mouse. Sorry to hear that the OTG adapter isn't working as expected, and we'd also be happy to help you with your battery life concerns. Can you please confirm if you've tried using the OTG adapter with different devices to isolate if the issue is device-specific or with the adapter itself?

**CUSTOMER**: Yes, I've tried it with both my laptop and desktop, but it just doesn't seem to work. As for the battery, I've been using it daily for about 2 months now, and I'm already seeing a low battery warning. I thought it was supposed to last up to 12 months?

**SUPPORT REP**: Thank you for providing that information. For the OTG adapter, it's possible that it might be defective. We'd be happy to replace it for you. Regarding the battery life, 2 months of daily use is indeed shorter than expected. A few questions to help us better understand: Are you using the Smart Sleep mode and the on/off switch regularly to conserve power? Also, have you checked if the battery type used is the recommended 1-AA alkaline battery?

**CUSTOMER**: Honestly, I wasn't aware of the Smart Sleep mode and on/off switch being for power conservation. I've been using the mouse continuously without turning it off. As for the battery, I used the one that came with the mouse.

**SUPPORT REP**: That's completely understandable, and it's great you're open to adjusting your usage. To extend your battery life, please start utilizing the Smart Sleep mode and the on/off switch when not in use. This should significantly improve the battery's lifespan. For the OTG adapter, I'm going to go ahead and process a replacement for you. You should receive an email with the return and replacement instructions within the next 24 hours. 

**CUSTOMER**: That sounds great, thank you so much for the help! I'm looking forward to the replacement and will definitely use the power-saving features from now on.

**SUPPORT REP**: You're welcome! It was our pleasure to assist you. If you have any more questions or concerns in the future, don't hesitate to reach out. We're always here to help. Have a fantastic day, and enjoy your Amazon Basics Wireless Mouse!

**CUSTOMER**: Thank you again, you too!

**SUPPORT REP**: Take care! (Chat Ended) ---

```
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Milk Frother, Immersion Blender Cordless Foam Maker, but I'm a bit disappointed with a few aspects. I received a different variant than what's shown in the images, and the build quality isn't as expected. Also, there's no battery charging indicator to show how much battery is remaining.

SUPPORT REP: Hello! Thank you for reaching out to us about your concerns with the Milk Frother. Sorry to hear that the variant you received doesn't match the product images and that the build quality isn't meeting your expectations. Additionally, I understand the frustration with the lack of a battery charging indicator. Can you please provide me with your order number so I can look into this further for you?

CUSTOMER: My order number is #MF12345. Also, I noticed the speed adjustment buttons could be improved. It starts directly at full speed, and you can only reduce it. It would be more intuitive if it increased in speed as you press the button.

SUPPORT REP: Thank you for providing the order number, #MF12345. I've located your order and I'm going to go ahead and document the discrepancies you've mentioned, including the product variant and build quality concerns. Regarding the speed adjustment buttons, I completely understand your point. This is valuable feedback that I'll pass on to our product development team. As a temporary workaround, you might find it helpful to start with the lowest speed and then increase as needed, though I acknowledge this isn't the ideal solution you're looking for.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. What about the battery charging indicator? Is there a way to know how much charge is left without having to guess?

SUPPORT REP: I've checked on this for you, and currently, the model you have doesn't have a visual battery level indicator. However, based on customer feedback, we're working on integrating this feature into future updates. In the meantime, a general guideline is that a full charge can provide up to 12 frothing sessions, as mentioned in some of our customer reviews. If you're finding that your usage exceeds this and you're unsure about the charge level, you can always charge it for about 30 minutes to an hour to ensure it's topped up. Would you like me to provide a prepaid return label for the product variant issue, or would you prefer a discount on your next purchase as a gesture of goodwill?

CUSTOMER: I think a prepaid return label would be great, thank you. But before I return it, can I confirm if the new variant will have the improvements we discussed, especially the battery indicator?

SUPPORT REP: Excellent choice! I'll go ahead and process the prepaid return label for you, which you'll receive via email shortly. Regarding your question, while we can't guarantee immediate implementation of all suggested improvements in the next variant, I can assure you that your feedback, along with others, is being considered for future product enhancements. The battery charging indicator, in particular, is a feature we're actively exploring for inclusion in upcoming models. If you'd like, I can also offer you a 10% discount on your next purchase, which would include any new and improved versions of the Milk Frother that might be released in the future.

CUSTOMER: That sounds like a plan. Thank you for your help and for listening to my concerns. I look forward to the return label and the discount for my next purchase.

SUPPORT REP: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to assist you. Your satisfaction is our top priority, and I'm glad we could find a solution that works for you. The return label and discount code (MF10DISCOUNT) will be in your email inbox shortly. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out. Have a wonderful day, and thank you for choosing our products!

CUSTOMER: Thank you again, and I wish you a great day too!

SUPPORT REP: Likewise! Take care!
```

inputs.text:
Support Chat Transcript

CUSTOMER (yang wang, customer_id: chops): Hi, I’m having trouble with the Pigeon 1.5 litre Hot Kettle I purchased recently. It shuts off before the water properly boils.

SUPPORT REP (emp_0325): Hello yang, thanks for contacting Pigeon support. I understand the kettle is shutting off prematurely. Could you confirm if the auto shut-off activates as soon as the water starts to heat, or after a short period of boiling?

CUSTOMER: It switches off just when the water starts to steam lightly, well before a rolling boil.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Based on your description, it may be an overly sensitive thermostat or an issue with the heating element. Have you tried using it on a different power outlet to rule out any voltage fluctuation?

CUSTOMER: Yes, I tried two different outlets. Same behavior.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking. In that case, we’d like to arrange a replacement kettle for you. We’ll email you a return label and once the faulty unit is received at our service center, we’ll dispatch a replacement immediately.

CUSTOMER: That would be great. How long will the process take?

SUPPORT REP: After the courier picks up the kettle, replacement delivery usually takes 3–5 business days. We’ll also share a troubleshooting guide in case you face any similar issues in the future.

CUSTOMER: Perfect, thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, yang. If you have any other questions about the kettle or your order, feel free to reach out at any time.

Support (emp_0878): Thanks for contacting us. I understand how frustrating that can be. Could you confirm whether you’re using the inner pot when boiling and roughly how much water you fill it with?

Customer: I usually fill around 1 litre and sometimes use it without the inner pot for noodles.

Support (emp_0878): Understood. The auto‑shutoff might be triggered if the base isn’t seated properly or if there’s residue on the heating plate. Please try cleaning the base plate with a soft dry cloth and ensure the kettle is firmly placed on the stand. Also, avoid exceeding the max level marking.

Customer: Okay, I’ll try that. What about the hot handle area?

Support (emp_0878): Some warmth near the handle can occur, but it shouldn’t be uncomfortable. If it feels excessively hot, we can arrange an inspection or replacement under warranty. I’ll email you a checklist and a link to schedule a service visit.

Customer: That would be great, thank you.

Support (emp_0878): You’re welcome. Once you’ve tried these steps, reply to the email if the issue persists and we’ll prioritize a replacement.

inputs.product_name: Philips EasySpeed Plus Steam Iron GC2145/20-2200W, Quick Heat Up with up to 30 g/min steam, 110 g steam Boost, Scratch Resistant Ceramic Soleplate, Vertical steam & Drip-Stop
inputs.text:
Customer: Hello, I recently bought the Philips EasySpeed Plus Steam Iron GC2145/20. Overall it works fine, but I’ve noticed occasional dripping when ironing at lower temperatures.

Support (Monika Singh, emp_0379): Thank you for contacting us and for choosing the Philips EasySpeed Plus iron. Dripping at low temperatures can sometimes occur if the steam function is used below the recommended fabric settings. Could you confirm which fabric setting you’re using when you see the dripping?

Customer: It usually happens on the synthetic setting. I keep the steam on because I thought it would help smooth out light wrinkles.

Support: That helps, thank you. For synthetic fabrics, we recommend either reducing the steam intensity or turning off steam completely, as the soleplate temperature is intentionally lower and may not fully vaporize the water, leading to droplets. Please try ironing synthetics with steam off and then re‑enable steam only for cotton or linen.

Customer: Understood. I’ll try turning off steam for synthetics. Is there anything else I should do to avoid leaks?

Support: Yes, a couple of tips: (1) Always empty the water tank after use to prevent mineral buildup; (2) Allow the iron to pre‑heat for a minute after you set the temperature before enabling steam; and (3) Use filtered or distilled water if your tap water is very hard. These steps usually reduce or eliminate dripping.

Customer: That’s clear. If the issue continues even after following these steps, what are my options?

Support: If you still experience persistent leaking after trying these recommendations, please reach back out with your purchase details. We can help you with warranty support, including repair or replacement if needed. In the meantime, I’ll email you a short care‑and‑usage guide for this model.

Customer: Great, thank you for the detailed explanation and support.

Support: You’re welcome. We appreciate your feedback—proper use of the steam settings should improve your experience with the iron. Have a good day!

observed_output.review_content: I would not consider buying an i-phone simply because my friend owns two of them – or blindly go for a new Android model suggested by my son or nephew (both of whom are more tech savvy than me) because their recommendations are obviously based on their own needs and expectations, which may differ from mine. I am an old-fashioned mechanical engineer with a basic understanding of parameters like millimetres, megapixels and megabytes – but I think of a cellphone as a utility item, not a status symbol. Applying a technocratic approach, I would not choose a costlier option unless I get additional features which suit my requirements.My foremost requirement – which is entirely non-negotiable – is that my handset must have provision for two SIM cards, since I do not want to carry two separate handsets for my CUG and personal numbers. My other requirements are not difficult to fulfil: a phonebook with at least 2000 contacts, basic net connectivity, a basic camera for photos and videos and scope for downloading a few apps such as the ubiquitous WhatsApp and my favourite word games (which do not need much memory or processing capacity). I would certainly appreciate practical features like high reliability, software and security updates and high battery capacity (sufficient for 24 hours or preferably 48 hours at my normal level of usage). Besides, I would like to use a new handset for at least two years.Apart from exigencies, I do not intend to use my cellphone for surfing the Internet, videoconferencing or sending e-mails as I prefer using a desktop or laptop for such activities.I am equally clear about what I do not need. I do not intend to use my cellphone for watching movies, reading books, listening to music or creating fancy social media posts. Nor do I want a device for taking high resolution photos during a vacation as I would prefer to use a camera. At the risk of sounding flippant, I would say that I do not want a device to unlock my car or count the strokes in a game of golf – primarily because I do not own a car and I do not play golf!Having used smartphones of Samsung and Motorola makes over the past few years, I vastly prefer the former. My last phone, which gave me over 30 months of good service, was a Samsung M30. Since that model is obsolete now, I focused on its upgraded cousins: M32, M33 and M52. The last was immediately ruled out as it does not support two SIM cards along with an SD card. After studying the relative specifications of M32 and M33, I concluded that the latter offers better value for money. Generally, it is worth going for the higher memory and higher RAM versions as these parameters affect the performance and the difference in cost is relatively small. With these considerations, I narrowed down my choice to M33 with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage (Just twenty years ago, I was using a desktop with 2GB memory!)As a confirmation for my choice, I compared the phone I had selected with OnePlus Nord CE 2 (8GB RAM, 128GB Storage) which my son had recommended. The specification of the Samsung phone was found to be equivalent or superior for the major parameters, except that the display screen technology was TFT instead of AMOLED. I also watched some Youtube videos about these handsets for a better appreciation of their competing features. The clinching factor was that the Samsung phone was priced substantially lower than the OnePlus product.As for body colour, my first choice was Emerald Brown, but I settled for the Mystique Green since the former was not available in my selected configuration. I was thinking this would be irrelevant since I use a case which completely encloses the handset, but it turned out that the body colour can be glimpsed through the cutout for the cameras on the rear of the phone.Despite a strong family resemblance with my old one (M30), the new phone (M33) offers decidedly superior specifications and it meets my requirements perfectly. It is a few millimetres longer and a few grams heavier than my old phone, but these differences are acceptable to me. Thanks to the 50MP front camera and 8MP selfie camera, the quality of photos and videos is above my expectations (see sample pic taken at night at a distance of about 30 metres from the stage).  This phone offers two years of android updates and four years of security patch updates, which reduces the worries on these fronts. Youtube reviewers complain that the M33 has plain looks, it is heavy, its audio does not offer an ‘immersive listening experience’ and its screen is plain old TFT instead of AMOLED. I am willing to live with these perceived shortcomings, so long as the M33 meets my requirements.I was glad to find that Samsung has taken an environmentally friendly step of offering many models of handsets without chargers – because old chargers, like old handsets, add to e-waste. However, it needs to be kept in mind that new handsets require higher capacity chargers. The recommended charger for M33 is 25 watts, but the chargers I had at home are rated at 5 or 10 watts.To cut a long story short, I ordered a 25-watt charger along with the phone to avoid compromising with the charging time. After using the new handset for a couple of weeks, I find that my phone is at 60-70% charge at the end of the day, and it takes 30-40 minutes for complete charging (one of the useful features of M33 is that it shows the time remaining for complete charging as soon as it is plugged in for charging). It turns out that I could have managed with the old 10-watt charger, except that it would have taken 60-90 minutes for full charging.I conclude by emphasizing that Samsung Galaxy M33 5g is the perfect phone – but for my requirements. observed_output.review_content: I would not consider buying an i-phone simply because my friend owns two of them – or blindly go for a new Android model suggested by my son or nephew (both of whom are more tech savvy than me) because their recommendations are obviously based on their own needs and expectations, which may differ from mine. My other requirements are not difficult to fulfil: a phonebook with at least 2000 contacts, basic net connectivity, a basic camera for photos and videos and scope for downloading a few apps such as the ubiquitous WhatsApp and my favourite word games (which do not need much memory or processing capacity). I would certainly appreciate practical features like high reliability, software and security updates and high battery capacity (sufficient for 24 hours or preferably 48 hours at my normal level of usage). Besides, I would like to use a new handset for at least two years.Apart from exigencies, I do not intend to use my cellphone for surfing the Internet, videoconferencing or sending e-mails as I prefer using a desktop or laptop for such activities.I am equally clear about what I do not need. I do not intend to use my cellphone for watching movies, reading books, listening to music or creating fancy social media posts. Nor do I want a device for taking high resolution photos during a vacation as I would prefer to use a camera. inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I recently purchased the Aquaguard Aura RO+UV+UF+Taste Adjuster water purifier. The unit works well overall, but I’m confused about the taste adjuster settings and I’m not sure if the Active Copper feature is enabled correctly.

Support Rep (Bhupinder Kapoor - emp_0944): Thank you for reaching out, Jaime. I’m glad to hear the purifier is working well. I can help clarify both the taste adjuster and Active Copper features. First, could you confirm whether you’ve set the source water type (borewell, tanker, or municipal) on the MTDS controller?

Customer: I haven’t changed any setting yet; we primarily use municipal water. I also noticed that sometimes the taste varies slightly from day to day.

Support Rep: Understood. For municipal water, we recommend starting with the default MTDS setting and then slowly increasing it one step at a time until you reach a taste you prefer. Small day‑to‑day variations can occur based on the input water quality. Regarding Active Copper, when the purifier is powered on and dispensing, copper ions are automatically infused, so there’s no separate switch to toggle. If you ever feel the taste is too strong or too mild, you can fine‑tune using the MTDS controller.

Customer: That helps. Is there anything I should watch for in terms of maintenance that might affect taste or copper levels?

Support Rep: Yes. Please ensure cartridges are replaced as per the service alerts, and periodically check the pre‑filter for clogging. If you notice a sudden change in taste or flow rate, it’s often a sign that filters need servicing. You’ll also see LED indications when service is due. If the issue persists after adjusting MTDS and basic cleaning, we can arrange a technician visit.

Customer: Great, I’ll follow these steps. Could you email me a short guide on recommended settings for municipal water?

Support Rep: Absolutely. I’ll send you a quick reference guide with recommended MTDS ranges and maintenance tips for municipal water. If you have any further questions, feel free to contact us again.

Customer: Thanks for the detailed explanation and support.

Support Rep: You’re welcome, Jaime. Enjoy your purified water, and have a great day.

inputs.product_name: boAt Type C A750 Stress Resistant, Tangle-free, Sturdy Flat Cable with 6.5A Fast Charging
inputs.text:
Customer: Hello, I recently purchased the boAt Type C A750 cable. While the charging speed is great, I'm a bit confused about whether it's safe to use with my older power bank and laptop USB ports.

Support (emp_0143 – Finance Manager assisting with policy clarification): Thank you for reaching out and for choosing the boAt Type C A750 cable. I can help clarify usage guidelines and warranty implications. Could you share the output rating (voltage and amperage) listed on your power bank and laptop USB ports?

Customer: The power bank says 5V/2A, and my laptop USB ports are standard USB 3.0.

Support: Great, thanks for the details. The A750 cable supports up to 6.5A fast charging, but it will only draw as much current as your device and charger safely support. Using it with a 5V/2A power bank and USB 3.0 laptop ports is safe; you just won’t get the maximum 6.5A fast-charging performance—charging will occur at your charger’s supported rate.

Customer: That makes sense. Is there anything I should avoid to prevent damage?

Support: To keep everything safe and within warranty, we recommend: (1) Using BIS-certified or manufacturer-recommended chargers; (2) Avoiding visibly damaged adapters or ports; (3) Not sharply bending or pinching the flat cable near the connectors despite its stress-resistant design; and (4) Ensuring the cable is kept away from moisture and high heat sources. The product is designed for 10000+ bends, but careful use will extend its life further.

Customer: Understood. What’s the warranty coverage if something goes wrong?

Support: The boAt Type C A750 cable typically comes with a 2-year warranty from the date of purchase, covering manufacturing defects like connector failure, internal breakage not caused by misuse, or issues with data transfer under normal usage. Physical damage due to cuts, burns, or improper handling is usually not covered. Please retain your invoice, as it will be required for any claim.

Customer: Thanks, that clears things up. I’ll keep the invoice and follow these guidelines.

Support: You’re welcome. If you notice any intermittent charging, data sync issues, or visible wear, please contact us with your purchase details and we’ll guide you through the replacement or claim process. Have a great day and enjoy the hassle-free charging experience with your A750 cable.

@@ -1,31 +1,228 @@

-  # Removed 'with self.assertRaises(KeyError):'

-
-  # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
-  lru_dict.touch(1)
-  self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
-
-  # Touch fails on missing key.
-  with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
-    lru_dict.touch(22)+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# Copyright 2013 The Swarming Authors. All rights reserved.
+# Use of this source code is governed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 that
+# can be found in the LICENSE file.
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+sys.path.insert(0, ROOT_DIR)
+
+from utils import lru
+
+
+class LRUDictTest(unittest.TestCase):
+  @staticmethod
+  def prepare_lru_dict(keys):
+    """Returns new LRUDict with given |keys| added one by one."""
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    for key in keys:
+      lru_dict.add(key, None)
+    return lru_dict
+
+  def assert_order(self, lru_dict, expected_keys):
+    """Asserts order of keys in |lru_dict| is |expected_keys|.
+
+    expected_keys[0] is supposedly oldest key, expected_keys[-1] is newest.
+
+    Destroys |lru_dict| state in the process.
+    """
+    # Check keys iteration works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(expected_keys))
+
+    # Check pop_oldest returns keys in expected order.
+    actual_keys = []
+    while lru_dict:
+      oldest_key, _ = lru_dict.pop_oldest()
+      actual_keys.append(oldest_key)
+    self.assertEqual(actual_keys, expected_keys)
+
+  def assert_same_data(self, lru_dict, regular_dict):
+    """Asserts that given |lru_dict| contains same data as |regular_dict|."""
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.keys_set(), set(regular_dict.keys()))
+    self.assertEqual(set(lru_dict.itervalues()), set(regular_dict.values()))
+
+    for k, v in regular_dict.items():
+      self.assertEqual(lru_dict.get(k), v)
+
+  def test_basic_dict_funcs(self):
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+
+    # Add a bunch.
+    data = {1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three'}
+    for k, v in data.items():
+      lru_dict.add(k, v)
+    # Check its there.
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Replace value.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one!!!')
+    data[1] = 'one!!!'
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Check pop works.
+    self.assertEqual(lru_dict.pop(2), 'two')
+    data.pop(2)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Pop missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.pop(2)
+
+    # Touch has no effect on set of keys and values.
+    lru_dict.touch(1)
+    self.assert_same_data(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch fails on missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
+      lru_dict.touch(22)
+
+  def test_magic_methods(self):
+    # Check __nonzero__, __len__ and __contains__ for empty dict.
+    lru_dict = lru.LRUDict()
+    self.assertFalse(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 0)
+    self.assertFalse(1 in lru_dict)
+
+    # Dict with one item.
+    lru_dict.add(1, 'one')
+    self.assertTrue(lru_dict)
+    self.assertEqual(len(lru_dict), 1)
+    self.assertTrue(1 in lru_dict)
+    self.assertFalse(2 in lru_dict)
+
+  def test_order(self):
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge cases.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([]), [])
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict([1]), [1])
+
+    # No touches.
+    self.assert_order(self.prepare_lru_dict(data), data)
+
+    # Touching newest item is noop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # Touch to move to newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # Pop newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(1)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [2, 3])
+
+    # Pop in the middle.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # Pop oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(3)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 2])
+
+    # Add oldest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(4, 4), (5, 5)])
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [4, 5] + data)
+
+    # Add newest.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data + [4])
+
+  def test_load_save(self):
+    def save_and_load(lru_dict):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        lru_dict.save(tmp_name)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        try:
+          os.unlink(tmp_name)
+        except OSError:
+          pass
+
+    data = [1, 2, 3]
+
+    # Edge case.
+    empty = save_and_load(lru.LRUDict())
+    self.assertFalse(empty)
+
+    # Normal flow.
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(self.prepare_lru_dict(data))
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, data)
+
+    # After touches.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.touch(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3, 2])
+
+    # After pop.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.pop(2)
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [1, 3])
+
+    # After add.
+    lru_dict = self.prepare_lru_dict(data)
+    lru_dict.add(4, 4)
+    lru_dict.batch_insert_oldest([(5, 5), (6, 6)])
+    lru_dict = save_and_load(lru_dict)
+    self.assert_order(lru_dict, [5, 6] + data + [4])
+
+  def test_corrupted_state_file(self):
+    def load_from_state(state_text):
+      handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=u'lru_test')
+      os.close(handle)
+      try:
+        with open(tmp_name, 'w') as f:
+          f.write(state_text)
+        return lru.LRUDict.load(tmp_name)
+      finally:
+        os.unlink(tmp_name)
+
+    # Loads correct state just fine.
+    self.assertIsNotNone(load_from_state(json.dumps([
+        ['key1', 'value1'],
+        ['key2', 'value2'],
+    ])))
+
+    # Not a json.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('garbage, not a state')
+
+    # Not a list.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state('{}')
+
+    # Not a list of pairs.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value', 'and whats this?'],
+      ]))
+
+    # Duplicate keys.
+    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+      load_from_state(json.dumps([
+          ['key', 'value'],
+          ['key', 'another_value'],
+      ]))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+  VERBOSE = '-v' in sys.argv
+  logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG if VERBOSE else logging.ERROR)
+  unittest.main()

+    # Pop missing key.
+    with self.assertRaises(KeyError):

inputs.product_name: Bajaj DX-7 1000W Dry Iron with Advance Soleplate and Anti-bacterial German Coating Technology, White
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Bajaj DX-7 dry iron from your online store. Overall it works, but I'm worried about how it handles delicate fabrics like silk and chiffon.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Hello, thank you for contacting support and for choosing the Bajaj DX-7. I understand your concern about using the iron safely on delicate materials. Could you let me know if you've tried the lower temperature settings and whether the iron seems to get too hot even on those levels?

CUSTOMER: Yes, even on the lower setting, I'm nervous that it might scorch the fabric. I previously used another brand that had clearer guidance for each fabric type.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): That makes sense. This model uses a standard temperature dial, but you can safely use it on delicate fabrics by pre‑testing on a small, hidden section and always starting at the lowest setting. For very delicate items, we recommend using a thin pressing cloth between the iron and the fabric to avoid direct contact. I can also send you a concise fabric‑specific temperature guide for this product.

CUSTOMER: A guide and the pressing cloth tip would be really helpful. I'm also curious about maintenance—how should I clean the soleplate without damaging the anti‑bacterial coating?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Great question. To clean the soleplate, first unplug the iron and let it cool down completely. Then use a soft, slightly damp cloth with mild soap—avoid abrasive cleaners or metal scrubbers so the coating stays intact. Wipe it dry thoroughly before the next use. I’ll email you the fabric guide and a short care checklist so you have everything in one place.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that answers my questions.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): You’re welcome. If you still feel uncertain after trying these tips, please reach out again and we can review alternative models better suited for frequent delicate‑fabric use. Have a great day!

inputs.product_name: Bajaj DX-7 1000W Dry Iron with Advance Soleplate and Anti-bacterial German Coating Technology, White
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Bajaj DX-7 dry iron from your online store. Overall it works, but I'm worried about how it handles delicate fabrics like silk and chiffon.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Hello, thank you for contacting support and for choosing the Bajaj DX-7. I understand your concern about using the iron safely on delicate materials. Could you let me know if you've tried the lower temperature settings and whether the iron seems to get too hot even on those levels?

CUSTOMER: Yes, even on the lower setting, I'm nervous that it might scorch the fabric. I previously used another brand that had clearer guidance for each fabric type.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): That makes sense. This model uses a standard temperature dial, but you can safely use it on delicate fabrics by pre‑testing on a small, hidden section and always starting at the lowest setting. For very delicate items, we recommend using a thin pressing cloth between the iron and the fabric to avoid direct contact. I can also send you a concise fabric‑specific temperature guide for this product.

CUSTOMER: A guide and the pressing cloth tip would be really helpful. I'm also curious about maintenance—how should I clean the soleplate without damaging the anti‑bacterial coating?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Great question. To clean the soleplate, first unplug the iron and let it cool down completely. Then use a soft, slightly damp cloth with mild soap—avoid abrasive cleaners or metal scrubbers so the coating stays intact. Wipe it dry thoroughly before the next use. I’ll email you the fabric guide and a short care checklist so you have everything in one place.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that answers my questions.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): You’re welcome. If you still feel uncertain after trying these tips, please reach out again and we can review alternative models better suited for frequent delicate‑fabric use. Have a great day!

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Lifelong LLSM120G sandwich griller. Overall it heats quickly and works fine, but I have a couple of concerns.

SUPPORT REP (Ray Williams - emp_0528): Thanks for reaching out, Philip. I’m happy to help. Could you describe the issues you’re facing in a bit more detail?

CUSTOMER: Sure. First, the power cord length is very short, so I’m struggling to place it conveniently on my kitchen counter. Second, I notice that the outer body gets quite warm after a few minutes of use, and I’m worried about safety.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Regarding the cord length, this model ships with a compact cord to reduce tangling and storage issues, but I realise that can be inconvenient. A practical workaround is to use a heavy‑duty, grounded extension cord rated for kitchen appliances, placed away from water sources. For the warm outer body: some heating is expected due to the 750W elements, but the unit is designed with heat‑resistant housing.

SUPPORT REP: Could you tell me whether you’re using it continuously for long sessions or mostly for quick sandwiches, and whether it’s placed near a wall or other objects?

CUSTOMER: Mostly quick sandwiches, but it is close to the backsplash on the counter.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks, that helps. I recommend leaving a few inches of clearance around the unit to let heat dissipate, and avoiding covering the vents. Also, always keep the handle and base dry and use heat‑proof gloves if needed. If the housing feels excessively hot (too hot to touch briefly), please stop using the device and share a short video or photos so we can assess a potential defect.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll adjust the placement and try with an extension cord. If it still seems unsafe, I’ll contact you again.

SUPPORT REP: That sounds good. I’ve logged your feedback about cord length and perceived heating so our product team can review it for future revisions. If you experience any burning smell, discoloration, or visible damage, stop using the griller and reach out immediately so we can help with inspection or replacement options.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Philip. If you have more questions about safe usage or warranty coverage, I’m here to help.

+def getEmailAddress(vcard):
+	"""
+	Get email address.
+	Supported formats:
+		- email;something
+		- email;type=something
+	something := (internet,work,home, other)
+	"""
+	
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'email':
+				list = vcard[key]
+				return list[0]
+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'email':
+				list = vcard[key]
+				return list[0]
+	
+	return ""
+
+def findName(vcard):
+	"""
+	Find a version 3.0 name
+	"""
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+	
+	return None
+
+################################################################################
+##  reads a vcard and stores as hash pairs key/value where value is a list    ##
+################################################################################
+
+def readVCARD (buffer) :
+
+	"""
+
+	skips fom <file> until a 'begin' tag from VCARD is encountered.
+	from this point starts constructing a map (key, [values] ) 
+	VCARD entry format -> tag:value 
+	
+		key <- tag
+		[values] <- list with the values of <tag> if there are more tags with the same name
+
+	"""
+	r=' '
+	bgn,end = -1, -1;
+	d = dict()
+	while r and bgn < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		if len (r)  == 0 : return dict()
+		if string.find('begin',string.lower(string.strip(r))) :
+			bgn = 1
+	while r and end < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		s = string.split(string.lower(string.strip(r)),':')
+ 		if s[0] <> '' :
+			if d.has_key(s[0]) :
+				d[s[0]].append(s[1])
+			elif len(s) > 1:
+				d[s[0]] = [s[1]]	
+			else :
+				d[s[0]] = ['']
+			if s[0] == 'end' : end = 1	
+	return d
+
+##################################################################################
+
+###############################################################################################
+## writes on a given file an xml representation for claws-mail addressbook received as a hash  ##
+###############################################################################################
+
+def writeXMLREPR (vcard,file,uid) :
+
+	"""
+	based on <vcard> and <uid> writes only recognized tags (the ones defined in <keywds> list)
+	NOTE: <url> and <org> tag will be written as attributes (there are such tags in claws-mail's
+	      XML schema)
+	"""
+	if len (vcard.keys()) == 0 : return
+	item = vcard.get(keywds[2]);
+	if item:
+		name = string.split(item[0],';')
+	else:
+		""" version 3.0 n ?"""
+		name = findName(vcard)
+		if not name:
+			return
+
+	fn, ln, nick, cn, a = '', '', '', '', ''
+
+	if len(name) >= 2 :
+		fn = name[0]
+		ln = name[1]
+	elif len(name) ==1 :
+		fn = name[0]
+	
+	if vcard.has_key(keywds[4]) :
+		nick = vcard.get(keywds[4])[0]
+	if len(vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]) :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]
+	else :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[0])[0];
+
+	a += str('\n<person uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" first-name=\"' + fn + '\" last-name=\"' + ln
+		+ '\" nick-name=\"' + nick + '\" cn=\"' + cn + '\" >\n')
+	a += '\t<address-list>\n'
+	if vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+		for c in vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+			uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+			a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' + nick  + '\" email=\"' + c + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	else :
+		email = getEmailAddress(vcard)
+		uid[0] = uid[0]+1
+		a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' +  nick + '\" email=\"' + email + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	a += '\t</address-list>\n'
+	a += '\t<attribute-list>\n'
+	for key in keywds[5:] :
+		if vcard.get(key) :
+        	        for c in vcard.get(key) :
+        	       	        uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+	                       	a += '\t\t<attribute uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" name=\"' + key +'\">'+c+'</attribute>\n'
+	a += '\t</attribute-list>\n'
+	a += '</person>\n'
+	file.write(a)
+	file.flush()
+		
+###################################################################################################
+
+def convert (in_f, o_f, name='INBOX') :
+	d = {'d':1}
+	uid = [int(time.time())]
+	
+	try :
+		print 'proccessing...\n'
+		o_f.write('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1" ?>\n<address-book name="'+name+'" >\n');
+		
+		buf = normalizeLongLines(in_f)
+		buffer = StringIO.StringIO(buf)
+		while len(d.keys()) > 0 :
+			d = readVCARD(buffer)
+			writeXMLREPR (d, o_f, uid)
+			uid[0] = uid [0]+1
+		
+		o_f.write('\n</address-book>')
+		print 'finished processing...\n'
+	except IOError, err :
+		print 'Caught an IOError : ',err,'\t ABORTING!!!'
+		raise err
+
+#################################################################################################
+
+def execute () :
+	if len(sys.argv) <> 3 and len(sys.argv) <> 2 :
+		print str("\nUsage: vcard2xml.py  source_file [destination_file]\n\n" +
+		'\tWhen only <source_file> is specified will overwrite the existing addressbook.\n'+
+		'\tWhen both arguments are suplied will create a new additional addressbook named \n\tas the destination file.'+'\n\tNOTE: in both cases the Claws Mail must be closed and ran at least once.\n\n')
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	in_file = None
+	out_file = None
+	path_to_out = os.environ['HOME']+'/.claws-mail/'
+	adr_idx = 'addrbook--index.xml'
+	adr_idx_file = None
+	tmp_adr_idx_file= None
+	got_ex = 0
+
+	try :
+		in_file = open(sys.argv[1])
+	except IOError, e:
+		print 'Could not open input file <',sys.argv[1],'>  ABORTING'
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+		try :
+			dlist = os.listdir(path_to_out);
+			flist=[]
+			for l in dlist :
+				if l.find('addrbook') == 0 and l.find("addrbook--index.xml") < 0 and l.find('bak') < 0 :
+					flist.append(l)
+			flist.sort()
+			out_file = flist.pop()
+			os.rename(path_to_out+out_file, path_to_out+out_file+'.tmp')
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+out_file,'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file)
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	else :
+		try :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx, path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			tmp_adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx,'w')
+		except Exception, e :
+			print 'Could not open <', path_to_out+adr_idx,'> file. Make sure you started Claws Mail at least once.'
+			sys.exit(1)
+		try :
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+sys.argv[2],'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file, sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0])
+			l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+			while l :
+				if l.strip() == '</book_list>' :
+					adr_idx_file.write('\t<book name="'+sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0] +'" file="'+sys.argv[2]+'" />\n')
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				else :
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	
+
+	if got_ex :
+		#clean up the mess
+		print 'got exception, cleaning up the mess... changed files will be restored...\n'
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if out_file :
+			out_file.close()
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name)
+		else :
+			os.remove(out_file.name)
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp', path_to_out+adr_idx)
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+				
+	else :
+		#closing all and moving temporary data into place
+		print 'closing open files...\n'
+		in_file.close()
+		out_file.close()	
+		if len(sys.argv) == 3 :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp',path_to_out+adr_idx+'.bak' )
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name+'.bak')
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+		print 'done!'
+		
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    execute ()
+
+

inputs.product_name: Acer 139 cm (55 inches) I Series 4K Ultra HD Android Smart LED TV AR55AR2851UDFL (Black)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Acer 139 cm (55 inches) I Series 4K Ultra HD Android Smart LED TV, and overall the picture quality is great. However, I’m noticing that when I connect my Bestor 8K HDMI 2.1 cable to my laptop, the TV sometimes flickers and briefly loses signal.

SUPPORT REP (Mukesh Kapoor, HR Associate assisting via routed support line): Thank you for reaching out and for choosing our Acer I Series TV. I’m sorry about the flickering issue you’re experiencing when using the Bestor 8K HDMI cable. Let’s run through a few checks to narrow this down.

SUPPORT REP: First, can you confirm the HDMI port you’re using on the TV (e.g., HDMI 1 or HDMI 2) and whether the flicker happens on all apps or only when using the laptop input?

CUSTOMER: I’m using HDMI 1, and the flicker only happens when I use my laptop as the source. OTT apps running directly on the TV work fine.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful. Please try the following:
1) Switch the cable to HDMI 2 on the TV and check if the flicker persists.
2) On your laptop, ensure the output resolution is set to 4K at 60Hz instead of trying to push 8K, as the TV panel is 4K.
3) If possible, test with a different HDMI cable to rule out a cable defect.

CUSTOMER: I changed to HDMI 2 and set my laptop to 4K 60Hz. The flicker is reduced but still happens occasionally.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Next steps:
- On the TV, go to Settings > Picture > Advanced and disable any HDMI-CEC or input auto-switching features.
- Ensure the TV’s software is updated to the latest version under Settings > About > System Update.
If the issue continues after these changes, we can arrange a technician visit to check the HDMI ports and internal board.

CUSTOMER: I’ve updated the TV and disabled HDMI-CEC. The connection now seems stable.

SUPPORT REP: That’s great to hear. I’ll document this interaction under your customer profile and note that the issue was resolved through configuration changes. If the flicker returns or you notice any new symptoms, please contact us and we’ll escalate to a field technician.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome. Enjoy your Acer I Series TV, and feel free to reach out if you need anything else.

instruction:
Employee_id: emp_0803
Please update sales record 10484 for customer annette roulet (customer ID oldwo) to reflect her purchase on 2012-06-15 of the Zoul USB C Backup Cable for External Drives (product ID B00SMJPA9C). The record should show the actual price ₹940, discounted price ₹499 with a 47% discount, a product rating of 4.3 based on 187 ratings, categorize this purchase under FOLLOW-UP, and include the product description as a high-speed USB-C cable for external hard drives and SSDs optimized for consistent data transfer and durable daily use, along with the product link https://shop.inazuma.com/products/B00SMJPA9C. Also create a logged customer support interaction with chat ID 752 for this same product and customer, handled by employee emp_0803, using the following full conversation text as the interaction content, dated 2016-07-05:

"CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently bought the Zoul USB C Backup Cable for External Drives that I used with my latest order. The transfer speed is good, but the connector feels a bit loose on one of my external SSDs and sometimes disconnects if the cable is nudged.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal Ranjan): Thanks for reaching out and for purchasing the Zoul USB C Backup Cable. Let me help you troubleshoot this. Could you confirm which brand/model of SSD you’re using and whether the issue occurs on multiple USB-C ports or only a specific one?

CUSTOMER: I’m using a 1TB Samsung T7 and I’ve tested it on two USB-C ports on my laptop. The issue seems slightly better on one port, but I still get random disconnects if the cable moves.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Understood. This might be a seating tolerance issue between the connector and that drive’s port. Please try gently reinserting the connector until you hear/feel a firm click and check that there’s no dust or debris in the SSD port. Also test the cable with another USB-C device, such as a phone or different drive, to see if the behavior is consistent.

CUSTOMER: I tested with my phone and another smaller SSD. The connection is stable there. The issue is mostly with the Samsung T7.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Thanks for testing that. Since the cable works reliably with other devices, this points to a minor fit variance with that specific drive. As a workaround, avoid bending the cable sharply near the connector and use a short strain-relief loop so the connector isn’t under tension. If you’re still unhappy with the connection stability, we can either arrange a replacement cable from a different batch or offer a partial refund on this purchase.

CUSTOMER: I’d prefer a replacement from another batch to see if that improves the fit.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Absolutely, I will initiate a replacement request right away and you’ll receive confirmation by email shortly. The new cable should arrive within a few business days. If the replacement still gives you trouble, contact us again and we’ll explore a refund option.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Thanks for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): You’re welcome. We appreciate your business and feedback—it helps us improve future batches. Have a great day!"

inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I'm having intermittent tracking issues with my Lenovo 130 Wireless Compact Mouse B099SD8PRP. The cursor occasionally lags or jumps, especially when I'm switching quickly between spreadsheets and browser tabs.

Support (Alok Mathur, emp_0883): Thanks for contacting support, Manuel. I understand you’re seeing lag and jumpy cursor behavior with the mouse. Let me ask a couple of quick questions: does this occur only on a particular surface (e.g., glossy desk, glass, or fabric mousepad), and are you using the original Nano USB receiver directly in the laptop/PC, or through a hub or docking station?

Customer: I’m using it on a wooden desk without a mousepad, and the Nano receiver is plugged into a USB hub connected to my laptop.

Support: That’s helpful, thank you. The 1000 DPI optical sensor in this model can become less accurate on certain surfaces and when the wireless signal is slightly degraded. Let’s try three steps: (1) plug the Nano USB receiver directly into the laptop’s USB port instead of the hub; (2) move any nearby wireless devices (Wi‑Fi router, external drives) away from the receiver by at least 20–30 cm; and (3) test the mouse on a non‑reflective mousepad or sheet of paper to see if tracking stabilizes.

Customer: I switched the receiver to the laptop and tried the mouse on a mousepad. The cursor is much smoother now, but I’d still like slightly higher precision when editing images.

Support: Great, that confirms it was a combination of surface and wireless interference. For finer control, you can reduce pointer speed in your OS settings so the 1000 DPI sensor feels more precise. Also make sure no other wireless mouse or keyboard is sharing the same USB hub. If you’d like, I can also share our recommended accessory list for this mouse (mousepads and USB extenders) via email.

Customer: Yes, please send that over. Thanks for the help.

Support: You’re welcome, Manuel. I’ll email the accessory recommendations and a short troubleshooting checklist for future reference. If you run into any more issues with B099SD8PRP, just reply to that email or reopen a support chat.

Customer: Hi, I bought the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Kettle recently. It heats water fast, but I’ve noticed a slight plastic smell during boiling even after several uses. Is this normal, and how can I get rid of it?

Support (emp_0680): Hello Guillermo, thank you for reaching out and for choosing the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Electric Kettle. A mild odor can sometimes occur with new appliances due to manufacturing residues, but it should reduce over time. Let’s try a deep-clean cycle: fill the kettle to the max line with a 50/50 mix of water and white vinegar, bring it to a boil, then let it sit for 20 minutes before discarding. Rinse and boil plain water 2–3 times afterwards.

Customer: I’ve tried boiling water a few times, but not with vinegar. Is it safe for the stainless steel interior?

Support (emp_0680): Yes, using a diluted white vinegar solution in the proportions mentioned is safe for the stainless steel interior and is a common descaling/odor-removal method. Just avoid abrasive scrubbers on the inner surface. If the smell persists after two cleaning cycles, please let us know so we can review warranty options or arrange an inspection.

Customer: Great, I’ll try that today. If the issue continues, how do I contact you for a possible replacement?

Support (emp_0680): You can reach us through this support channel using your customer ID "peric" or via the purchase invoice you received from Inazuma. Keep the product serial number and your purchase date handy so we can quickly validate the warranty and, if needed, initiate a replacement request.

Please update the existing engineering issue in the sunlianqiang/kbengine repository with the title "Refine PyPIRC old-format test expectations and clarify legacy behavior" and internal reference ID 76235b1e-3267-42c8-adc4-b9cbcec358b6 so that it reflects Rajesh Singh’s recommendation. inputs.title: Refine PyPIRC old-format test expectations and clarify legacy behavior
inputs.description: Rajesh Singh (emp_1098), a Software Engineering Team Lead at Inazuma.co, recommends improving the PyPIRC legacy configuration test by making the expectations more explicit and documenting the differences between the new and old .pypirc formats. This helps future maintainers understand why the old-format behavior is still tested and how it aligns with current distribution tooling practices.
inputs.patch:
--- kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
+++ kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
@@ -96,7 +96,15 @@
-        # old format
-        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
-        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
-        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
-                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
-        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+        # old format
+        # In the legacy format, only a single section is defined and
+        # PyPIRCCommand is expected to infer the default repository
+        # settings based on that server-login section.
+        #
+        # This ensures that existing projects depending on the old
+        # configuration style continue to work even as newer index
+        # server layouts are introduced.
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
+        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
+                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
+                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
+        self.assertEqual(config, waited)

-    # 2. handle the old format
+"""Tests for distutils.pypirc.pypirc."""
+import sys
+import os
+import unittest
+import tempfile
 
-    # new format
