instruction:
Employee ID emp_0812:
Please record a new customer support chat under chat reference 861 for customer Christina Berglund (customer ID bergs) regarding her device Redmi 10A (Slate Grey, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, product ID B09XB7SRQ5). The chat should capture the following full conversation that took place on November 12, 2018:

"CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Redmi 10A and I’m facing frequent app freezes and occasional reboots, especially when using the camera and switching between apps quickly. Can you help?

SUPPORT REP (Jonathan Sinclair, Business Development): Thanks for reaching out, Christina. I’m sorry to hear about the issues you’re experiencing with your Redmi 10A. To assist you better, could you confirm whether all system and app updates have been installed, and whether you’ve recently added any new apps just before the freezes began?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the phone says it’s up to date. I did install a couple of games last week, but the freezing happens even when I’m just using the camera or WhatsApp.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Let’s try a couple of troubleshooting steps. First, please clear the cache for the camera and messaging apps from Settings > Apps. Next, try restarting the device in safe mode to see if the issue persists without third‑party apps running. If the phone is still freezing in safe mode, it may indicate a deeper system or hardware issue.

CUSTOMER: I tried safe mode and it still froze once when I opened the camera.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking that. Since the problem persists in safe mode, I’d like to register this as a service case and arrange a diagnostic at our authorized service center. The technicians can run hardware checks on the memory and storage and, if needed, re‑flash the software. If a defect is confirmed, you’ll be eligible for a repair or replacement as per warranty terms.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Please proceed.

SUPPORT REP: I’ve created a service request tied to your customer profile and purchase record. You’ll receive an email shortly with the case number, service center details near your location, and instructions on backing up your data before handing over the device. If you notice any new symptoms or error messages, please include them when you visit the center so we have a complete picture.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the clear explanation and next steps.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Christina. We appreciate your patience and will do our best to resolve this quickly. If you have any questions or need to reschedule your appointment, feel free to reply to the email or contact our support line."

input_bindings.subject: Automation Proposal: Linking IT Ticket 30590 with Email and CRM Workflows
input_bindings.body:
Hi Nicole,

I’m reaching out from the engineering team regarding your earlier issue with the locked email account (IT Ticket 30590). Beyond the immediate fix that Nishant implemented, we’re working on improving how IT tickets, email threads, and customer-support chats connect behind the scenes.

Specifically, I’m proposing a small pilot where your future email access incidents are automatically associated with a unified thread ID, so that:
- IT can see related email messages directly within the ticket view,
- Customer-support representatives can reference the same thread when assisting your clients,
- We can better audit and prevent repeat lockout patterns.

This email has been attached to Ticket 30590 as a starting point for that unified thread. If you’re comfortable participating, I’d appreciate any feedback on what kind of status updates or alerts you’d like to receive when access issues occur (e.g., automatic notifications, escalation rules, or integration with your sales dashboards).

Thanks for your time, and for helping us make our internal tooling more reliable for the Sales team.

Best regards,
Rahul

Software Engineer, Support Tooling (EN12)
Inazuma.co

After sending an automation proposal regarding IT ticket-email-CRM linkage, I'm now unable to access the internal workflow orchestration dashboard used to monitor ticket routing rules. input_bindings.Resolution: Hi Rahul, thanks for reporting the issue with the workflow orchestration dashboard. We identified that the backend service responsible for ticket-email-CRM synchronization had an overloaded worker queue and one of the API gateway routes was misconfigured, leading to intermittent 503 errors on the UI. inputs.product_name: Fire-Boltt Tank 1.85" Bluetooth Calling Smart Watch, 123 Sports Mode, 8 UI Interactions, Built in Speaker & Mic, 7 Days Battery & Fire-Boltt Health Suite
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Fire-Boltt Tank 1.85" smartwatch. The health tracking features are useful, but I'm facing issues with Bluetooth calling—calls keep dropping after a few minutes.

SUPPORT REP (Abhinav Sharma - HR Associate assisting via support desk): Thank you for reaching out, Hari. I'm sorry to hear about the call drops. Let me help troubleshoot this. Could you confirm the phone model you are pairing with the watch and whether you have granted all Bluetooth and notification permissions?

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Samsung Galaxy A52. I’ve enabled Bluetooth and notifications, but I’m not sure about all the app permissions.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Please open the Fire-Boltt app, go to Settings > Permissions, and ensure Bluetooth, Phone, and Notifications are all allowed. Also, disable battery optimization for the app in your phone settings, as that can interrupt connections. After making these changes, try a test call.

CUSTOMER: I’ve updated the permissions and disabled battery optimization. The test call lasted longer, but it still disconnected once.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking. As a next step, please unpair and re-pair the watch, then restart both your phone and the smartwatch. If the issue continues, we can log a case for a potential firmware update or replacement, depending on diagnostics results.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll try that. If it still fails, I’d prefer a replacement device.

SUPPORT REP: That’s completely fair. I’ve noted your preference for a replacement if reconnection steps don’t resolve the issue. You’ll receive a follow-up email with instructions and a reference number for this case. Thank you for your patience and for choosing this smartwatch.

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Fire-Boltt Tank 1.85" smartwatch. The health tracking features are useful, but I'm facing issues with Bluetooth calling—calls keep dropping after a few minutes.

CUSTOMER: I’ve updated the permissions and disabled battery optimization. The test call lasted longer, but it still disconnected once.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking. As a next step, please unpair and re-pair the watch, then restart both your phone and the smartwatch. If the issue continues, we can log a case for a potential firmware update or replacement, depending on diagnostics results.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll try that. If it still fails, I’d prefer a replacement device.

SUPPORT REP: That’s completely fair. I’ve noted your preference for a replacement if reconnection steps don’t resolve the issue. You’ll receive a follow-up email with instructions and a reference number for this case. Thank you for your patience and for choosing this smartwatch.

inputs.product_name: RC PRINT GI 790 Ink Refill for Canon G-series PIXMA Printers
inputs.text:
Customer Support Chat Transcript

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm having trouble with the RC PRINT GI 790 ink refill I bought for my Canon PIXMA G2010. After refilling, the prints are coming out streaky and some colors seem faded. I followed the basic instructions, but I'm not sure if I missed a step.

SUPPORT REP (Allen Thompson, Engineering): Thanks for reaching out, Paolo. I understand how frustrating print quality issues can be, especially when you're relying on accurate colors. Let me walk you through a quick diagnostic and a few steps that usually resolve these problems.

First, please confirm:
1) Which exact printer model are you using (e.g., G2010, G3010, etc.)?
2) Whether you fully cleaned the ink tank and print head before using the RC PRINT GI 790 ink, as mixing old pigment ink with new dye ink can cause streaks.

In the meantime, here are some steps you can try:
- Run the printer's built-in nozzle check and head cleaning routine from the maintenance menu.
- Make sure the ink tanks are not overfilled and that the vent caps are properly open.
- Print a test page using the printer's highest quality setting to see if the issue persists.

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Canon PIXMA G2012. I did a quick clean of the tank, but I don't think I fully flushed the old ink out. I haven't run the nozzle check yet.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. Since G2012 is fully compatible with RC PRINT GI 790, the issue is likely due to residual pigment ink mixing with the new dye-based ink.

Here is what I recommend:
1) Perform a deep cleaning cycle from the printer maintenance settings (not just a standard cleaning).
2) If possible, flush the print head with compatible cleaning solution recommended for Canon G-series before refilling again.
3) After cleaning, refill with fresh RC PRINT GI 790 ink, ensuring each color tank is filled only to the indicated line.
4) Run a nozzle check and align the print head.

If, after these steps, streaks remain, please send us a scanned sample of the print. We can analyze the pattern and confirm if the print head has a hardware issue or if further software-level calibration is needed.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. I'll perform the deep cleaning and refill properly following your steps. If it still looks off, I'll send a sample.

SUPPORT REP: Great. Once you've tried these steps, reply to this chat or email us the scanned print at support@inazuma-print.com with the subject line "RC PRINT GI 790 – Quality Check for Paolo (frans)". We'll monitor your case and, if needed, arrange a replacement ink batch or additional guidance.

Thank you for your patience and for choosing RC PRINT GI 790. We're here to help you get clear, vibrant prints again.

inputs.product_name: RC PRINT GI 790 Ink Refill for Canon G-series PIXMA Printers
inputs.text:
Customer Support Chat Transcript

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm having trouble with the RC PRINT GI 790 ink refill I bought for my Canon PIXMA G2010. After refilling, the prints are coming out streaky and some colors seem faded. I followed the basic instructions, but I'm not sure if I missed a step.

SUPPORT REP (Allen Thompson, Engineering): Thanks for reaching out, Paolo. I understand how frustrating print quality issues can be, especially when you're relying on accurate colors. Let me walk you through a quick diagnostic and a few steps that usually resolve these problems.

First, please confirm:
1) Which exact printer model are you using (e.g., G2010, G3010, etc.)?
2) Whether you fully cleaned the ink tank and print head before using the RC PRINT GI 790 ink, as mixing old pigment ink with new dye ink can cause streaks.

In the meantime, here are some steps you can try:
- Run the printer's built-in nozzle check and head cleaning routine from the maintenance menu.
- Make sure the ink tanks are not overfilled and that the vent caps are properly open.
- Print a test page using the printer's highest quality setting to see if the issue persists.

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Canon PIXMA G2012. I did a quick clean of the tank, but I don't think I fully flushed the old ink out. I haven't run the nozzle check yet.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. Since G2012 is fully compatible with RC PRINT GI 790, the issue is likely due to residual pigment ink mixing with the new dye-based ink.

Here is what I recommend:
1) Perform a deep cleaning cycle from the printer maintenance settings (not just a standard cleaning).
2) If possible, flush the print head with compatible cleaning solution recommended for Canon G-series before refilling again.
3) After cleaning, refill with fresh RC PRINT GI 790 ink, ensuring each color tank is filled only to the indicated line.
4) Run a nozzle check and align the print head.

If, after these steps, streaks remain, please send us a scanned sample of the print. We can analyze the pattern and confirm if the print head has a hardware issue or if further software-level calibration is needed.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. I'll perform the deep cleaning and refill properly following your steps. If it still looks off, I'll send a sample.

SUPPORT REP: Great. Once you've tried these steps, reply to this chat or email us the scanned print at support@inazuma-print.com with the subject line "RC PRINT GI 790 – Quality Check for Paolo (frans)". We'll monitor your case and, if needed, arrange a replacement ink batch or additional guidance.

Thank you for your patience and for choosing RC PRINT GI 790. We're here to help you get clear, vibrant prints again.

instruction:
Employee_id: emp_0359
Please create an IT support ticket with reference number 70489 at medium priority for an issue reported by employee ID emp_0195 on February 14, 2020, and assign it to technician employee ID emp_0359. The issue description should state: "Hello IT team, this is Aaron Blake from the Information Technology department. My corporate laptop is intermittently losing access to our internal Git repositories hosted over VPN. The connection drops specifically when performing large git clone or pull operations, and I receive timeout errors in my terminal. I have already tried restarting the VPN client, rebooting the machine, and switching from office Wi‑Fi to a wired connection, but the behavior is consistent. This issue is slowing down my development work on several cloud services projects. Could you please investigate network or VPN configuration issues on my account and advise on next steps?" The resolution field should record the response from Alok Sharma from the Engineering IT support group: "Hi Aaron, this is Alok Sharma from the Engineering IT support group. Based on the symptoms you described, the intermittent drops during large Git operations are likely related to an aggressive VPN idle-timeout and packet inspection on large transfers. I have raised the bandwidth threshold for your user profile, refreshed your VPN policy, and whitelisted the Git host for deep inspection on the internal firewall. Please sign out of the VPN, restart the client, and then try a fresh git clone of one of the affected repositories. If you still experience timeouts, capture the exact time and repository URL so we can pull detailed VPN and firewall logs for deeper analysis."

This ticket should reflect the existing issue raised by Akash Roy from HR about unstable VPN connectivity when accessing the Inazuma.co portal remotely, and keep Steven Parker’s resolution notes intact while merely changing the assignment details to emp_0250.

Record her skill set as Customer Communication, Troubleshooting, RMA Processing, Case Documentation, Empathy, and Process Compliance. Installed the V-Guard Zio instant water geyser in our main bathroom and have been using it daily for a few weeks. Heating performance is impressive – water gets hot within seconds and stays consistent even with short on-off usage. The safety features give confidence, especially the thermostat cutoff and anti-siphon protection, which were clearly explained in the manual. Build quality feels solid and the stainless steel inner tank looks durable.

Overall, this is a reliable instant geyser that delivers strong heating and good safety, making it a worthwhile upgrade despite the minor inconveniences around accessories and display size.

inputs.title: Clarify behavior of `configure` endpoint for requests with query parameters
inputs.description: The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators.

--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [
     url(r'^login', login_views.login, name='login'),
     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.
+    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+
+    # The following comments are added to make future maintenance safer:
+    # - Do not reintroduce a trailing `$` without verifying querystring flows.
+    # - If a more restrictive pattern is required, consider explicitly
+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.
     url(r'^checkenv', admin_views.checkenv, name='checkenv'),
     url(r'^storage', admin_views.storage, name='storage'),
     url(r'^network', admin_views.network, name='network'),

input_bindings.title: Clarify behavior of `configure` endpoint for requests with query parameters
input_bindings.description: The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators.
input_bindings.patch:
--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [
     url(r'^login', login_views.login, name='login'),
     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.
+    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+
+    # The following comments are added to make future maintenance safer:
+    # - Do not reintroduce a trailing `$` without verifying querystring flows.
+    # - If a more restrictive pattern is required, consider explicitly
+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.
     url(r'^checkenv', admin_views.checkenv, name='checkenv'),
     url(r'^storage', admin_views.storage, name='storage'),
     url(r'^network', admin_views.network, name='network'),

inputs.product_name: Pajaka® South Indian Filter Coffee Maker 200 ML 2-4 Cup
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently received the Pajaka South Indian Filter Coffee Maker I ordered, but the decoction seems to be leaking from the side instead of dripping properly into the bottom container.

SUPPORT REP (emp_0508): Thanks for reaching out, Paul. I see your customer record under ID vinet and I’ve linked this chat to your recent order. The Pajaka filter should produce a steady drip; leakage usually indicates that the upper chamber isn’t sealed correctly or the grind size is off. Could you confirm the grind level you’re using and whether the top chamber is screwed in firmly?

CUSTOMER: I’m using a medium–fine grind, and I’ve tried tightening the top chamber, but I still see coffee dripping down the outside.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, it’s likely a manufacturing defect in the threading or the gasket. I can arrange a replacement unit with an additional quality check, or process a refund if you prefer.

CUSTOMER: A replacement would be great, as I really want to keep using traditional filter coffee.

SUPPORT REP: Perfect, I’ve initiated a replacement for the same model, tied to your customer ID vinet. You’ll receive a confirmation email shortly and the new unit should arrive within 3–5 business days. If the issue persists with the replacement, we can discuss switching to a different model. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: That’s all, thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Paul. Enjoy your coffee once the new filter arrives, and feel free to contact us again if you need anything.

inputs.description: The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators.
inputs.patch:
--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [
     url(r'^login', login_views.login, name='login'),
     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.
+    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+
+    # The following comments are added to make future maintenance safer:
+    # - Do not reintroduce a trailing `$` without verifying querystring flows.
+    # - If a more restrictive pattern is required, consider explicitly
+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.
     url(r'^checkenv', admin_views.checkenv, name='checkenv'),
     url(r'^storage', admin_views.storage, name='storage'),
     url(r'^network', admin_views.network, name='network'),

inputs.product_name: Pajaka® South Indian Filter Coffee Maker 200 ML 2-4 Cup
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently received the Pajaka South Indian Filter Coffee Maker I ordered, but the decoction seems to be leaking from the side instead of dripping properly into the bottom container.

SUPPORT REP (emp_0508): Thanks for reaching out, Paul. I see your customer record under ID vinet and I’ve linked this chat to your recent order. The Pajaka filter should produce a steady drip; leakage usually indicates that the upper chamber isn’t sealed correctly or the grind size is off. Could you confirm the grind level you’re using and whether the top chamber is screwed in firmly?

CUSTOMER: I’m using a medium–fine grind, and I’ve tried tightening the top chamber, but I still see coffee dripping down the outside.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, it’s likely a manufacturing defect in the threading or the gasket. I can arrange a replacement unit with an additional quality check, or process a refund if you prefer.

CUSTOMER: A replacement would be great, as I really want to keep using traditional filter coffee.

SUPPORT REP: Perfect, I’ve initiated a replacement for the same model, tied to your customer ID vinet. You’ll receive a confirmation email shortly and the new unit should arrive within 3–5 business days. If the issue persists with the replacement, we can discuss switching to a different model. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: That’s all, thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Paul. Enjoy your coffee once the new filter arrives, and feel free to contact us again if you need anything.

inputs.body:
Hi Harsh,

This is Priya from Customer Support Management. I saw the IT ticket you raised regarding access issues to Teams and Slack (Ticket ID: 61043) and wanted to ensure you have all the necessary support from our side as well.

Could you please confirm if the access problem is affecting any of your ongoing customer-facing or cross-functional coordination activities that involve our support teams? If so, share a brief summary of the critical projects or deliverables impacted, so I can coordinate with the relevant stakeholders and help prioritize resolution.

In parallel, I’ll stay aligned with Rohan from IT to track progress on the VPN, firewall, and server configuration checks they’re performing. Once I have an update, I’ll send you a concise summary of the steps taken and any actions required from your end.

Thanks for your patience and collaboration.

Best regards,

input_bindings.title: Clarify behavior of `configure` endpoint for requests with query parameters
input_bindings.description: The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators.
input_bindings.patch:
--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [
     url(r'^login', login_views.login, name='login'),
     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.
+    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+
+    # The following comments are added to make future maintenance safer:
+    # - Do not reintroduce a trailing `$` without verifying querystring flows.
+    # - If a more restrictive pattern is required, consider explicitly
+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.
     url(r'^checkenv', admin_views.checkenv, name='checkenv'),
     url(r'^storage', admin_views.storage, name='storage'),
     url(r'^network', admin_views.network, name='network'),

SUPPORT REP (emp_0137): You’re welcome, Francisco. Your safety is our priority. If you have any additional questions, please reply to the confirmation email or contact support."

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I’m having trouble with the Inalsa Electric Fan Heater Hotty I purchased. After about 20 minutes of use on the hot setting, I notice a burning smell and I’m worried it might be unsafe.

CUSTOMER: That would help. Please proceed with the inspection request.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the quick response.

SUPPORT REP (emp_0137): You’re welcome, Francisco. Your safety is our priority. If you have any additional questions, please reply to the confirmation email or contact support.

inputs.Issue:
Hello IT Support,

I'm facing recurring VPN connectivity drops while supporting Education department customers. Sessions to the Inazuma.co engineering and CRM systems disconnect intermittently, especially during peak hours, which impacts my ability to troubleshoot issues and update tickets in real time.

I've already verified my local network, restarted the VPN client, and checked basic credentials, but the instability continues. Could you please investigate potential server-side or configuration issues, and confirm whether there are known outages or throttling affecting support engineers?

Thank you,

Amarjit Rao
Customer Support Engineer – Education & VPN
emp_1860
inputs.Resolution:
Hi Amarjit,

Thank you for reporting the intermittent VPN connectivity issue.

We have:
1) Reviewed the VPN gateway logs and identified several timeouts linked to your user profile during peak support hours.
2) Increased the session idle timeout for support engineers and moved your profile to the higher-priority gateway pool used by Engineering and Customer Support.
3) Updated the DNS configuration on the VPN servers to reduce lookup delays that were contributing to random disconnects.

Next steps for you:
- Install the latest Inazuma.co VPN client pushed via the internal software portal.
- Reboot your laptop and connect to the "ENG-SUPPORT-VPN" profile.
- If disconnects persist, capture the exact timestamp and error message and reply back to this ticket so we can deep-dive into your individual tunnel logs.

We will continue monitoring your sessions for the next week to ensure stability.

Best regards,
Lisa Montgomery
IT Team Lead
emp_1190

We will continue monitoring your sessions for the next week to ensure stability.

Best regards,
Lisa Montgomery

inputs.product_name: Bajaj DX-7 1000W Dry Iron with Advance Soleplate and Anti-bacterial German Coating Technology, White
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Bajaj DX-7 dry iron from your online store. Overall it works, but I'm worried about how it handles delicate fabrics like silk and chiffon.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Hello, thank you for contacting support and for choosing the Bajaj DX-7. I understand your concern about using the iron safely on delicate materials. Could you let me know if you've tried the lower temperature settings and whether the iron seems to get too hot even on those levels?

CUSTOMER: Yes, even on the lower setting, I'm nervous that it might scorch the fabric. I previously used another brand that had clearer guidance for each fabric type.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): That makes sense. This model uses a standard temperature dial, but you can safely use it on delicate fabrics by pre‑testing on a small, hidden section and always starting at the lowest setting. For very delicate items, we recommend using a thin pressing cloth between the iron and the fabric to avoid direct contact. I can also send you a concise fabric‑specific temperature guide for this product.

CUSTOMER: A guide and the pressing cloth tip would be really helpful. I'm also curious about maintenance—how should I clean the soleplate without damaging the anti‑bacterial coating?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Great question. To clean the soleplate, first unplug the iron and let it cool down completely. Then use a soft, slightly damp cloth with mild soap—avoid abrasive cleaners or metal scrubbers so the coating stays intact. Wipe it dry thoroughly before the next use. I’ll email you the fabric guide and a short care checklist so you have everything in one place.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that answers my questions.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): You’re welcome. If you still feel uncertain after trying these tips, please reach out again and we can review alternative models better suited for frequent delicate‑fabric use. Have a great day!

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that answers my questions.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): You’re welcome. If you still feel uncertain after trying these tips, please reach out again and we can review alternative models better suited for frequent delicate‑fabric use. Have a great day!

input_bindings.product_name: Bajaj DX-7 1000W Dry Iron with Advance Soleplate and Anti-bacterial German Coating Technology, White
input_bindings.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Bajaj DX-7 dry iron from your online store. Overall it works, but I'm worried about how it handles delicate fabrics like silk and chiffon.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Hello, thank you for contacting support and for choosing the Bajaj DX-7. I understand your concern about using the iron safely on delicate materials. Could you let me know if you've tried the lower temperature settings and whether the iron seems to get too hot even on those levels?

CUSTOMER: Yes, even on the lower setting, I'm nervous that it might scorch the fabric. I previously used another brand that had clearer guidance for each fabric type.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): That makes sense. This model uses a standard temperature dial, but you can safely use it on delicate fabrics by pre‑testing on a small, hidden section and always starting at the lowest setting. For very delicate items, we recommend using a thin pressing cloth between the iron and the fabric to avoid direct contact. I can also send you a concise fabric‑specific temperature guide for this product.

CUSTOMER: A guide and the pressing cloth tip would be really helpful. I'm also curious about maintenance—how should I clean the soleplate without damaging the anti‑bacterial coating?

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): Great question. To clean the soleplate, first unplug the iron and let it cool down completely. Then use a soft, slightly damp cloth with mild soap—avoid abrasive cleaners or metal scrubbers so the coating stays intact. Wipe it dry thoroughly before the next use. I’ll email you the fabric guide and a short care checklist so you have everything in one place.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that answers my questions.

SUPPORT REP (emp_1048): You’re welcome. If you still feel uncertain after trying these tips, please reach out again and we can review alternative models better suited for frequent delicate‑fabric use. Have a great day!

inputs.product_name: Inazuma SecureMail Access Suite
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm unable to access my corporate email account through the Inazuma SecureMail Access Suite. It keeps showing an account locked error, and I have several urgent client follow-ups pending. Could you help me get back in quickly?

SUPPORT REP (emp_0192): Thank you for reaching out and I’m sorry for the inconvenience. I can see that your account was locked due to multiple failed login attempts from different locations. I’ve now unlocked your account and initiated a secure password reset. You’ll receive a temporary password and instructions in a separate message. Please log in with that temporary password and then choose a new strong password.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the quick action. Is there anything I should do to prevent this from happening again?

SUPPORT REP (emp_0192): Yes. Please avoid using old saved credentials in your browser or email client after you reset the password, and ensure you’re logging in only via the official SecureMail portal. If you receive any suspicious login alerts or see the lock issue again, contact us immediately and we’ll investigate. I’ll also share a short best‑practices guide for secure email access.

CUSTOMER: That helps. I appreciate the prompt support.

SUPPORT REP (emp_0192): You’re welcome. Your email access should now be restored. If you face any further issues with SecureMail or other Inazuma products, just reach out and we’ll be happy to assist.

+def getEmailAddress(vcard):
+	"""
+	Get email address.
+	Supported formats:
+		- email;something
+		- email;type=something
+	something := (internet,work,home, other)
+	"""

+	for key in vcard:

+

+def findName(vcard):
+	"""
+	Find a version 3.0 name
+	"""
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+	
+	return None
+
+################################################################################
+##  reads a vcard and stores as hash pairs key/value where value is a list    ##
+################################################################################
+
+def readVCARD (buffer) :
+
+	"""
+
+	skips fom <file> until a 'begin' tag from VCARD is encountered.
+	from this point starts constructing a map (key, [values] ) 
+	VCARD entry format -> tag:value 
+	
+		key <- tag
+		[values] <- list with the values of <tag> if there are more tags with the same name
+
+	"""
+	r=' '
+	bgn,end = -1, -1;
+	d = dict()
+	while r and bgn < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		if len (r)  == 0 : return dict()
+		if string.find('begin',string.lower(string.strip(r))) :
+			bgn = 1
+	while r and end < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		s = string.split(string.lower(string.strip(r)),':')
+ 		if s[0] <> '' :
+			if d.has_key(s[0]) :
+				d[s[0]].append(s[1])
+			elif len(s) > 1:
+				d[s[0]] = [s[1]]	
+			else :
+				d[s[0]] = ['']
+			if s[0] == 'end' : end = 1	
+	return d
+
+##################################################################################
+
+###############################################################################################
+## writes on a given file an xml representation for claws-mail addressbook received as a hash  ##
+###############################################################################################
+
+def writeXMLREPR (vcard,file,uid) :
+
+	"""
+	based on <vcard> and <uid> writes only recognized tags (the ones defined in <keywds> list)
+	NOTE: <url> and <org> tag will be written as attributes (there are such tags in claws-mail's
+	      XML schema)
+	"""
+	if len (vcard.keys()) == 0 : return
+	item = vcard.get(keywds[2]);
+	if item:
+		name = string.split(item[0],';')
+	else:
+		""" version 3.0 n ?"""
+		name = findName(vcard)
+		if not name:
+			return
+
+	fn, ln, nick, cn, a = '', '', '', '', ''
+
+	if len(name) >= 2 :
+		fn = name[0]
+		ln = name[1]
+	elif len(name) ==1 :
+		fn = name[0]
+	
+	if vcard.has_key(keywds[4]) :
+		nick = vcard.get(keywds[4])[0]
+	if len(vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]) :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]
+	else :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[0])[0];
+
+	a += str('\n<person uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" first-name=\"' + fn + '\" last-name=\"' + ln
+		+ '\" nick-name=\"' + nick + '\" cn=\"' + cn + '\" >\n')
+	a += '\t<address-list>\n'
+	if vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+		for c in vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+			uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+			a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' + nick  + '\" email=\"' + c + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	else :

+		uid[0] = uid[0]+1
+		a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' +  nick + '\" email=\"' + email + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	a += '\t</address-list>\n'
+	a += '\t<attribute-list>\n'

+        	        for c in vcard.get(key) :

+	a += '</person>\n'
+	file.write(a)

CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Lifelong LLSM120G sandwich griller. Overall it heats quickly and works fine, but I have a couple of concerns.

CUSTOMER: Sure. First, the power cord length is very short, so I’m struggling to place it conveniently on my kitchen counter. Second, I notice that the outer body gets quite warm after a few minutes of use, and I’m worried about safety.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Regarding the cord length, this model ships with a compact cord to reduce tangling and storage issues, but I realise that can be inconvenient. A practical workaround is to use a heavy‑duty, grounded extension cord rated for kitchen appliances, placed away from water sources. For the warm outer body: some heating is expected due to the 750W elements, but the unit is designed with heat‑resistant housing.

SUPPORT REP: Could you tell me whether you’re using it continuously for long sessions or mostly for quick sandwiches, and whether it’s placed near a wall or other objects?

CUSTOMER: Mostly quick sandwiches, but it is close to the backsplash on the counter.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks, that helps. I recommend leaving a few inches of clearance around the unit to let heat dissipate, and avoiding covering the vents. Also, always keep the handle and base dry and use heat‑proof gloves if needed. If the housing feels excessively hot (too hot to touch briefly), please stop using the device and share a short video or photos so we can assess a potential defect.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll adjust the placement and try with an extension cord. If it still seems unsafe, I’ll contact you again.

SUPPORT REP: That sounds good. I’ve logged your feedback about cord length and perceived heating so our product team can review it for future revisions. If you experience any burning smell, discoloration, or visible damage, stop using the griller and reach out immediately so we can help with inspection or replacement options.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Philip. If you have more questions about safe usage or warranty coverage, I’m here to help.

CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Lifelong LLSM120G sandwich griller. Overall it heats quickly and works fine, but I have a couple of concerns.

SUPPORT REP (Ray Williams - emp_0528): Thanks for reaching out, Philip. I’m happy to help. Could you describe the issues you’re facing in a bit more detail?

CUSTOMER: Sure. First, the power cord length is very short, so I’m struggling to place it conveniently on my kitchen counter. Second, I notice that the outer body gets quite warm after a few minutes of use, and I’m worried about safety.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Regarding the cord length, this model ships with a compact cord to reduce tangling and storage issues, but I realise that can be inconvenient. A practical workaround is to use a heavy‑duty, grounded extension cord rated for kitchen appliances, placed away from water sources. For the warm outer body: some heating is expected due to the 750W elements, but the unit is designed with heat‑resistant housing.

SUPPORT REP: Could you tell me whether you’re using it continuously for long sessions or mostly for quick sandwiches, and whether it’s placed near a wall or other objects?

CUSTOMER: Mostly quick sandwiches, but it is close to the backsplash on the counter.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks, that helps. I recommend leaving a few inches of clearance around the unit to let heat dissipate, and avoiding covering the vents. Also, always keep the handle and base dry and use heat‑proof gloves if needed. If the housing feels excessively hot (too hot to touch briefly), please stop using the device and share a short video or photos so we can assess a potential defect.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll adjust the placement and try with an extension cord. If it still seems unsafe, I’ll contact you again.

SUPPORT REP: That sounds good. I’ve logged your feedback about cord length and perceived heating so our product team can review it for future revisions. If you experience any burning smell, discoloration, or visible damage, stop using the griller and reach out immediately so we can help with inspection or replacement options.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Philip. If you have more questions about safe usage or warranty coverage, I’m here to help.

+##################################################################################
+
+###############################################################################################
+## writes on a given file an xml representation for claws-mail addressbook received as a hash  ##
+###############################################################################################
+
+def writeXMLREPR (vcard,file,uid) :
+
+	"""
+	based on <vcard> and <uid> writes only recognized tags (the ones defined in <keywds> list)
+	NOTE: <url> and <org> tag will be written as attributes (there are such tags in claws-mail's
+	      XML schema)
+	"""
+	if len (vcard.keys()) == 0 : return
+	item = vcard.get(keywds[2]);
+	if item:
+		name = string.split(item[0],';')
+	else:
+		""" version 3.0 n ?"""
+		name = findName(vcard)
+		if not name:
+			return
+
+	fn, ln, nick, cn, a = '', '', '', '', ''
+
+	if len(name) >= 2 :
+		fn = name[0]
+		ln = name[1]
+	elif len(name) ==1 :
+		fn = name[0]
+	
+	if vcard.has_key(keywds[4]) :
+		nick = vcard.get(keywds[4])[0]
+	if len(vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]) :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]
+	else :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[0])[0];
+
+	a += str('\n<person uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" first-name=\"' + fn + '\" last-name=\"' + ln
+		+ '\" nick-name=\"' + nick + '\" cn=\"' + cn + '\" >\n')
+	a += '\t<address-list>\n'
+	if vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+		for c in vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+			uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+			a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' + nick  + '\" email=\"' + c + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	else :
+		email = getEmailAddress(vcard)
+		uid[0] = uid[0]+1
+		a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' +  nick + '\" email=\"' + email + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	a += '\t</address-list>\n'
+	a += '\t<attribute-list>\n'
+	for key in keywds[5:] :
+		if vcard.get(key) :
+        	        for c in vcard.get(key) :
+        	       	        uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+	                       	a += '\t\t<attribute uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" name=\"' + key +'\">'+c+'</attribute>\n'
+	a += '\t</attribute-list>\n'
+	a += '</person>\n'
+	file.write(a)
+	file.flush()
+		
+###################################################################################################
+
+def convert (in_f, o_f, name='INBOX') :
+	d = {'d':1}
+	uid = [int(time.time())]
+	
+	try :
+		print 'proccessing...\n'
+		o_f.write('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1" ?>\n<address-book name="'+name+'" >\n');
+		
+		buf = normalizeLongLines(in_f)
+		buffer = StringIO.StringIO(buf)
+		while len(d.keys()) > 0 :
+			d = readVCARD(buffer)
+			writeXMLREPR (d, o_f, uid)
+			uid[0] = uid [0]+1
+		
+		o_f.write('\n</address-book>')
+		print 'finished processing...\n'
+	except IOError, err :
+		print 'Caught an IOError : ',err,'\t ABORTING!!!'
+		raise err
+
+#################################################################################################
+
+def execute () :
+	if len(sys.argv) <> 3 and len(sys.argv) <> 2 :
+		print str("\nUsage: vcard2xml.py  source_file [destination_file]\n\n" +
+		'\tWhen only <source_file> is specified will overwrite the existing addressbook.\n'+
+		'\tWhen both arguments are suplied will create a new additional addressbook named \n\tas the destination file.'+'\n\tNOTE: in both cases the Claws Mail must be closed and ran at least once.\n\n')
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	in_file = None
+	out_file = None
+	path_to_out = os.environ['HOME']+'/.claws-mail/'
+	adr_idx = 'addrbook--index.xml'
+	adr_idx_file = None
+	tmp_adr_idx_file= None
+	got_ex = 0
+
+	try :
+		in_file = open(sys.argv[1])
+	except IOError, e:
+		print 'Could not open input file <',sys.argv[1],'>  ABORTING'
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+		try :
+			dlist = os.listdir(path_to_out);
+			flist=[]
+			for l in dlist :
+				if l.find('addrbook') == 0 and l.find("addrbook--index.xml") < 0 and l.find('bak') < 0 :
+					flist.append(l)
+			flist.sort()
+			out_file = flist.pop()
+			os.rename(path_to_out+out_file, path_to_out+out_file+'.tmp')
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+out_file,'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file)
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	else :
+		try :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx, path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			tmp_adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx,'w')
+		except Exception, e :
+			print 'Could not open <', path_to_out+adr_idx,'> file. Make sure you started Claws Mail at least once.'
+			sys.exit(1)
+		try :
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+sys.argv[2],'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file, sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0])
+			l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+			while l :
+				if l.strip() == '</book_list>' :
+					adr_idx_file.write('\t<book name="'+sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0] +'" file="'+sys.argv[2]+'" />\n')
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				else :
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	
+
+	if got_ex :
+		#clean up the mess
+		print 'got exception, cleaning up the mess... changed files will be restored...\n'
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if out_file :
+			out_file.close()
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name)
+		else :
+			os.remove(out_file.name)
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp', path_to_out+adr_idx)
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+				
+	else :
+		#closing all and moving temporary data into place
+		print 'closing open files...\n'
+		in_file.close()
+		out_file.close()	
+		if len(sys.argv) == 3 :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp',path_to_out+adr_idx+'.bak' )
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name+'.bak')
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+		print 'done!'
+		
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    execute ()
+
+

inputs.product_name: Lifelong LLSM120G Sandwich Griller , Classic Pro 750 W Sandwich Maker with 4 Slice Non-Stick Fixed Plates for Sandwiches at Home with 1 Year Warranty (Black)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Lifelong LLSM120G sandwich griller. Overall it heats quickly and works fine, but I have a couple of concerns.

SUPPORT REP (Ray Williams - emp_0528): Thanks for reaching out, Philip. I’m happy to help. Could you describe the issues you’re facing in a bit more detail?

CUSTOMER: Sure. First, the power cord length is very short, so I’m struggling to place it conveniently on my kitchen counter. Second, I notice that the outer body gets quite warm after a few minutes of use, and I’m worried about safety.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Regarding the cord length, this model ships with a compact cord to reduce tangling and storage issues, but I realise that can be inconvenient. A practical workaround is to use a heavy‑duty, grounded extension cord rated for kitchen appliances, placed away from water sources. For the warm outer body: some heating is expected due to the 750W elements, but the unit is designed with heat‑resistant housing.

SUPPORT REP: Could you tell me whether you’re using it continuously for long sessions or mostly for quick sandwiches, and whether it’s placed near a wall or other objects?

CUSTOMER: Mostly quick sandwiches, but it is close to the backsplash on the counter.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks, that helps. I recommend leaving a few inches of clearance around the unit to let heat dissipate, and avoiding covering the vents. Also, always keep the handle and base dry and use heat‑proof gloves if needed. If the housing feels excessively hot (too hot to touch briefly), please stop using the device and share a short video or photos so we can assess a potential defect.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll adjust the placement and try with an extension cord. If it still seems unsafe, I’ll contact you again.

SUPPORT REP: That sounds good. I’ve logged your feedback about cord length and perceived heating so our product team can review it for future revisions. If you experience any burning smell, discoloration, or visible damage, stop using the griller and reach out immediately so we can help with inspection or replacement options.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Philip. If you have more questions about safe usage or warranty coverage, I’m here to help.

+def getEmailAddress(vcard):
+	"""
+	Get email address.
+	Supported formats:
+		- email;something
+		- email;type=something
+	something := (internet,work,home, other)
+	"""
+	
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'email':
+				list = vcard[key]
+				return list[0]
+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'email':
+				list = vcard[key]
+				return list[0]
+	
+	return ""
+
+def findName(vcard):
+	"""
+	Find a version 3.0 name
+	"""
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+	
+	return None
+
+################################################################################
+##  reads a vcard and stores as hash pairs key/value where value is a list    ##
+################################################################################
+
+def readVCARD (buffer) :
+
+	"""
+
+	skips fom <file> until a 'begin' tag from VCARD is encountered.
+	from this point starts constructing a map (key, [values] ) 
+	VCARD entry format -> tag:value 
+	
+		key <- tag
+		[values] <- list with the values of <tag> if there are more tags with the same name
+
+	"""
+	r=' '
+	bgn,end = -1, -1;
+	d = dict()
+	while r and bgn < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		if len (r)  == 0 : return dict()
+		if string.find('begin',string.lower(string.strip(r))) :
+			bgn = 1
+	while r and end < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		s = string.split(string.lower(string.strip(r)),':')
+ 		if s[0] <> '' :
+			if d.has_key(s[0]) :
+				d[s[0]].append(s[1])
+			elif len(s) > 1:
+				d[s[0]] = [s[1]]	
+			else :
+				d[s[0]] = ['']
+			if s[0] == 'end' : end = 1	
+	return d
+
+##################################################################################
+
+###############################################################################################
+## writes on a given file an xml representation for claws-mail addressbook received as a hash  ##
+###############################################################################################
+
+def writeXMLREPR (vcard,file,uid) :
+
+	"""
+	based on <vcard> and <uid> writes only recognized tags (the ones defined in <keywds> list)
+	NOTE: <url> and <org> tag will be written as attributes (there are such tags in claws-mail's
+	      XML schema)
+	"""
+	if len (vcard.keys()) == 0 : return
+	item = vcard.get(keywds[2]);
+	if item:
+		name = string.split(item[0],';')
+	else:
+		""" version 3.0 n ?"""
+		name = findName(vcard)
+		if not name:
+			return
+
+	fn, ln, nick, cn, a = '', '', '', '', ''
+
+	if len(name) >= 2 :
+		fn = name[0]
+		ln = name[1]
+	elif len(name) ==1 :
+		fn = name[0]
+	
+	if vcard.has_key(keywds[4]) :
+		nick = vcard.get(keywds[4])[0]
+	if len(vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]) :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]
+	else :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[0])[0];
+
+	a += str('\n<person uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" first-name=\"' + fn + '\" last-name=\"' + ln
+		+ '\" nick-name=\"' + nick + '\" cn=\"' + cn + '\" >\n')
+	a += '\t<address-list>\n'
+	if vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+		for c in vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+			uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+			a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' + nick  + '\" email=\"' + c + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	else :
+		email = getEmailAddress(vcard)
+		uid[0] = uid[0]+1
+		a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' +  nick + '\" email=\"' + email + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	a += '\t</address-list>\n'
+	a += '\t<attribute-list>\n'
+	for key in keywds[5:] :
+		if vcard.get(key) :
+        	        for c in vcard.get(key) :
+        	       	        uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+	                       	a += '\t\t<attribute uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" name=\"' + key +'\">'+c+'</attribute>\n'
+	a += '\t</attribute-list>\n'
+	a += '</person>\n'
+	file.write(a)
+	file.flush()
+		
+###################################################################################################
+
+def convert (in_f, o_f, name='INBOX') :
+	d = {'d':1}
+	uid = [int(time.time())]
+	
+	try :
+		print 'proccessing...\n'
+		o_f.write('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1" ?>\n<address-book name="'+name+'" >\n');
+		
+		buf = normalizeLongLines(in_f)
+		buffer = StringIO.StringIO(buf)
+		while len(d.keys()) > 0 :
+			d = readVCARD(buffer)
+			writeXMLREPR (d, o_f, uid)
+			uid[0] = uid [0]+1
+		
+		o_f.write('\n</address-book>')
+		print 'finished processing...\n'
+	except IOError, err :
+		print 'Caught an IOError : ',err,'\t ABORTING!!!'
+		raise err
+
+#################################################################################################
+
+def execute () :
+	if len(sys.argv) <> 3 and len(sys.argv) <> 2 :
+		print str("\nUsage: vcard2xml.py  source_file [destination_file]\n\n" +
+		'\tWhen only <source_file> is specified will overwrite the existing addressbook.\n'+
+		'\tWhen both arguments are suplied will create a new additional addressbook named \n\tas the destination file.'+'\n\tNOTE: in both cases the Claws Mail must be closed and ran at least once.\n\n')
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	in_file = None
+	out_file = None
+	path_to_out = os.environ['HOME']+'/.claws-mail/'
+	adr_idx = 'addrbook--index.xml'
+	adr_idx_file = None
+	tmp_adr_idx_file= None
+	got_ex = 0
+
+	try :
+		in_file = open(sys.argv[1])
+	except IOError, e:
+		print 'Could not open input file <',sys.argv[1],'>  ABORTING'
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+		try :
+			dlist = os.listdir(path_to_out);
+			flist=[]
+			for l in dlist :
+				if l.find('addrbook') == 0 and l.find("addrbook--index.xml") < 0 and l.find('bak') < 0 :
+					flist.append(l)
+			flist.sort()
+			out_file = flist.pop()
+			os.rename(path_to_out+out_file, path_to_out+out_file+'.tmp')
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+out_file,'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file)
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	else :
+		try :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx, path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			tmp_adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx,'w')
+		except Exception, e :
+			print 'Could not open <', path_to_out+adr_idx,'> file. Make sure you started Claws Mail at least once.'
+			sys.exit(1)
+		try :
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+sys.argv[2],'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file, sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0])
+			l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+			while l :
+				if l.strip() == '</book_list>' :
+					adr_idx_file.write('\t<book name="'+sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0] +'" file="'+sys.argv[2]+'" />\n')
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				else :
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	
+
+	if got_ex :
+		#clean up the mess
+		print 'got exception, cleaning up the mess... changed files will be restored...\n'
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if out_file :
+			out_file.close()
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name)
+		else :
+			os.remove(out_file.name)
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp', path_to_out+adr_idx)
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+				
+	else :
+		#closing all and moving temporary data into place
+		print 'closing open files...\n'
+		in_file.close()
+		out_file.close()	
+		if len(sys.argv) == 3 :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp',path_to_out+adr_idx+'.bak' )
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name+'.bak')
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+		print 'done!'
+		
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    execute ()
+
+

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Lifelong LLSM120G sandwich griller. Overall it heats quickly and works fine, but I have a couple of concerns.

SUPPORT REP (Ray Williams - emp_0528): Thanks for reaching out, Philip. I’m happy to help. Could you describe the issues you’re facing in a bit more detail?

CUSTOMER: Sure. First, the power cord length is very short, so I’m struggling to place it conveniently on my kitchen counter. Second, I notice that the outer body gets quite warm after a few minutes of use, and I’m worried about safety.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Regarding the cord length, this model ships with a compact cord to reduce tangling and storage issues, but I realise that can be inconvenient. A practical workaround is to use a heavy‑duty, grounded extension cord rated for kitchen appliances, placed away from water sources. For the warm outer body: some heating is expected due to the 750W elements, but the unit is designed with heat‑resistant housing.

SUPPORT REP: Could you tell me whether you’re using it continuously for long sessions or mostly for quick sandwiches, and whether it’s placed near a wall or other objects?

CUSTOMER: Mostly quick sandwiches, but it is close to the backsplash on the counter.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks, that helps. I recommend leaving a few inches of clearance around the unit to let heat dissipate, and avoiding covering the vents. Also, always keep the handle and base dry and use heat‑proof gloves if needed. If the housing feels excessively hot (too hot to touch briefly), please stop using the device and share a short video or photos so we can assess a potential defect.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll adjust the placement and try with an extension cord. If it still seems unsafe, I’ll contact you again.

SUPPORT REP: That sounds good. I’ve logged your feedback about cord length and perceived heating so our product team can review it for future revisions. If you experience any burning smell, discoloration, or visible damage, stop using the griller and reach out immediately so we can help with inspection or replacement options.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Philip. If you have more questions about safe usage or warranty coverage, I’m here to help.

inputs.Issue:
Hello IT Team,

Following up on our recent coordination regarding VPN connectivity for HR systems, I'm experiencing intermittent access issues to the HR application used by MA- and HR-level employees. Specifically, my sessions drop whenever I try to access employee records or generate reports, and I occasionally see timeout errors linked to the VPN gateway.

Could you please investigate whether there are any configuration or routing problems affecting HR-related VPN traffic and help stabilize access so that I can reliably reach the employee systems?

Thank you,
Aaron Douglas (emp_0391), Management Associate MA11
inputs.Resolution:
Dear Aaron,

Thank you for reporting the intermittent VPN access issues to the HR application. To address this, we will perform the following steps:
1. Review current VPN gateway logs for your user profile (emp_0391) to identify repeated timeout or session drop patterns.
2. Check routing and firewall rules specifically for HR application subnets to ensure traffic from management and HR associates is not being throttled or blocked.
3. Verify that your VPN client is running the latest approved configuration profile and that the keep-alive settings are correctly applied.
4. If necessary, we will temporarily increase logging on the HR application gateway and coordinate a brief maintenance window to apply configuration fixes.

In the meantime, please avoid switching networks during active VPN sessions and try reconnecting if you notice a drop. We will update you once the review is complete and any changes have been deployed.

Best regards,
IT Support – Assigned to emp_0688

The date of purchase should be recorded as 2012-06-15.

In addition, record a customer support interaction with chat reference 752 for this same product and customer, handled by employee emp_0803. Attach the full conversation text exactly as follows, including all messages and line breaks:

"CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently bought the Zoul USB C Backup Cable for External Drives that I used with my latest order. The transfer speed is good, but the connector feels a bit loose on one of my external SSDs and sometimes disconnects if the cable is nudged.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal Ranjan): Thanks for reaching out and for purchasing the Zoul USB C Backup Cable. Let me help you troubleshoot this. Could you confirm which brand/model of SSD you’re using and whether the issue occurs on multiple USB-C ports or only a specific one?

CUSTOMER: I’m using a 1TB Samsung T7 and I’ve tested it on two USB-C ports on my laptop. The issue seems slightly better on one port, but I still get random disconnects if the cable moves.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Understood. This might be a seating tolerance issue between the connector and that drive’s port. Please try gently reinserting the connector until you hear/feel a firm click and check that there’s no dust or debris in the SSD port. Also test the cable with another USB-C device, such as a phone or different drive, to see if the behavior is consistent.

CUSTOMER: I tested with my phone and another smaller SSD. The connection is stable there. The issue is mostly with the Samsung T7.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Thanks for testing that. Since the cable works reliably with other devices, this points to a minor fit variance with that specific drive. As a workaround, avoid bending the cable sharply near the connector and use a short strain-relief loop so the connector isn’t under tension. If you’re still unhappy with the connection stability, we can either arrange a replacement cable from a different batch or offer a partial refund on this purchase.

CUSTOMER: I’d prefer a replacement from another batch to see if that improves the fit.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Absolutely, I will initiate a replacement request right away and you’ll receive confirmation by email shortly. The new cable should arrive within a few business days. If the replacement still gives you trouble, contact us again and we’ll explore a refund option.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Thanks for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): You’re welcome. We appreciate your business and feedback—it helps us improve future batches. Have a great day!"

input_bindings.product_name: Zoul USB C Backup Cable for External Drives
input_bindings.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently bought the Zoul USB C Backup Cable for External Drives that I used with my latest order. The transfer speed is good, but the connector feels a bit loose on one of my external SSDs and sometimes disconnects if the cable is nudged.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal Ranjan): Thanks for reaching out and for purchasing the Zoul USB C Backup Cable. Let me help you troubleshoot this. Could you confirm which brand/model of SSD you’re using and whether the issue occurs on multiple USB-C ports or only a specific one?

CUSTOMER: I’m using a 1TB Samsung T7 and I’ve tested it on two USB-C ports on my laptop. The issue seems slightly better on one port, but I still get random disconnects if the cable moves.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Understood. This might be a seating tolerance issue between the connector and that drive’s port. Please try gently reinserting the connector until you hear/feel a firm click and check that there’s no dust or debris in the SSD port. Also test the cable with another USB-C device, such as a phone or different drive, to see if the behavior is consistent.

CUSTOMER: I tested with my phone and another smaller SSD. The connection is stable there. The issue is mostly with the Samsung T7.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Thanks for testing that. Since the cable works reliably with other devices, this points to a minor fit variance with that specific drive. As a workaround, avoid bending the cable sharply near the connector and use a short strain-relief loop so the connector isn’t under tension. If you’re still unhappy with the connection stability, we can either arrange a replacement cable from a different batch or offer a partial refund on this purchase.

CUSTOMER: I’d prefer a replacement from another batch to see if that improves the fit.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Absolutely, I will initiate a replacement request right away and you’ll receive confirmation by email shortly. The new cable should arrive within a few business days. If the replacement still gives you trouble, contact us again and we’ll explore a refund option.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Thanks for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): You’re welcome. We appreciate your business and feedback—it helps us improve future batches. Have a great day!

inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I'm having intermittent tracking issues with my Lenovo 130 Wireless Compact Mouse B099SD8PRP. The cursor occasionally lags or jumps, especially when I'm switching quickly between spreadsheets and browser tabs.

Support (Alok Mathur, emp_0883): Thanks for contacting support, Manuel. I understand you’re seeing lag and jumpy cursor behavior with the mouse. Let me ask a couple of quick questions: does this occur only on a particular surface (e.g., glossy desk, glass, or fabric mousepad), and are you using the original Nano USB receiver directly in the laptop/PC, or through a hub or docking station?

Customer: I’m using it on a wooden desk without a mousepad, and the Nano receiver is plugged into a USB hub connected to my laptop.

Support: That’s helpful, thank you. The 1000 DPI optical sensor in this model can become less accurate on certain surfaces and when the wireless signal is slightly degraded. Let’s try three steps: (1) plug the Nano USB receiver directly into the laptop’s USB port instead of the hub; (2) move any nearby wireless devices (Wi‑Fi router, external drives) away from the receiver by at least 20–30 cm; and (3) test the mouse on a non‑reflective mousepad or sheet of paper to see if tracking stabilizes.

Customer: I switched the receiver to the laptop and tried the mouse on a mousepad. The cursor is much smoother now, but I’d still like slightly higher precision when editing images.

Support: Great, that confirms it was a combination of surface and wireless interference. For finer control, you can reduce pointer speed in your OS settings so the 1000 DPI sensor feels more precise. Also make sure no other wireless mouse or keyboard is sharing the same USB hub. If you’d like, I can also share our recommended accessory list for this mouse (mousepads and USB extenders) via email.

Customer: Yes, please send that over. Thanks for the help.

Support: You’re welcome, Manuel. I’ll email the accessory recommendations and a short troubleshooting checklist for future reference. If you run into any more issues with B099SD8PRP, just reply to that email or reopen a support chat.

input_bindings.text:
Customer: Hi, I'm having intermittent tracking issues with my Lenovo 130 Wireless Compact Mouse B099SD8PRP. The cursor occasionally lags or jumps, especially when I'm switching quickly between spreadsheets and browser tabs.

Support (Alok Mathur, emp_0883): Thanks for contacting support, Manuel. I understand you’re seeing lag and jumpy cursor behavior with the mouse. Let me ask a couple of quick questions: does this occur only on a particular surface (e.g., glossy desk, glass, or fabric mousepad), and are you using the original Nano USB receiver directly in the laptop/PC, or through a hub or docking station?

Customer: I’m using it on a wooden desk without a mousepad, and the Nano receiver is plugged into a USB hub connected to my laptop.

Support: That’s helpful, thank you. The 1000 DPI optical sensor in this model can become less accurate on certain surfaces and when the wireless signal is slightly degraded. Let’s try three steps: (1) plug the Nano USB receiver directly into the laptop’s USB port instead of the hub; (2) move any nearby wireless devices (Wi‑Fi router, external drives) away from the receiver by at least 20–30 cm; and (3) test the mouse on a non‑reflective mousepad or sheet of paper to see if tracking stabilizes.

Customer: I switched the receiver to the laptop and tried the mouse on a mousepad. The cursor is much smoother now, but I’d still like slightly higher precision when editing images.

Support: Great, that confirms it was a combination of surface and wireless interference. For finer control, you can reduce pointer speed in your OS settings so the 1000 DPI sensor feels more precise. Also make sure no other wireless mouse or keyboard is sharing the same USB hub. If you’d like, I can also share our recommended accessory list for this mouse (mousepads and USB extenders) via email.

Customer: Yes, please send that over. Thanks for the help.

Support: You’re welcome, Manuel. I’ll email the accessory recommendations and a short troubleshooting checklist for future reference. If you run into any more issues with B099SD8PRP, just reply to that email or reopen a support chat.

input_bindings.text:
Customer: Hi, I'm having intermittent tracking issues with my Lenovo 130 Wireless Compact Mouse B099SD8PRP. The cursor occasionally lags or jumps, especially when I'm switching quickly between spreadsheets and browser tabs.

Support (Alok Mathur, emp_0883): Thanks for contacting support, Manuel. I understand you’re seeing lag and jumpy cursor behavior with the mouse. Let me ask a couple of quick questions: does this occur only on a particular surface (e.g., glossy desk, glass, or fabric mousepad), and are you using the original Nano USB receiver directly in the laptop/PC, or through a hub or docking station?

Customer: I’m using it on a wooden desk without a mousepad, and the Nano receiver is plugged into a USB hub connected to my laptop.

Support: That’s helpful, thank you. The 1000 DPI optical sensor in this model can become less accurate on certain surfaces and when the wireless signal is slightly degraded. Let’s try three steps: (1) plug the Nano USB receiver directly into the laptop’s USB port instead of the hub; (2) move any nearby wireless devices (Wi‑Fi router, external drives) away from the receiver by at least 20–30 cm; and (3) test the mouse on a non‑reflective mousepad or sheet of paper to see if tracking stabilizes.

Customer: I switched the receiver to the laptop and tried the mouse on a mousepad. The cursor is much smoother now, but I’d still like slightly higher precision when editing images.

Support: Great, that confirms it was a combination of surface and wireless interference. For finer control, you can reduce pointer speed in your OS settings so the 1000 DPI sensor feels more precise. Also make sure no other wireless mouse or keyboard is sharing the same USB hub. If you’d like, I can also share our recommended accessory list for this mouse (mousepads and USB extenders) via email.

Customer: Yes, please send that over. Thanks for the help.

Support: You’re welcome, Manuel. I’ll email the accessory recommendations and a short troubleshooting checklist for future reference. If you run into any more issues with B099SD8PRP, just reply to that email or reopen a support chat.

inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I bought the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Kettle recently. It heats water fast, but I’ve noticed a slight plastic smell during boiling even after several uses. Is this normal, and how can I get rid of it?

Support (emp_0680): Hello Guillermo, thank you for reaching out and for choosing the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Electric Kettle. A mild odor can sometimes occur with new appliances due to manufacturing residues, but it should reduce over time. Let’s try a deep-clean cycle: fill the kettle to the max line with a 50/50 mix of water and white vinegar, bring it to a boil, then let it sit for 20 minutes before discarding. Rinse and boil plain water 2–3 times afterwards.

Customer: I’ve tried boiling water a few times, but not with vinegar. Is it safe for the stainless steel interior?

Support (emp_0680): Yes, using a diluted white vinegar solution in the proportions mentioned is safe for the stainless steel interior and is a common descaling/odor-removal method. Just avoid abrasive scrubbers on the inner surface. If the smell persists after two cleaning cycles, please let us know so we can review warranty options or arrange an inspection.

Customer: Great, I’ll try that today. If the issue continues, how do I contact you for a possible replacement?

Support (emp_0680): You can reach us through this support channel using your customer ID "peric" or via the purchase invoice you received from Inazuma. Keep the product serial number and your purchase date handy so we can quickly validate the warranty and, if needed, initiate a replacement request.

inputs.product_name: Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Kettle for Fast Boiling, Tea, Coffee & Instant Meals
inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I bought the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Kettle recently. It heats water fast, but I’ve noticed a slight plastic smell during boiling even after several uses. Is this normal, and how can I get rid of it?

Support (emp_0680): Hello Guillermo, thank you for reaching out and for choosing the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Electric Kettle. A mild odor can sometimes occur with new appliances due to manufacturing residues, but it should reduce over time. Let’s try a deep-clean cycle: fill the kettle to the max line with a 50/50 mix of water and white vinegar, bring it to a boil, then let it sit for 20 minutes before discarding. Rinse and boil plain water 2–3 times afterwards.

Customer: I’ve tried boiling water a few times, but not with vinegar. Is it safe for the stainless steel interior?

Support (emp_0680): Yes, using a diluted white vinegar solution in the proportions mentioned is safe for the stainless steel interior and is a common descaling/odor-removal method. Just avoid abrasive scrubbers on the inner surface. If the smell persists after two cleaning cycles, please let us know so we can review warranty options or arrange an inspection.

Customer: Great, I’ll try that today. If the issue continues, how do I contact you for a possible replacement?

Support (emp_0680): You can reach us through this support channel using your customer ID "peric" or via the purchase invoice you received from Inazuma. Keep the product serial number and your purchase date handy so we can quickly validate the warranty and, if needed, initiate a replacement request.

This helps future maintainers understand why the old-format behavior is still tested and how it aligns with current distribution tooling practices. Keep the issue status as open, associate it with employee ID emp_1098, and attach exactly the following patch as the diff for kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py:

--- kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
+++ kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
@@ -96,7 +96,15 @@
-        # old format
-        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
-        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
-        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
-                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
-        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+        # old format
+        # In the legacy format, only a single section is defined and
+        # PyPIRCCommand is expected to infer the default repository
+        # settings based on that server-login section.
+        #
+        # This ensures that existing projects depending on the old
+        # configuration style continue to work even as newer index
+        # server layouts are introduced.
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)

+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that would be helpful.

SUPPORT REP: You're welcome. We appreciate your feedback and will share it with our product team to improve future batches.
