inputs.description: Rajesh Singh (emp_1098), a Software Engineering Team Lead at Inazuma.co, recommends improving the PyPIRC legacy configuration test by making the expectations more explicit and documenting the differences between the new and old .pypirc formats. This helps future maintainers understand why the old-format behavior is still tested and how it aligns with current distribution tooling practices.
inputs.patch:
--- kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
+++ kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
@@ -96,7 +96,15 @@
-        # old format
-        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
-        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
-        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
-                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
-        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+        # old format
+        # In the legacy format, only a single section is defined and
+        # PyPIRCCommand is expected to infer the default repository
+        # settings based on that server-login section.
+        #
+        # This ensures that existing projects depending on the old
+        # configuration style continue to work even as newer index
+        # server layouts are introduced.
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
+        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
+                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
+                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
+        self.assertEqual(config, waited)

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm reaching out because the Pilot Frixion Clicker Roller Pen I purchased is not writing consistently and the ink fades quickly on some of my office documents.

SUPPORT REP (Lisa Montgomery, IT Team Lead): Thank you for contacting support. I understand how important reliable pens are for your daily work. Could you please confirm your order reference and whether you're using the pen on standard office paper or any coated/laminated surfaces?

CUSTOMER: The order is linked to customer ID 'vaffe', and I'm mostly using it on standard A4 copier paper.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. The Frixion pens use thermo-sensitive ink, which can appear lighter or fade if exposed to heat or if the paper is stored near warm equipment. I recommend avoiding prolonged exposure to high temperatures (for example, near printers or sunlight). For critical legal or archival documents, we suggest using a non-erasable pen as stated in the product description.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. Is there anything you can do about this particular batch of pens?

SUPPORT REP: I can arrange a replacement pack from a newer batch and include guidance on best-use scenarios. You will receive an email with shipment details shortly. If the replacement still does not meet your expectations, we can explore a refund or an alternative product.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that would be helpful.

SUPPORT REP: You're welcome. We appreciate your feedback and will share it with our product team to improve future batches.

inputs.subject: Follow-up: Customer support onboarding and escalation process overview
inputs.body:
Hi Jay,

Welcome to the customer support collaboration initiative. As discussed, I'm sharing a summary of our onboarding approach and escalation process so you can align your BPO workflows with the Customer Support team.

Key points:
- All new tickets initiated via phone or chat are logged in the CRM and tagged with the appropriate product category.
- Complex technical issues are escalated to Engineering via IT tickets linked to the corresponding email thread ID (e.g., VPN or platform connectivity problems).
- For warranty or replacement cases, please ensure that purchase details and customer identifiers are validated before initiating RMAs.

I'll be happy to walk you through a few recent cases and show how we coordinate between BPO and Customer Support teams to maintain response quality and resolution speed.

Please let me know a suitable time this week for a 30-minute walkthrough.

Regards,
Arjun

inputs.product_name: Electvision Remote Control Compatible with Amazon Fire tv Stick (Pairing Manual Will be Back Side Remote Control)(P)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm facing issues with my Electvision remote that I use with the Amazon Fire TV Stick. It intermittently stops responding and sometimes delays actions.

SUPPORT REP: Hello Paolo, thanks for reaching out. I understand how frustrating remote issues can be, especially while streaming. I see this chat is linked to your existing IT ticket 13121 that was raised due to connectivity problems. To start, can you confirm whether the remote issues occur only when the Fire TV is connected to your home Wi‑Fi network, or do they also occur when you use an alternate connection such as the VPN workaround suggested in your IT ticket resolution?

CUSTOMER: The remote lag and unresponsiveness seem worse when the network connectivity is unstable. When I switch to the VPN as suggested by IT, it improves slightly but the problem still occurs.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful information. Since we already know there was a temporary network outage affecting the Inazuma.co portal, it’s possible that intermittent connectivity could also impact how quickly the Fire TV interface processes remote commands. Let’s try a few steps: (1) Restart your Fire TV Stick and router, (2) Re‑pair the Electvision remote following the pairing manual printed on the back of the remote, and (3) Test again on both your normal Wi‑Fi and VPN. Please let me know if the responsiveness improves after these steps.

CUSTOMER: I followed the steps and re‑paired the remote. The performance is slightly better on VPN, but I still see occasional delays.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, I recommend we log this as a product support case linked to your existing ticket so our hardware support team can review whether the Electvision remote or the Fire TV configuration needs adjustment or replacement. You may receive a follow‑up email with troubleshooting instructions or an RMA if a defect is confirmed. Meanwhile, you can reduce background apps on the Fire TV and keep the remote in direct line‑of‑sight to the device to minimize latency.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. Please proceed with the follow‑up.

SUPPORT REP: Certainly, Paolo. I’ve documented this interaction and tied it to your IT ticket 13121. Our support team will follow up with next steps. Thank you for your patience.

inputs.product_name: Electvision Remote Control Compatible with Amazon Fire tv Stick (Pairing Manual Will be Back Side Remote Control)(P)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm facing issues with my Electvision remote that I use with the Amazon Fire TV Stick. It intermittently stops responding and sometimes delays actions.

SUPPORT REP: Hello Paolo, thanks for reaching out. I understand how frustrating remote issues can be, especially while streaming. I see this chat is linked to your existing IT ticket 13121 that was raised due to connectivity problems. To start, can you confirm whether the remote issues occur only when the Fire TV is connected to your home Wi‑Fi network, or do they also occur when you use an alternate connection such as the VPN workaround suggested in your IT ticket resolution?

CUSTOMER: The remote lag and unresponsiveness seem worse when the network connectivity is unstable. When I switch to the VPN as suggested by IT, it improves slightly but the problem still occurs.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful information. Since we already know there was a temporary network outage affecting the Inazuma.co portal, it’s possible that intermittent connectivity could also impact how quickly the Fire TV interface processes remote commands. Let’s try a few steps: (1) Restart your Fire TV Stick and router, (2) Re‑pair the Electvision remote following the pairing manual printed on the back of the remote, and (3) Test again on both your normal Wi‑Fi and VPN. Please let me know if the responsiveness improves after these steps.

CUSTOMER: I followed the steps and re‑paired the remote. The performance is slightly better on VPN, but I still see occasional delays.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, I recommend we log this as a product support case linked to your existing ticket so our hardware support team can review whether the Electvision remote or the Fire TV configuration needs adjustment or replacement. You may receive a follow‑up email with troubleshooting instructions or an RMA if a defect is confirmed. Meanwhile, you can reduce background apps on the Fire TV and keep the remote in direct line‑of‑sight to the device to minimize latency.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. Please proceed with the follow‑up.

SUPPORT REP: Certainly, Paolo. I’ve documented this interaction and tied it to your IT ticket 13121. Our support team will follow up with next steps. Thank you for your patience.

inputs.Issue:
Hello IT Team,

Following up on internal discussions regarding VPN connectivity and its impact on customer support workflows, I am raising a formal IT ticket. Over the past week, I have intermittently lost access to the Inazuma.co VPN from my company laptop when connecting from home. During these drops, I am unable to access the CRM system and the internal ticketing portal, which delays my ability to respond to escalated customer issues and coordinate with engineering.

I have tried restarting my machine, reconnecting to my home router, and signing out/signing back into the VPN client, but the connection still drops every few hours without a clear error message.

Could you please investigate the root cause and help stabilize my VPN access so that customer conversations and IT ticket coordination are not impacted?

Thank you,

Mitali Deshpande
Customer Support Coordinator
inputs.Resolution:
Dear Mitali,

Thank you for providing detailed information about the VPN connectivity issues. We have reviewed the VPN server logs and noticed several timeouts associated with your user profile around the times you reported drops.

Actions taken:
1. Cleared and refreshed your VPN session tokens on the authentication server.
2. Updated your VPN client configuration to the latest profile recommended for remote users.
3. Enabled adaptive reconnect settings on your account so the client automatically retries the connection when a brief network fluctuation occurs.

Next steps for you:
1. Please install the updated VPN profile that has been emailed to you.
2. Restart your laptop and connect to the VPN using the new profile.
3. Monitor connectivity for the next 48 hours while accessing CRM and the internal ticketing portal.

If you still experience any disconnections, reply to this ticket with the approximate time of the drop and a screenshot of any error messages, and we will escalate to the network infrastructure team.

Best regards,

Emily Sanders
Software Engineering Associate
Inazuma.co IT Support

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Fire-Boltt Tank 1.85" smartwatch. The health tracking features are useful, but I'm facing issues with Bluetooth calling—calls keep dropping after a few minutes.

SUPPORT REP (Abhinav Sharma - HR Associate assisting via support desk): Thank you for reaching out, Hari. I'm sorry to hear about the call drops. Let me help troubleshoot this. Could you confirm the phone model you are pairing with the watch and whether you have granted all Bluetooth and notification permissions?

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Samsung Galaxy A52. I’ve enabled Bluetooth and notifications, but I’m not sure about all the app permissions.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Please open the Fire-Boltt app, go to Settings > Permissions, and ensure Bluetooth, Phone, and Notifications are all allowed. Also, disable battery optimization for the app in your phone settings, as that can interrupt connections. After making these changes, try a test call.

CUSTOMER: I’ve updated the permissions and disabled battery optimization. The test call lasted longer, but it still disconnected once.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking. As a next step, please unpair and re-pair the watch, then restart both your phone and the smartwatch. If the issue continues, we can log a case for a potential firmware update or replacement, depending on diagnostics results.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll try that. If it still fails, I’d prefer a replacement device.

SUPPORT REP: That’s completely fair. I’ve noted your preference for a replacement if reconnection steps don’t resolve the issue. You’ll receive a follow-up email with instructions and a reference number for this case. Thank you for your patience and for choosing this smartwatch.

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Fire-Boltt Tank 1.85" smartwatch. The health tracking features are useful, but I'm facing issues with Bluetooth calling—calls keep dropping after a few minutes.

SUPPORT REP (Abhinav Sharma - HR Associate assisting via support desk): Thank you for reaching out, Hari. I'm sorry to hear about the call drops. Let me help troubleshoot this. Could you confirm the phone model you are pairing with the watch and whether you have granted all Bluetooth and notification permissions?

CUSTOMER: I'm using a Samsung Galaxy A52. I’ve enabled Bluetooth and notifications, but I’m not sure about all the app permissions.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Please open the Fire-Boltt app, go to Settings > Permissions, and ensure Bluetooth, Phone, and Notifications are all allowed. Also, disable battery optimization for the app in your phone settings, as that can interrupt connections. After making these changes, try a test call.

CUSTOMER: I’ve updated the permissions and disabled battery optimization. The test call lasted longer, but it still disconnected once.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking. As a next step, please unpair and re-pair the watch, then restart both your phone and the smartwatch. If the issue continues, we can log a case for a potential firmware update or replacement, depending on diagnostics results.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll try that. If it still fails, I’d prefer a replacement device.

SUPPORT REP: That’s completely fair. I’ve noted your preference for a replacement if reconnection steps don’t resolve the issue. You’ll receive a follow-up email with instructions and a reference number for this case. Thank you for your patience and for choosing this smartwatch.

Please create an IT support ticket with reference number 70489 at medium priority for an issue raised by employee emp_0195 and assigned on 2020-02-14 to the support engineer emp_0359. The issue description should read: "Hello IT team, this is Aaron Blake from the Information Technology department. My corporate laptop is intermittently losing access to our internal Git repositories hosted over VPN. The connection drops specifically when performing large git clone or pull operations, and I receive timeout errors in my terminal. I have already tried restarting the VPN client, rebooting the machine, and switching from office Wi‑Fi to a wired connection, but the behavior is consistent. This issue is slowing down my development work on several cloud services projects. Could you please investigate network or VPN configuration issues on my account and advise on next steps?" The ticket should also record the following resolution from Alok Sharma in the Engineering IT support group: "Hi Aaron, this is Alok Sharma from the Engineering IT support group. Based on the symptoms you described, the intermittent drops during large Git operations are likely related to an aggressive VPN idle-timeout and packet inspection on large transfers. I have raised the bandwidth threshold for your user profile, refreshed your VPN policy, and whitelisted the Git host for deep inspection on the internal firewall. Please sign out of the VPN, restart the client, and then try a fresh git clone of one of the affected repositories. If you still experience timeouts, capture the exact time and repository URL so we can pull detailed VPN and firewall logs for deeper analysis."

1) We can arrange a complimentary set of different ear tip sizes so you can find a tighter, more comfortable seal.

3) Regarding build quality, I’d like to better understand what feels flimsy to you (for example, hinges, charging case lid, or earbud body), so we can log precise feedback for our product team.

Would you like us to proceed with sending the additional ear tips and an app recommendation list via email?

inputs.product_name: Compact Stainless Steel Travel Kettle 0.8L, Auto Shut-Off, Dual Voltage, Foldable Handle
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Compact Stainless Steel Travel Kettle (0.8L) using my account, and I have a concern about the auto shut-off feature. It sometimes seems to turn off before the water reaches a full boil.

SUPPORT REP (Murugan Kumar, Finance Associate): Hello, thanks for reaching out and for purchasing the travel kettle. I understand how important a reliable auto shut-off is, especially when you’re on the move. Could you please confirm if this early shut-off happens every time or only occasionally, and whether you’re using the kettle with a standard wall socket or a travel adapter?

CUSTOMER: It happens occasionally, mostly when I’m using a travel adapter in hotels. At home with a regular wall socket, it seems to work fine.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful information, thank you. Since the kettle is dual voltage, variations in power from certain travel adapters can trigger the safety shut-off sooner than expected. I recommend checking that your adapter supports the correct voltage range and isn’t limiting current. Also, please ensure the kettle base and cord are firmly connected and the water level is between the minimum and maximum markers.

CUSTOMER: I’ll double-check the adapter specs and water levels. If it still keeps shutting off early, what should I do next?

SUPPORT REP: If the issue persists after verifying the adapter and usage, we can treat this as a potential hardware or compatibility issue. In that case, please share your order ID and a short photo or video of the behavior. Our support team will review it and, if needed, help you with a replacement or repair under the applicable warranty terms. We’ll aim to make this process as smooth as possible.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. I’ll collect the details and get back to you.

SUPPORT REP: Perfect, thank you. We appreciate your patience and want to ensure you can use the kettle confidently during your travels. Feel free to reach out with any other questions in the meantime.

CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Compact Stainless Steel Travel Kettle (0.8L) using my account, and I have a concern about the auto shut-off feature. It sometimes seems to turn off before the water reaches a full boil.

SUPPORT REP (Murugan Kumar, Finance Associate): Hello, thanks for reaching out and for purchasing the travel kettle. I understand how important a reliable auto shut-off is, especially when you’re on the move. Could you please confirm if this early shut-off happens every time or only occasionally, and whether you’re using the kettle with a standard wall socket or a travel adapter?

CUSTOMER: It happens occasionally, mostly when I’m using a travel adapter in hotels. At home with a regular wall socket, it seems to work fine.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful information, thank you. Since the kettle is dual voltage, variations in power from certain travel adapters can trigger the safety shut-off sooner than expected. I recommend checking that your adapter supports the correct voltage range and isn’t limiting current. Also, please ensure the kettle base and cord are firmly connected and the water level is between the minimum and maximum markers.

CUSTOMER: I’ll double-check the adapter specs and water levels. If it still keeps shutting off early, what should I do next?

SUPPORT REP: If the issue persists after verifying the adapter and usage, we can treat this as a potential hardware or compatibility issue. In that case, please share your order ID and a short photo or video of the behavior. Our support team will review it and, if needed, help you with a replacement or repair under the applicable warranty terms. We’ll aim to make this process as smooth as possible.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. I’ll collect the details and get back to you.

SUPPORT REP: Perfect, thank you. We appreciate your patience and want to ensure you can use the kettle confidently during your travels. Feel free to reach out with any other questions in the meantime.

instruction:
Employee_id: emp_0409
Please create a new product sentiment record for the V-Guard Zio Instant Water Geyser (product ID B0B9RN5X8B), with the category exactly recorded as "Home&Kitchen|Heating,Cooling&AirQuality|WaterHeaters&Geysers|InstantWaterHeaters". Use sentiment reference 42001 and link it to review REV-B0B9RN5X8B-42001 from customer hanna moos (customer ID blaus). The product description to associate is: "POWERFUL INSTANT HEATING with a 3 kW heating element, advanced 4-layer safety (pressure release valve, thermostat cutoff at 55°C, overheating protection at 90°C, anti-siphon protection), and a stylish, energy-efficient design with eco-friendly insulation and status display. Robust inner tank made of high-grade 304 stainless steel and rust-proof outer body for long-term durability, backed by multi-year warranty and pan-India installation and service support." The review content to store is:

"Installed the V-Guard Zio instant water geyser in our main bathroom and have been using it daily for a few weeks. Heating performance is impressive – water gets hot within seconds and stays consistent even with short on-off usage. The safety features give confidence, especially the thermostat cutoff and anti-siphon protection, which were clearly explained in the manual. Build quality feels solid and the stainless steel inner tank looks durable.

What could be better: the status display is helpful but a bit small to read from a distance, and the initial installation required an additional purchase of inlet/outlet pipes, which was not obvious at the time of ordering. Noise level during heating is acceptable but noticeable in a quiet house.

Overall, this is a reliable instant geyser that delivers strong heating and good safety, making it a worthwhile upgrade despite the minor inconveniences around accessories and display size." Set the review date as 2019-11-23.

input_bindings.product_name: V-Guard Zio Instant Water Geyser | 3 Litre | 3000 W Heating | White-Blue | | 2 Year Warranty
input_bindings.about_product: POWERFUL INSTANT HEATING with a 3 kW heating element, advanced 4-layer safety (pressure release valve, thermostat cutoff at 55°C, overheating protection at 90°C, anti-siphon protection), and a stylish, energy-efficient design with eco-friendly insulation and status display. Robust inner tank made of high-grade 304 stainless steel and rust-proof outer body for long-term durability, backed by multi-year warranty and pan-India installation and service support.
input_bindings.review_content:
Installed the V-Guard Zio instant water geyser in our main bathroom and have been using it daily for a few weeks. Heating performance is impressive – water gets hot within seconds and stays consistent even with short on-off usage. The safety features give confidence, especially the thermostat cutoff and anti-siphon protection, which were clearly explained in the manual. Build quality feels solid and the stainless steel inner tank looks durable.

What could be better: the status display is helpful but a bit small to read from a distance, and the initial installation required an additional purchase of inlet/outlet pipes, which was not obvious at the time of ordering. Noise level during heating is acceptable but noticeable in a quiet house.

Overall, this is a reliable instant geyser that delivers strong heating and good safety, making it a worthwhile upgrade despite the minor inconveniences around accessories and display size.

instruction:
Employee_id: emp_0802
Please create a new open issue in the 827992983/yue repository with the identifier issue-configure-query-params-002. The issue title should be "Clarify behavior of `configure` endpoint for requests with query parameters". Use the following text verbatim as the issue description:

"The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators."

Attach the following exact yue/urls.py diff as the patch content for the issue:

"--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [
     url(r'^login', login_views.login, name='login'),
     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.
+    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+
+    # The following comments are added to make future maintenance safer:
+    # - Do not reintroduce a trailing `$` without verifying querystring flows.
+    # - If a more restrictive pattern is required, consider explicitly
+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.
     url(r'^checkenv', admin_views.checkenv, name='checkenv'),
     url(r'^storage', admin_views.storage, name='storage'),
     url(r'^network', admin_views.network, name='network'),
"

Record the issue as created at 2025-06-03 10:15:00, keep its status set to open, and associate it with employee ID emp_0802.

inputs.title: Clarify behavior of `configure` endpoint for requests with query parameters
inputs.description: The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators.
inputs.patch:
--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [
     url(r'^login', login_views.login, name='login'),
     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.
+    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+
+    # The following comments are added to make future maintenance safer:
+    # - Do not reintroduce a trailing `$` without verifying querystring flows.
+    # - If a more restrictive pattern is required, consider explicitly
+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.
     url(r'^checkenv', admin_views.checkenv, name='checkenv'),
     url(r'^storage', admin_views.storage, name='storage'),
     url(r'^network', admin_views.network, name='network'),

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently received the Pajaka South Indian Filter Coffee Maker I ordered, but the decoction seems to be leaking from the side instead of dripping properly into the bottom container.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: That’s all, thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Paul. Enjoy your coffee once the new filter arrives, and feel free to contact us again if you need anything.

inputs.product_name: Prestige PIC 16.0+ 1900W Induction Cooktop with Soft Touch Push Buttons (Black)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I purchased the Prestige PIC 16.0+ induction cooktop last week. It works fine overall, but sometimes it stops heating when I use certain pans. Can you help me understand what might be wrong?

SUPPORT REP (Sanjay Kapoor, Finance Associate liaising with Support): Hello Felipe, thanks for reaching out. I can help clarify this. The cooktop requires induction-compatible cookware with a flat base and a bottom diameter between 12cm and 26cm. Could you confirm whether the pans that stop heating are induction-ready and fall within that size range?

CUSTOMER: Now that you mention it, one of the pans I use is older and I’m not sure it’s induction-ready.

SUPPORT REP: That could be the issue. If the pan isn’t induction-compatible or is too small/too large, the cooktop may stop heating for safety reasons. Please try using a pan that clearly states it’s induction-compatible and has a flat bottom in the recommended size range. If the problem persists even with compatible cookware, let us know and we’ll arrange a technical check.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll try with a different pan and see if that resolves the problem.

SUPPORT REP: Great. I’ll also send you a brief guide summarizing the compatible cookware requirements and basic troubleshooting steps. If you still face issues after trying this, please contact us again with the exact pan details and we’ll investigate further.

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm unable to access my corporate email account through the Inazuma SecureMail Access Suite. It keeps showing an account locked error, and I have several urgent client follow-ups pending. Could you help me get back in quickly?

I’ve now unlocked your account and initiated a secure password reset. You’ll receive a temporary password and instructions in a separate message. Please log in with that temporary password and then choose a new strong password.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the quick action. Is there anything I should do to prevent this from happening again?

SUPPORT REP (emp_0192): Yes. Please avoid using old saved credentials in your browser or email client after you reset the password, and ensure you’re logging in only via the official SecureMail portal. If you receive any suspicious login alerts or see the lock issue again, contact us immediately and we’ll investigate. I’ll also share a short best‑practices guide for secure email access.

CUSTOMER: That helps. I appreciate the prompt support.

SUPPORT REP (emp_0192): You’re welcome. Your email access should now be restored. If you face any further issues with SecureMail or other Inazuma products, just reach out and we’ll be happy to assist.

+def getEmailAddress(vcard):
+	"""
+	Get email address.
+	Supported formats:
+		- email;something
+		- email;type=something
+	something := (internet,work,home, other)
+	"""
+	
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'email':
+				list = vcard[key]

+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'email':
+				list = vcard[key]
+				return list[0]
+	
+	return ""
+
+def findName(vcard):
+	"""
+	Find a version 3.0 name
+	"""
+	for key in vcard:
+		items = key.split(';')
+		if len(items) == 2:
+			if items[0].lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+		else:
+			if key.lower() == 'n':
+				return  vcard[key]
+	
+	return None
+
+################################################################################
+##  reads a vcard and stores as hash pairs key/value where value is a list    ##
+################################################################################
+
+def readVCARD (buffer) :
+
+	"""
+
+	skips fom <file> until a 'begin' tag from VCARD is encountered.
+	from this point starts constructing a map (key, [values] ) 
+	VCARD entry format -> tag:value 
+	
+		key <- tag
+		[values] <- list with the values of <tag> if there are more tags with the same name
+
+	"""
+	r=' '
+	bgn,end = -1, -1;
+	d = dict()
+	while r and bgn < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		if len (r)  == 0 : return dict()
+		if string.find('begin',string.lower(string.strip(r))) :
+			bgn = 1
+	while r and end < 0 :
+		r = buffer.readline()
+		s = string.split(string.lower(string.strip(r)),':')
+ 		if s[0] <> '' :
+			if d.has_key(s[0]) :
+				d[s[0]].append(s[1])
+			elif len(s) > 1:
+				d[s[0]] = [s[1]]	
+			else :
+				d[s[0]] = ['']
+			if s[0] == 'end' : end = 1	
+	return d
+
+##################################################################################
+
+###############################################################################################
+## writes on a given file an xml representation for claws-mail addressbook received as a hash  ##
+###############################################################################################
+
+def writeXMLREPR (vcard,file,uid) :
+
+	"""
+	based on <vcard> and <uid> writes only recognized tags (the ones defined in <keywds> list)
+	NOTE: <url> and <org> tag will be written as attributes (there are such tags in claws-mail's
+	      XML schema)
+	"""
+	if len (vcard.keys()) == 0 : return
+	item = vcard.get(keywds[2]);
+	if item:
+		name = string.split(item[0],';')
+	else:
+		""" version 3.0 n ?"""
+		name = findName(vcard)
+		if not name:
+			return
+
+	fn, ln, nick, cn, a = '', '', '', '', ''
+
+	if len(name) >= 2 :
+		fn = name[0]
+		ln = name[1]
+	elif len(name) ==1 :
+		fn = name[0]
+	
+	if vcard.has_key(keywds[4]) :
+		nick = vcard.get(keywds[4])[0]
+	if len(vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]) :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[1])[0]
+	else :
+		cn = vcard.get(keywds[0])[0];
+
+	a += str('\n<person uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" first-name=\"' + fn + '\" last-name=\"' + ln
+		+ '\" nick-name=\"' + nick + '\" cn=\"' + cn + '\" >\n')
+	a += '\t<address-list>\n'
+	if vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+		for c in vcard.get(keywds[3]) :
+			uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+			a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' + nick  + '\" email=\"' + c + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	else :
+		email = getEmailAddress(vcard)
+		uid[0] = uid[0]+1
+		a += '\t\t<address uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" alias=\"' +  nick + '\" email=\"' + email + '\" remarks=\"\" />\n'
+	a += '\t</address-list>\n'
+	a += '\t<attribute-list>\n'
+	for key in keywds[5:] :
+		if vcard.get(key) :
+        	        for c in vcard.get(key) :
+        	       	        uid[0] = uid[0] + 1
+	                       	a += '\t\t<attribute uid=\"' + str(uid[0]) + '\" name=\"' + key +'\">'+c+'</attribute>\n'
+	a += '\t</attribute-list>\n'
+	a += '</person>\n'
+	file.write(a)
+	file.flush()
+		
+###################################################################################################
+
+def convert (in_f, o_f, name='INBOX') :
+	d = {'d':1}
+	uid = [int(time.time())]
+	
+	try :
+		print 'proccessing...\n'
+		o_f.write('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1" ?>\n<address-book name="'+name+'" >\n');
+		
+		buf = normalizeLongLines(in_f)
+		buffer = StringIO.StringIO(buf)
+		while len(d.keys()) > 0 :
+			d = readVCARD(buffer)
+			writeXMLREPR (d, o_f, uid)
+			uid[0] = uid [0]+1
+		
+		o_f.write('\n</address-book>')
+		print 'finished processing...\n'
+	except IOError, err :
+		print 'Caught an IOError : ',err,'\t ABORTING!!!'
+		raise err
+
+#################################################################################################
+
+def execute () :
+	if len(sys.argv) <> 3 and len(sys.argv) <> 2 :
+		print str("\nUsage: vcard2xml.py  source_file [destination_file]\n\n" +
+		'\tWhen only <source_file> is specified will overwrite the existing addressbook.\n'+
+		'\tWhen both arguments are suplied will create a new additional addressbook named \n\tas the destination file.'+'\n\tNOTE: in both cases the Claws Mail must be closed and ran at least once.\n\n')
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	in_file = None
+	out_file = None
+	path_to_out = os.environ['HOME']+'/.claws-mail/'
+	adr_idx = 'addrbook--index.xml'
+	adr_idx_file = None
+	tmp_adr_idx_file= None
+	got_ex = 0
+
+	try :
+		in_file = open(sys.argv[1])
+	except IOError, e:
+		print 'Could not open input file <',sys.argv[1],'>  ABORTING'
+		sys.exit(1)
+
+	if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+		try :
+			dlist = os.listdir(path_to_out);
+			flist=[]
+			for l in dlist :
+				if l.find('addrbook') == 0 and l.find("addrbook--index.xml") < 0 and l.find('bak') < 0 :
+					flist.append(l)
+			flist.sort()
+			out_file = flist.pop()
+			os.rename(path_to_out+out_file, path_to_out+out_file+'.tmp')
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+out_file,'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file)
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	else :
+		try :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx, path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			tmp_adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp')
+			adr_idx_file = open(path_to_out+adr_idx,'w')
+		except Exception, e :
+			print 'Could not open <', path_to_out+adr_idx,'> file. Make sure you started Claws Mail at least once.'
+			sys.exit(1)
+		try :
+			out_file = open(path_to_out+sys.argv[2],'w')
+			convert(in_file, out_file, sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0])
+			l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+			while l :
+				if l.strip() == '</book_list>' :
+					adr_idx_file.write('\t<book name="'+sys.argv[2].split('.xml')[0] +'" file="'+sys.argv[2]+'" />\n')
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				else :
+					adr_idx_file.write(l)
+				l = tmp_adr_idx_file.readline()
+		except Exception, e:
+			got_ex = 1
+			print 'got exception: ', e
+	
+
+	if got_ex :
+		#clean up the mess
+		print 'got exception, cleaning up the mess... changed files will be restored...\n'
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if out_file :
+			out_file.close()
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name)
+		else :
+			os.remove(out_file.name)
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp', path_to_out+adr_idx)
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+				
+	else :
+		#closing all and moving temporary data into place
+		print 'closing open files...\n'
+		in_file.close()
+		out_file.close()	
+		if len(sys.argv) == 3 :
+			os.rename(path_to_out+adr_idx+'.tmp',path_to_out+adr_idx+'.bak' )
+		if len(sys.argv) == 2 :
+			os.rename(out_file.name+'.tmp', out_file.name+'.bak')
+		if adr_idx_file :
+			adr_idx_file.close()
+		if tmp_adr_idx_file :
+			tmp_adr_idx_file.close()
+		print 'done!'
+		
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    execute ()
+

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Lifelong LLSM120G sandwich griller. Overall it heats quickly and works fine, but I have a couple of concerns.

SUPPORT REP (Ray Williams - emp_0528): Thanks for reaching out, Philip. I’m happy to help. Could you describe the issues you’re facing in a bit more detail?

CUSTOMER: Sure. First, the power cord length is very short, so I’m struggling to place it conveniently on my kitchen counter. Second, I notice that the outer body gets quite warm after a few minutes of use, and I’m worried about safety.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Regarding the cord length, this model ships with a compact cord to reduce tangling and storage issues, but I realise that can be inconvenient. A practical workaround is to use a heavy‑duty, grounded extension cord rated for kitchen appliances, placed away from water sources. For the warm outer body: some heating is expected due to the 750W elements, but the unit is designed with heat‑resistant housing.

SUPPORT REP: Could you tell me whether you’re using it continuously for long sessions or mostly for quick sandwiches, and whether it’s placed near a wall or other objects?

CUSTOMER: Mostly quick sandwiches, but it is close to the backsplash on the counter.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks, that helps. I recommend leaving a few inches of clearance around the unit to let heat dissipate, and avoiding covering the vents. Also, always keep the handle and base dry and use heat‑proof gloves if needed. If the housing feels excessively hot (too hot to touch briefly), please stop using the device and share a short video or photos so we can assess a potential defect.

CUSTOMER: Okay, I’ll adjust the placement and try with an extension cord. If it still seems unsafe, I’ll contact you again.

SUPPORT REP: That sounds good. I’ve logged your feedback about cord length and perceived heating so our product team can review it for future revisions. If you experience any burning smell, discoloration, or visible damage, stop using the griller and reach out immediately so we can help with inspection or replacement options.

CUSTOMER: Thanks for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Philip. If you have more questions about safe usage or warranty coverage, I’m here to help.

"CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently bought the Zoul USB C Backup Cable for External Drives that I used with my latest order. The transfer speed is good, but the connector feels a bit loose on one of my external SSDs and sometimes disconnects if the cable is nudged.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal Ranjan): Thanks for reaching out and for purchasing the Zoul USB C Backup Cable. Let me help you troubleshoot this. Could you confirm which brand/model of SSD you’re using and whether the issue occurs on multiple USB-C ports or only a specific one?

CUSTOMER: I’m using a 1TB Samsung T7 and I’ve tested it on two USB-C ports on my laptop. The issue seems slightly better on one port, but I still get random disconnects if the cable moves.

SUPPORT REP (Kunal): Understood. This might be a seating tolerance issue between the connector and that drive’s port. Please try gently reinserting the connector until you hear/feel a firm click and check that there’s no dust or debris in the SSD port. inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I'm having intermittent tracking issues with my Lenovo 130 Wireless Compact Mouse B099SD8PRP. The cursor occasionally lags or jumps, especially when I'm switching quickly between spreadsheets and browser tabs.

Support (Alok Mathur, emp_0883): Thanks for contacting support, Manuel. I understand you’re seeing lag and jumpy cursor behavior with the mouse. Let me ask a couple of quick questions: does this occur only on a particular surface (e.g., glossy desk, glass, or fabric mousepad), and are you using the original Nano USB receiver directly in the laptop/PC, or through a hub or docking station?

Customer: I’m using it on a wooden desk without a mousepad, and the Nano receiver is plugged into a USB hub connected to my laptop.

Support: That’s helpful, thank you. The 1000 DPI optical sensor in this model can become less accurate on certain surfaces and when the wireless signal is slightly degraded. Let’s try three steps: (1) plug the Nano USB receiver directly into the laptop’s USB port instead of the hub; (2) move any nearby wireless devices (Wi‑Fi router, external drives) away from the receiver by at least 20–30 cm; and (3) test the mouse on a non‑reflective mousepad or sheet of paper to see if tracking stabilizes.

Customer: I switched the receiver to the laptop and tried the mouse on a mousepad. The cursor is much smoother now, but I’d still like slightly higher precision when editing images.

Support: Great, that confirms it was a combination of surface and wireless interference. For finer control, you can reduce pointer speed in your OS settings so the 1000 DPI sensor feels more precise. Also make sure no other wireless mouse or keyboard is sharing the same USB hub. If you’d like, I can also share our recommended accessory list for this mouse (mousepads and USB extenders) via email.

Customer: Yes, please send that over. Thanks for the help.

Support: You’re welcome, Manuel. I’ll email the accessory recommendations and a short troubleshooting checklist for future reference. If you run into any more issues with B099SD8PRP, just reply to that email or reopen a support chat.

inputs.text:
Customer: Hi, I bought the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Kettle recently. It heats water fast, but I’ve noticed a slight plastic smell during boiling even after several uses. Is this normal, and how can I get rid of it?

Support (emp_0680): Hello Guillermo, thank you for reaching out and for choosing the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Electric Kettle. A mild odor can sometimes occur with new appliances due to manufacturing residues, but it should reduce over time. Let’s try a deep-clean cycle: fill the kettle to the max line with a 50/50 mix of water and white vinegar, bring it to a boil, then let it sit for 20 minutes before discarding. Rinse and boil plain water 2–3 times afterwards.

Customer: I’ve tried boiling water a few times, but not with vinegar. Is it safe for the stainless steel interior?

Support (emp_0680): Yes, using a diluted white vinegar solution in the proportions mentioned is safe for the stainless steel interior and is a common descaling/odor-removal method. Just avoid abrasive scrubbers on the inner surface. If the smell persists after two cleaning cycles, please let us know so we can review warranty options or arrange an inspection.

Customer: Great, I’ll try that today. If the issue continues, how do I contact you for a possible replacement?

Support (emp_0680): You can reach us through this support channel using your customer ID "peric" or via the purchase invoice you received from Inazuma. Keep the product serial number and your purchase date handy so we can quickly validate the warranty and, if needed, initiate a replacement request.

Employee_id: emp_1098
Please update the existing open issue in the sunlianqiang/kbengine repository titled "Refine PyPIRC old-format test expectations and clarify legacy behavior" (issue reference 76235b1e-3267-42c8-adc4-b9cbcec358b6). The description should state that Rajesh Singh (emp_1098), a Software Engineering Team Lead at Inazuma.co, recommends improving the PyPIRC legacy configuration test by making the expectations more explicit and documenting the differences between the new and old .pypirc formats. This helps future maintainers understand why the old-format behavior is still tested and how it aligns with current distribution tooling practices. Keep the issue status as open and attach the following patch so it is recorded with the issue:

--- kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
+++ kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
@@ -96,7 +96,15 @@
-        # old format
-        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
-        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
-        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
-                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
-        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+        # old format
+        # In the legacy format, only a single section is defined and
+        # PyPIRCCommand is expected to infer the default repository
+        # settings based on that server-login section.
+        #
+        # This ensures that existing projects depending on the old
+        # configuration style continue to work even as newer index
+        # server layouts are introduced.
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
+        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
+                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
+                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
+        self.assertEqual(config, waited)

inputs.title: Refine PyPIRC old-format test expectations and clarify legacy behavior
inputs.description: Rajesh Singh (emp_1098), a Software Engineering Team Lead at Inazuma.co, recommends improving the PyPIRC legacy configuration test by making the expectations more explicit and documenting the differences between the new and old .pypirc formats. This helps future maintainers understand why the old-format behavior is still tested and how it aligns with current distribution tooling practices.
inputs.patch:
--- kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
+++ kbe/src/lib/python/Lib/distutils/tests/test_config.py
@@ -96,7 +96,15 @@
-        # old format
-        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
-        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
-        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
-                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
-        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+        # old format
+        # In the legacy format, only a single section is defined and
+        # PyPIRCCommand is expected to infer the default repository
+        # settings based on that server-login section.
+        #
+        # This ensures that existing projects depending on the old
+        # configuration style continue to work even as newer index
+        # server layouts are introduced.
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
+        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
+                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
+                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
+        self.assertEqual(config, waited)

@@ -1,25 +1,120 @@
-def test_server_registration(self):
-    # This test makes sure PyPIRCCommand knows how to:
-    # 1. handle several sections in .pypirc
-    # 2. handle the old format
+"""Tests for distutils.pypirc.pypirc."""
+import sys
+import os
+import unittest
+import tempfile
 
-    # new format
-    self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC)
-    cmd = self._cmd(self.dist)
-    config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+from distutils.core import PyPIRCCommand
+from distutils.core import Distribution
+from distutils.log import set_threshold
+from distutils.log import WARN
 
-    config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-    waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-              ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
-              ('server', 'server1'), ('username', 'me')]
-    self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+from distutils.tests import support
+from test.support import run_unittest
 
-    # old format
-    self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
-    cmd = self._cmd(self.dist)
-    config = cmd._read_pypirc()
-    config = list(sorted(config.items()))
-    waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
-              ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),

-    self.assertEqual(config, waited)+PYPIRC = """\
+[distutils]
+
+index-servers =
+    server1
+    server2
+
+[server1]
+username:me
+password:secret
+
+[server2]
+username:meagain
+password: secret
+realm:acme
+repository:http://another.pypi/
+"""
+

+[server-login]
+username:tarek
+password:secret
+"""
+
+WANTED = """\
+[distutils]
+index-servers =
+    pypi
+
+[pypi]
+username:tarek
+password:xxx
+"""
+
+
+class PyPIRCCommandTestCase(support.TempdirManager,
+                            support.LoggingSilencer,
+                            support.EnvironGuard,
+                            unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        """Patches the environment."""
+        super(PyPIRCCommandTestCase, self).setUp()
+        self.tmp_dir = self.mkdtemp()
+        os.environ['HOME'] = self.tmp_dir
+        self.rc = os.path.join(self.tmp_dir, '.pypirc')
+        self.dist = Distribution()
+
+        class command(PyPIRCCommand):
+            def __init__(self, dist):
+                PyPIRCCommand.__init__(self, dist)
+            def initialize_options(self):
+                pass
+            finalize_options = initialize_options
+
+        self._cmd = command
+        self.old_threshold = set_threshold(WARN)
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        """Removes the patch."""
+        set_threshold(self.old_threshold)
+        super(PyPIRCCommandTestCase, self).tearDown()
+
+    def test_server_registration(self):
+        # This test makes sure PyPIRCCommand knows how to:
+        # 1. handle several sections in .pypirc
+        # 2. handle the old format
+
+        # new format
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC)
+        cmd = self._cmd(self.dist)
+        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+
+        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
+                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
+                  ('server', 'server1'), ('username', 'me')]
+        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+
+        # old format
+        self.write_file(self.rc, PYPIRC_OLD)
+        config = cmd._read_pypirc()
+        config = list(sorted(config.items()))
+        waited = [('password', 'secret'), ('realm', 'pypi'),
+                  ('repository', 'https://pypi.python.org/pypi'),
+                  ('server', 'server-login'), ('username', 'tarek')]
+        self.assertEqual(config, waited)
+
+    def test_server_empty_registration(self):
+        cmd = self._cmd(self.dist)
+        rc = cmd._get_rc_file()
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(rc))
+        cmd._store_pypirc('tarek', 'xxx')
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(rc))
+        f = open(rc)
+        try:
+            content = f.read()
+            self.assertEqual(content, WANTED)
+        finally:
+            f.close()
+
+def test_suite():
+    return unittest.makeSuite(PyPIRCCommandTestCase)
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    run_unittest(test_suite())

Please update the existing issue in the sunlianqiang/kbengine repository with ID 76235b1e-3267-42c8-adc4-b9cbcec358b6. Attach the updated patch that expands the PyPIRC test module with clearer legacy behavior tests, including the detailed comments explaining how the old single-section .pypirc format is interpreted and ensuring the expected configuration values are asserted.

In the IT support system, assign ticket 90006 to the employee with ID emp_0122 with an assignment date of 2022-10-03, keeping the existing ticket details such as the medium priority and the narrative of Keith Thompson’s account lockout issue and its resolution intact.

Also record a new customer support interaction with chat ID 85220 for product B00S2SEV7K ("Pilot Frixion Clicker Roller Pen (Blue), (9000019529)"). Link it to customer ID "vaffe" and customer name "palle ibsen", and associate it with employee ID emp_1190. Store the full conversation text describing the customer’s concern about inconsistent writing and fading ink, the support representative Lisa Montgomery’s explanation about thermo-sensitive ink and usage conditions, the arrangement of a replacement pack with guidance on best-use scenarios, and the offer to consider a refund or alternative product if the replacement is unsatisfactory. Date this interaction as 2017-09-22.

inputs.product_name: Pilot Frixion Clicker Roller Pen (Blue), (9000019529)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm reaching out because the Pilot Frixion Clicker Roller Pen I purchased is not writing consistently and the ink fades quickly on some of my office documents.

SUPPORT REP (Lisa Montgomery, IT Team Lead): Thank you for contacting support. I understand how important reliable pens are for your daily work. Could you please confirm your order reference and whether you're using the pen on standard office paper or any coated/laminated surfaces?

CUSTOMER: The order is linked to customer ID 'vaffe', and I'm mostly using it on standard A4 copier paper.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for confirming. The Frixion pens use thermo-sensitive ink, which can appear lighter or fade if exposed to heat or if the paper is stored near warm equipment. I recommend avoiding prolonged exposure to high temperatures (for example, near printers or sunlight). For critical legal or archival documents, we suggest using a non-erasable pen as stated in the product description.

CUSTOMER: That makes sense. Is there anything you can do about this particular batch of pens?

SUPPORT REP: I can arrange a replacement pack from a newer batch and include guidance on best-use scenarios. You will receive an email with shipment details shortly. If the replacement still does not meet your expectations, we can explore a refund or an alternative product.

CUSTOMER: Thank you, that would be helpful.

SUPPORT REP: You're welcome. We appreciate your feedback and will share it with our product team to improve future batches.

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm facing issues with my Electvision remote that I use with the Amazon Fire TV Stick. It intermittently stops responding and sometimes delays actions.

SUPPORT REP: Hello Paolo, thanks for reaching out. I understand how frustrating remote issues can be, especially while streaming. I see this chat is linked to your existing IT ticket 13121 that was raised due to connectivity problems. To start, can you confirm whether the remote issues occur only when the Fire TV is connected to your home Wi‑Fi network, or do they also occur when you use an alternate connection such as the VPN workaround suggested in your IT ticket resolution?

CUSTOMER: The remote lag and unresponsiveness seem worse when the network connectivity is unstable. When I switch to the VPN as suggested by IT, it improves slightly but the problem still occurs.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful information. Since we already know there was a temporary network outage affecting the Inazuma.co portal, it’s possible that intermittent connectivity could also impact how quickly the Fire TV interface processes remote commands. Let’s try a few steps: (1) Restart your Fire TV Stick and router, (2) Re‑pair the Electvision remote following the pairing manual printed on the back of the remote, and (3) Test again on both your normal Wi‑Fi and VPN. Please let me know if the responsiveness improves after these steps.

CUSTOMER: I followed the steps and re‑paired the remote. The performance is slightly better on VPN, but I still see occasional delays.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. In that case, I recommend we log this as a product support case linked to your existing ticket so our hardware support team can review whether the Electvision remote or the Fire TV configuration needs adjustment or replacement. You may receive a follow‑up email with troubleshooting instructions or an RMA if a defect is confirmed. Meanwhile, you can reduce background apps on the Fire TV and keep the remote in direct line‑of‑sight to the device to minimize latency.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. Please proceed with the follow‑up.

SUPPORT REP: Certainly, Paolo. I’ve documented this interaction and tied it to your IT ticket 13121. Our support team will follow up with next steps. Thank you for your patience.

instruction:
Please create a new customer support chat record with ID 861 for customer Christina Berglund (customer ID bergs) regarding her Redmi 10A (Slate Grey, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage; product ID B09XB7SRQ5). The chat should be logged under support employee emp_0812 and should record the interaction that took place on 2018-11-12 with the following transcript as the chat text:

"CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Redmi 10A and I’m facing frequent app freezes and occasional reboots, especially when using the camera and switching between apps quickly. Can you help?

SUPPORT REP (Jonathan Sinclair, Business Development): Thanks for reaching out, Christina. I’m sorry to hear about the issues you’re experiencing with your Redmi 10A. To assist you better, could you confirm whether all system and app updates have been installed, and whether you’ve recently added any new apps just before the freezes began?

CUSTOMER: Yes, the phone says it’s up to date. I did install a couple of games last week, but the freezing happens even when I’m just using the camera or WhatsApp.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Let’s try a couple of troubleshooting steps. First, please clear the cache for the camera and messaging apps from Settings > Apps. Next, try restarting the device in safe mode to see if the issue persists without third‑party apps running. If the phone is still freezing in safe mode, it may indicate a deeper system or hardware issue.

CUSTOMER: I tried safe mode and it still froze once when I opened the camera.

SUPPORT REP: Thanks for checking that. Since the problem persists in safe mode, I’d like to register this as a service case and arrange a diagnostic at our authorized service center. The technicians can run hardware checks on the memory and storage and, if needed, re‑flash the software. If a defect is confirmed, you’ll be eligible for a repair or replacement as per warranty terms.

CUSTOMER: That works for me. Please proceed.

SUPPORT REP: I’ve created a service request tied to your customer profile and purchase record. You’ll receive an email shortly with the case number, service center details near your location, and instructions on backing up your data before handing over the device. If you notice any new symptoms or error messages, please include them when you visit the center so we have a complete picture.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the clear explanation and next steps.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Christina. We appreciate your patience and will do our best to resolve this quickly. If you have any questions or need to reschedule your appointment, feel free to reply to the email or contact our support line."

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I bought the iQOO Z6 Lite 5G recently and I’m unsure about the best way to optimize battery life while using 5G and high refresh rate.

SUPPORT REP (Riya Sharma - emp_1379): Hello matti, thanks for reaching out. Since you’re using 5G and a 120Hz refresh rate, both can impact battery life. I’d recommend enabling the phone’s adaptive refresh rate so it only uses 120Hz when needed, and turning off 5G when you’re on Wi‑Fi or don’t need high-speed data.

SUPPORT REP: You can also lower screen brightness, disable background app refresh for non-essential apps, and use the built-in battery optimization mode. These steps together usually provide a noticeable improvement.

CUSTOMER: That sounds helpful. Is there any risk in frequently switching between 5G and 4G?

SUPPORT REP: No functional risk to the device; it’s designed to handle that seamlessly. The main trade-off is convenience vs. battery usage. If you prioritize battery life, keeping 5G off when not needed is a good practice.

CUSTOMER: Understood, I’ll follow these steps. Thank you for the clear explanation.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, matti. If you experience any unusual battery drain even after these changes, feel free to contact us again and we can walk through more advanced diagnostics.

SUPPORT REP: That’s completely fair. I’ve noted your preference for a replacement if reconnection steps don’t resolve the issue. You’ll receive a follow-up email with instructions and a reference number for this case. Thank you for your patience and for choosing this smartwatch.

Customer Support Chat Transcript

CUSTOMER: Hi, I'm having trouble with the RC PRINT GI 790 ink refill I bought for my Canon PIXMA G2010. After refilling, the prints are coming out streaky and some colors seem faded. I followed the basic instructions, but I'm not sure if I missed a step.

inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Compact Stainless Steel Travel Kettle (0.8L) using my account, and I have a concern about the auto shut-off feature. It sometimes seems to turn off before the water reaches a full boil.

I understand how important a reliable auto shut-off is, especially when you’re on the move. Could you please confirm if this early shut-off happens every time or only occasionally, and whether you’re using the kettle with a standard wall socket or a travel adapter?

CUSTOMER: It happens occasionally, mostly when I’m using a travel adapter in hotels. At home with a regular wall socket, it seems to work fine.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful information, thank you. Since the kettle is dual voltage, variations in power from certain travel adapters can trigger the safety shut-off sooner than expected. I recommend checking that your adapter supports the correct voltage range and isn’t limiting current. Also, please ensure the kettle base and cord are firmly connected and the water level is between the minimum and maximum markers.

CUSTOMER: I’ll double-check the adapter specs and water levels. If it still keeps shutting off early, what should I do next?

SUPPORT REP: If the issue persists after verifying the adapter and usage, we can treat this as a potential hardware or compatibility issue. In that case, please share your order ID and a short photo or video of the behavior. Our support team will review it and, if needed, help you with a replacement or repair under the applicable warranty terms. We’ll aim to make this process as smooth as possible.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. I’ll collect the details and get back to you.

SUPPORT REP: Perfect, thank you. We appreciate your patience and want to ensure you can use the kettle confidently during your travels. Feel free to reach out with any other questions in the meantime.

inputs.title: Clarify behavior of `configure` endpoint for requests with query parameters
inputs.description: The `configure` endpoint in the `827992983/yue` repository was recently modified to remove the trailing `$` in its URL pattern to allow query parameters. While this fixes routing for URLs containing query strings, we should document and review the expected behavior for various request patterns (e.g., `/configure`, `/configure/`, `/configure?step=1`) to avoid regressions. This issue tracks adding explicit tests and documentation for the `configure` URL behavior, ensuring that query-parameter-based configuration flows remain stable and intuitive for administrators.

--- yue/urls.py
+++ yue/urls.py
@@ -4,6 +4,18 @@
 urlpatterns = [

     url(r'^logout', login_views.logout, name='logout'),
@@ -11,7 +23,16 @@
-    url(r'^configure', admin_views.configure, name='configure'),
+    # NOTE: The `configure` endpoint intentionally omits a trailing `$`
+    # so that URLs with query parameters (e.g. `/configure?step=1`) are
+    # correctly routed. To prevent unexpected matches, we document this
+    # behavior and add tests in `tests/test_urls_configure.py`.

+    #   matching allowed suffixes while still supporting `?` query parameters.

SUPPORT REP: Perfect, I’ve initiated a replacement for the same model, tied to your customer ID vinet. You’ll receive a confirmation email shortly and the new unit should arrive within 3–5 business days. If the issue persists with the replacement, we can discuss switching to a different model. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

CUSTOMER: That’s all, thank you for the quick help.

SUPPORT REP: You’re welcome, Paul. Enjoy your coffee once the new filter arrives, and feel free to contact us again if you need anything.

observed_output.text:
---

```
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Milk Frother, Immersion Blender Cordless Foam Maker, but I'm a bit disappointed with a few aspects. I received a different variant than what's shown in the images, and the build quality isn't as expected. Also, there's no battery charging indicator to show how much battery is remaining.

SUPPORT REP: Hello! Thank you for reaching out to us about your concerns with the Milk Frother. Sorry to hear that the variant you received doesn't match the product images and that the build quality isn't meeting your expectations. Additionally, I understand the frustration with the lack of a battery charging indicator. Can you please provide me with your order number so I can look into this further for you?

CUSTOMER: My order number is #MF12345. Also, I noticed the speed adjustment buttons could be improved. It starts directly at full speed, and you can only reduce it. It would be more intuitive if it increased in speed as you press the button.

SUPPORT REP: Thank you for providing the order number, #MF12345. I've located your order and I'm going to go ahead and document the discrepancies you've mentioned, including the product variant and build quality concerns. Regarding the speed adjustment buttons, I completely understand your point. This is valuable feedback that I'll pass on to our product development team. As a temporary workaround, you might find it helpful to start with the lowest speed and then increase as needed, though I acknowledge this isn't the ideal solution you're looking for.

CUSTOMER: That sounds good. What about the battery charging indicator? Is there a way to know how much charge is left without having to guess?

SUPPORT REP: I've checked on this for you, and currently, the model you have doesn't have a visual battery level indicator. However, based on customer feedback, we're working on integrating this feature into future updates. In the meantime, a general guideline is that a full charge can provide up to 12 frothing sessions, as mentioned in some of our customer reviews. If you're finding that your usage exceeds this and you're unsure about the charge level, you can always charge it for about 30 minutes to an hour to ensure it's topped up. Would you like me to provide a prepaid return label for the product variant issue, or would you prefer a discount on your next purchase as a gesture of goodwill?

CUSTOMER: I think a prepaid return label would be great, thank you. But before I return it, can I confirm if the new variant will have the improvements we discussed, especially the battery indicator?

SUPPORT REP: Excellent choice! I'll go ahead and process the prepaid return label for you, which you'll receive via email shortly. Regarding your question, while we can't guarantee immediate implementation of all suggested improvements in the next variant, I can assure you that your feedback, along with others, is being considered for future product enhancements. The battery charging indicator, in particular, is a feature we're actively exploring for inclusion in upcoming models. If you'd like, I can also offer you a 10% discount on your next purchase, which would include any new and improved versions of the Milk Frother that might be released in the future.

CUSTOMER: That sounds like a plan. Thank you for your help and for listening to my concerns. I look forward to the return label and the discount for my next purchase.

SUPPORT REP: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to assist you. Your satisfaction is our top priority, and I'm glad we could find a solution that works for you. The return label and discount code (MF10DISCOUNT) will be in your email inbox shortly. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out. Have a wonderful day, and thank you for choosing our products!

CUSTOMER: Thank you again, and I wish you a great day too!

SUPPORT REP: Likewise! Take care!
```

observed_output.text:
PARTH SHARMA: Hi Steven, I want to thank you for taking the time to discuss the upcoming product launch at Inazuma.co. Could you provide your insights on the timeline for the new features we're developing?

STEVEN PARKER: Of course, Parth. I'm happy to assist. Which part of the timeline would you like me to address?

PARTH SHARMA: Let's begin with the development phase. How do you think the collaboration between our engineering and IT teams will affect the timelines?

STEVEN PARKER: The collaboration should enhance efficiency in our processes. The initial phase is critical for establishing systems correctly, ensuring we're ready to handle any potential technical challenges.

PARTH SHARMA: That makes sense. We've structured the teams to enhance communication and problem-solving, utilizing our technical expertise in system design and architecture.

STEVEN PARKER: Exactly, with an optimal setup, we can maximize resources and ensure seamless integration across departments. Now, regarding cybersecurity measures, how are we addressing data privacy concerns during this launch?

PARTH SHARMA: We've put in place strong security protocols and are working closely with IT to ensure compliance with industry standards. Our approach includes continuous monitoring and proactive risk management.

STEVEN PARKER: That's reassuring. It's crucial for maintaining consumer trust. As for project management, how are we organizing tasks and milestones?

PARTH SHARMA: We've developed a detailed project plan outlining each phase and its milestones. Incorporating agile methodologies allows us to adapt swiftly to any changes or challenges.

STEVEN PARKER: Excellent strategy. It appears we're on track for a successful launch. If you need further assistance or have questions, please feel free to reach out.

inputs.product_name: Acer 139 cm (55 inches) I Series 4K Ultra HD Android Smart LED TV AR55AR2851UDFL (Black)
inputs.text:
CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased the Acer 139 cm (55 inches) I Series 4K Ultra HD Android Smart LED TV, and overall the picture quality is great. However, I’m noticing that when I connect my Bestor 8K HDMI 2.1 cable to my laptop, the TV sometimes flickers and briefly loses signal.

SUPPORT REP (Mukesh Kapoor, HR Associate assisting via routed support line): Thank you for reaching out and for choosing our Acer I Series TV. I’m sorry about the flickering issue you’re experiencing when using the Bestor 8K HDMI cable. Let’s run through a few checks to narrow this down.

SUPPORT REP: First, can you confirm the HDMI port you’re using on the TV (e.g., HDMI 1 or HDMI 2) and whether the flicker happens on all apps or only when using the laptop input?

CUSTOMER: I’m using HDMI 1, and the flicker only happens when I use my laptop as the source. OTT apps running directly on the TV work fine.

SUPPORT REP: That’s helpful. Please try the following:
1) Switch the cable to HDMI 2 on the TV and check if the flicker persists.
2) On your laptop, ensure the output resolution is set to 4K at 60Hz instead of trying to push 8K, as the TV panel is 4K.
3) If possible, test with a different HDMI cable to rule out a cable defect.

CUSTOMER: I changed to HDMI 2 and set my laptop to 4K 60Hz. The flicker is reduced but still happens occasionally.

SUPPORT REP: Understood. Next steps:
- On the TV, go to Settings > Picture > Advanced and disable any HDMI-CEC or input auto-switching features.
- Ensure the TV’s software is updated to the latest version under Settings > About > System Update.
If the issue continues after these changes, we can arrange a technician visit to check the HDMI ports and internal board.

CUSTOMER: I’ve updated the TV and disabled HDMI-CEC. The connection now seems stable.

SUPPORT REP: That’s great to hear. I’ll document this interaction under your customer profile and note that the issue was resolved through configuration changes. If the flicker returns or you notice any new symptoms, please contact us and we’ll escalate to a field technician.

CUSTOMER: Thank you for the detailed guidance.

SUPPORT REP: You’re most welcome. Enjoy your Acer I Series TV, and feel free to reach out if you need anything else.

Customer: Hi, I bought the Pigeon Quartz 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Kettle recently. It heats water fast, but I’ve noticed a slight plastic smell during boiling even after several uses. Is this normal, and how can I get rid of it?

Let’s try a deep-clean cycle: fill the kettle to the max line with a 50/50 mix of water and white vinegar, bring it to a boil, then let it sit for 20 minutes before discarding. Support (emp_0680): Yes, using a diluted white vinegar solution in the proportions mentioned is safe for the stainless steel interior and is a common descaling/odor-removal method. Just avoid abrasive scrubbers on the inner surface. If the smell persists after two cleaning cycles, please let us know so we can review warranty options or arrange an inspection.

Customer: Great, I’ll try that today. If the issue continues, how do I contact you for a possible replacement?

Support (emp_0680): You can reach us through this support channel using your customer ID "peric" or via the purchase invoice you received from Inazuma. Keep the product serial number and your purchase date handy so we can quickly validate the warranty and, if needed, initiate a replacement request.

observed_output.review_content: I would not consider buying an i-phone simply because my friend owns two of them – or blindly go for a new Android model suggested by my son or nephew (both of whom are more tech savvy than me) because their recommendations are obviously based on their own needs and expectations, which may differ from mine. I am an old-fashioned mechanical engineer with a basic understanding of parameters like millimetres, megapixels and megabytes – but I think of a cellphone as a utility item, not a status symbol. Applying a technocratic approach, I would not choose a costlier option unless I get additional features which suit my requirements.My foremost requirement – which is entirely non-negotiable – is that my handset must have provision for two SIM cards, since I do not want to carry two separate handsets for my CUG and personal numbers. My other requirements are not difficult to fulfil: a phonebook with at least 2000 contacts, basic net connectivity, a basic camera for photos and videos and scope for downloading a few apps such as the ubiquitous WhatsApp and my favourite word games (which do not need much memory or processing capacity). I would certainly appreciate practical features like high reliability, software and security updates and high battery capacity (sufficient for 24 hours or preferably 48 hours at my normal level of usage). Besides, I would like to use a new handset for at least two years.Apart from exigencies, I do not intend to use my cellphone for surfing the Internet, videoconferencing or sending e-mails as I prefer using a desktop or laptop for such activities.I am equally clear about what I do not need. Please look up the product with ID B08PFSZ7FH to confirm its current details, and then record a customer support chat for that same product. "CUSTOMER: Hi, I recently purchased an HDMI extender cable for my Fire Stick (product ID B08PFSZ7FH). It works fine most of the time, but occasionally the video signal drops for a few seconds and then comes back. Is this normal, or could it be a defect?

SUPPORT REP (Mithilesh Patel): Thanks for reaching out, Sven. Intermittent signal drops are not expected behavior, so let's run a few quick checks.
